MK1017KMWhat this pack is

This is a research pack for one application: the LSEG Business Management Summer Internship 2027, requisition R0123386, based at 5 Canada Square in London [S1]. It covers the role, the team, the firm, its rivals, the industry, the rules that shape it, the news, the recruitment process, and how to hold your ground in a scenario question. Everything comes from public sources read on or before 5 October 2026. Every non-obvious fact carries a marker such as [S72], which you can look up in the source table in Part 15.

The pack separates three kinds of claim. You should keep them separate when you speak, too.

Confirmed
A primary source (LSEG's own reports, a regulator) or two credible outlets. Say it as fact.
Reported
One credible source, such as trade press. Say "it was reported that".
Inferred
The author's reasoning from the evidence. Say "my reading is", and be ready to be told you are wrong.
Inputs that were not supplied

The brief left the candidate fields blank: no degree, year, CV, prior knowledge score, interview date or interviewer names. The pack therefore assumes a penultimate-year undergraduate with little finance background (about 3 out of 10). It treats the next step as the application (closing 30 October 2026, reviewed on a rolling basis [S1]), and it builds the CV grill in Part 11 as a method with placeholder examples. Once you have an interview date or a name, add them and re-read Parts 9 to 11.

MK1019KMThe 10-minute emergency version

If you read nothing else, read this page and the cheat sheet in Part 13.

1. What the job is, in two sentences

You spend nine weeks in one team inside LSEG's Markets division: an FX customer team, a primary markets research team, a business intelligence and strategy team, or a risk team [S1]. LSEG uses the same four bullets in several postings, so treat them as a menu. Your strengths and interests decide where you land [S1, S5] Confirmed

2. Ten facts to have ready

FactNumberSource
LSEG total income, FY2025 (excluding pass-through recoveries)£8,986m, up 7.1% organic[S72]
H1 2026 total income£4,799m, up 8.4% organic; 2026 guidance raised to 7.0 to 7.5%[S70]
Markets division, H1 2026£1,920m, up 11.9%: the fastest-growing division, about 40% of group revenue[S24, S71]
Recurring share of revenue, 202573%[S74]
SwapClear notional cleared, 2025$1,941 trillion, a record[S72]
LSEG FX average daily volume, H1 2026$561bn a day[S70]
FXall clients2,400+ institutions, 200+ liquidity providers[S340]
Ownership of the piecesLCH about 94% (above 95% after the July 2026 deal); Tradeweb 50.9%; Turquoise 84.2%[S23, S70, S74, S300]
People28,516 at end 2025 (the job ad's "25,000" is out of date)[S74]
Global FX market$9.6 trillion a day; UK share 37.8%, the largest centre[S162, S163]

3. Why LSEG, in 30 seconds

Say this in the interview

"What draws me to LSEG is how it is built. It owns venues like the London Stock Exchange, Tradeweb and FXall. But its clearing house, LCH, has open access written into its rules: it must clear on fair terms even for trades from rival venues, and banks still sit on its risk committee. That is why the market trusts it with over 90% of cleared interest rate swaps. Business management works where those businesses join, and that is where I want to learn." [S303, S305]

4. The one regulatory point per placement

  • FX customers: the FX Global Code, updated December 2024, sets the conduct standard. Never share one client's flow with another [S343].
  • Debt listings research: the new prospectus regime (POATRs) has been in force since 19 January 2026. Issuer pipelines are confidential and can be inside information under UK MAR [S151, S348].
  • BI and strategy: T+1 settlement in the UK and EU from 11 October 2027 changes post-trade workloads. LSE 24 launches in H1 2027 [S158, S24].
  • Risk: LCH sets initial margin at 99.7% confidence. Every member default it has handled stayed within the defaulter's margin [S93, S351, S354].

5. The priority order when good things collide

Rules and market integrity first, then fair treatment of every customer, then the process and the record, then speed. The sentence that holds every frame: "I'd want to get this right for the client without cutting a corner the firm would have to explain later." Part 11 explains why this order fits LSEG in particular.

6. The honest weak spots, so nothing surprises you

The share price fell about 41% from February 2025 to February 2026. Much of that came on fears that AI tools would erode LSEG's data business, and the activist fund Elliott built a stake [S90, S88]. London's listings market is still small next to New York's [S192]. Open access let Euronext move its clearing away [S301]. You can be clear-eyed about all three and still want to join. Part 8 shows how.

7. One question to ask

Say this in the interview

"LSEG says much of FXall's functionality now sits inside Workspace, with Tradeweb next. From the Markets side, how do you measure whether clients have actually moved their workflow?" [S301, S302]

What the posting really says, what a day in each of the four seats looks like, who sits around you in the Markets division, and the lines you must never cross.

This part does three jobs. First, it reads the job description (JD) line by line and translates each sentence into concrete work at a named LSEG unit. Key term

Markets division: one of LSEG's four reporting segments since 1 January 2025, formed by merging the old Capital Markets and Post Trade segments. The other three are Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell and Risk Intelligence [S22, S23]. Inside Markets, LSEG runs separate cash-generating units (CGUs), the smallest groups of assets that earn money on their own: Digital & Securities Markets, FX, Tradeweb, LCH Ltd, LCH SA, Post Trade Solutions and Regulatory Reporting [S22]. That list is the best public map of how Markets is run.

The insight that changes how you prepare

The four "exposure" bullets in the JD are not a description of one London team. The New York Business Management internship (R0123464) uses the same four bullets word for word, the same five businesses and the same "dynamic nature of the division" line [S9]. The London graduate programme R0123406 reuses them as "exposure/rotations" [S6]. Confirmed The bullets describe a pool of Markets placements. The JD then says how you land in one: "To allow us to place you in the right area, during the recruitment process we will get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business" [S1, S2].

So the recruitment process is also a matching process. Two things follow. First, you need a credible answer for all four seats, because you do not know which one you will get. Second, you can shape the match: an assessor who hears a specific, evidenced reason for preferring one seat has something to work with. Inferred

Say this in the interview

"I understand the internship sits in the Markets division, which brought Capital Markets and Post Trade together from January 2025, and that interns are matched to a team during recruitment. I'd be happy in any of the four areas. If I had to choose, I'd lean towards [seat], because [one specific reason tied to a fact in this pack]."

Figure 2 shows what every one of the four seats has in common: work arrives as a request from someone inside LSEG (or from a client through an account manager), it gets triaged, analysed and turned into a product, and the product is judged by an outcome. Figure 3 then shows how the four seats differ: which channel the work runs through, and who sits on the other side.

MK1021KMThe JD decoded, line by line

Each block below quotes one sentence or bullet of the JD exactly (long dashes in LSEG's text are shown as " - " to keep this pack's house style), then decodes it. For the four exposure bullets the decode is a full table: the LSEG unit, counterparties, what good looks like, tools and the structural fact the line reveals. Boilerplate lines get a shorter treatment, but none is skipped.

Opening paragraph

"Please review all the graduate programme opportunities and make one application."
Means LSEG runs one early-careers pool. Several programmes are open at once in London: Business Management (Markets), Business Analyst (Markets), Engineering, and graduate schemes for FTSE Russell and Data & Analytics [S3, S4]. Structural fact Only your first application is reviewed if you send more than one [S1]. In the UK, business internships exist only in Markets; FTSE Russell and D&A have graduate schemes but no UK business internship open [S4, S37]. Confirmed Use it Choosing this programme is itself a statement that you want Markets. Have a reason.
"Our Summer Business Management Internship Programme has been crafted to simulate our Business Graduate Programme so that you can understand what a career with LSEG would really be like."
Means The internship is a nine-week trial of the 12-month Business Graduate Programme, and the main feeder into it [S2, S37, S38]. Confirmed Unit Early Careers sits in the People function; most graduate requisitions are tagged "Division: People" in Workday [S4]. What good looks like Behaving like a first-year graduate: owning a deliverable, managing your own stakeholders. Structural fact Because the programme is a feeder, interviewers are asking "would I hire this person as a graduate in September 2028?", not "can they survive nine weeks?" Inferred
"LSEG is at the forefront of trading services - a fundamental part of the financial and transactional services that support and enhance the development of businesses and economies across the world."
Means "Trading services" is the Markets division. It is now LSEG's largest division by EBITDA: £1,929m in 2025 against £1,617m for Data & Analytics [S22]. Total income was £3,467m in 2025 (+8.9% organic) and £1,920m in H1 2026 (+11.9%), at a 58.6% EBITDA margin [S22, S24]. The CEO told investors in July 2026: "Remember that Markets is 40% of LSEG revenue" [S71]. Confirmed Structural fact The public debate about LSEG is about data and AI; the seat you are applying for is in the part of the group with the fastest growth. Use it One number, used once, beats five numbers recited.
Key term

EBITDA and margin: EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, a rough measure of operating profit. The margin is EBITDA divided by income. A 58.6% margin means about 59p of every £1 of Markets income is left after operating costs.

"As an intern, you will join one of our flagship trading services - London Stock Exchange, LSEG FX, Tradeweb, Turquoise - or LCH our global leading multi-asset clearing houses."
Means Five brands, which map onto the CGUs above. The Annual Report lists the venues: "the London Stock Exchange, AIM, Turquoise, FXall, FX Matching and Tradeweb", combined with "multi-asset class clearing infrastructure" [S23]. Confirmed Unit and ownership London Stock Exchange plc is a Recognised Investment Exchange (RIE), 100% owned. Turquoise is an equity MTF, 84.2% owned. LSEG FX runs FXall and FX Matching, 100% owned. Tradeweb is separately listed and majority-owned (about 50.9% economic interest). LCH Group, parent of LCH Ltd (UK) and LCH SA (France), is about 94% owned (94.4% per the Annual Report, 94.2% per the 2024 results), rising above 95% after a €70m minority buy-in agreed in July 2026 [S300, S121, S221]. Ownership of the others: [S300, S303]. Confirmed Structural fact These are separate regulated legal entities with their own boards. That shapes everything you do: data, people and decisions do not move freely between them [S300, S304]. Trap Do not call LCH "the LSEG clearing division". Name LCH Ltd and LCH SA as separate companies in different countries [S22, S28].
Key term

RIE (Recognised Investment Exchange): a UK exchange recognised by the FCA under the Financial Services and Markets Act. It must run fair and orderly markets and police its own rules. London Stock Exchange plc operates its markets "in its capacity as a Recognised Investment Exchange" [S13, S95].

Key term

MTF (multilateral trading facility): a regulated trading venue run by an investment firm rather than an exchange. It brings many buyers and sellers together under non-discretionary rules. Turquoise is an MTF; so are LSEG FX's venues, authorised by the FCA in the UK and the Central Bank of Ireland in the EU [S95, S341].

"We help customers across the trade life cycle, ensuring compliance and efficiency in clearing and reporting obligations, while granting access to diverse liquidity pools across various asset classes, fostering growth for customers, communities, and economies worldwide."
Means This is almost word for word the Annual Report's Markets introduction ("We help customers across the trade lifecycle optimise their financial resource consumption and risk, manage their regulatory reporting obligations ... We provide access to diverse liquidity pools") [S23]. Confirmed The JD was written from the divisional strategy text. Unit by stage Raise capital: LSE plc primary markets. Trade: LSE, Turquoise, FXall, FX Matching, Tradeweb. Clear: LCH Ltd and LCH SA. After the trade: Post Trade Solutions (compression and optimisation) and Regulatory Reporting [S22, S300]. Structural fact "Clearing and reporting obligations" are legal duties on LSEG's customers. LSEG sells compliance as a product. Use it If you can walk an interviewer through the trade life cycle and name the LSEG unit at each stage, you have shown you understand "how it fits together", which the JD asks for later.
Key term

Trade life cycle: the stages a trade goes through. Pre-trade (raising capital, getting prices), execution (agreeing the trade on a venue), clearing (a central counterparty steps in between buyer and seller), settlement (cash and asset actually swap) and post-trade (reporting, compression, record-keeping). Liquidity pool: a place where buyers and sellers meet, so you can trade size without moving the price much.

"The dynamic nature of the division means grads will join a fast-paced environment where instant reaction and long-term vision are equally important."
Means The same sentence appears in the FTSE Russell graduate JD, so it is programme-wide wording, not a team signal [S8]. Confirmed What it points at "Instant reaction": an FX client ticket, a margin number that moved overnight, a platform incident. "Long-term vision": LSE 24, the 24-hour-a-day, five-day venue launching in H1 2027, or the move of FXall into Workspace [S24, S302]. Use it Prepare one story where you reacted fast and one where you planned over months. The strengths interview tests both.

The four exposure bullets

The JD introduces these with "As an intern you can expect exposure across:". The word "Or" at the start of three bullets is the tell: each is a separate placement, not a rotation through all four [S1]. Inferred

Bullet 1: "Solve problems for our FX customers! We understand their business goals, maintain relationships with existing customers, keep them informed and deal with post sale activity."
Account management and customer success inside LSEG FX. The "and Sales" in the URL slug fits this seat [S2].
LSEG unitLSEG FX (the FX CGU). Platforms: FXall (dealer-to-client) and FX Matching (dealer-to-dealer), plus a US Streaming FX Spot business and links to LCH ForexClear [S22, S24, S45]. Likely team: FX Sales and Account Management or Customer Success [S17]. Inferred
Day to dayWork the client queue: a user cannot see a bank's prices, a new trading entity needs setting up, allocations fail, confirmations do not reach the client's order system. Prepare client "business reviews": volume by currency pair, number of liquidity providers used, adoption of newer features such as Forward First Fixing (over $330bn traded in Q2 2026) [S17, S302]. Send release notes and outage notices ("keep them informed") [S11]. Post-sale: onboarding, connectivity, entitlements, renewals. Inferred
CounterpartiesBanks acting as liquidity providers; asset managers; hedge funds; corporate treasurers; on FX Matching, interbank dealers. Contacts sit in "trading, treasury, eFX, sales, operations, and technology functions" [S17]. FXall has 2,400+ institutional clients and 200+ liquidity providers across 500+ currency pairs [S340].
Good looks likeRetention and renewals, revenue growth on assigned accounts, fast issue resolution, adoption of new functionality: "Achieve individual revenue, growth, retention and targets across assigned accounts" [S17]. For an intern: a review pack the account manager actually takes into the meeting, or a recurring problem fixed for good. Inferred
ToolsLSEG Workspace (much of FXall's functionality now sits inside it), FXall Admin (the "reference data and permissioning tool"), Excel, a CRM, and Power BI or Tableau for usage MI [S302, S317, S21, S5]. Which exact tools this team uses is Inferred.
Structural factFX is over-the-counter: there is no single exchange. LSEG earns venue, transaction and workflow fees, roughly 75% transactional and 25% recurring [S303]. Volume rises with volatility: "greater volumes driven by higher volatility in the market" [S23]. So the account manager's real job is to embed LSEG in client workflow so volume stays when volatility falls. Inferred FX revenue was £272m in 2025 (+7.5%) and £145m in H1 2026 (+7.6%); average daily volume $561bn in H1 2026 [S22, S24].
Control angleClient information is confidential under the FX Global Code (Principles 19 and 20) [S343]. LSEG is hiring an FX Market Surveillance Product Director to detect "potential market abuse, misconduct, and anomalies" on its FX platforms [S14].
Key term

FXall: LSEG's dealer-to-client FX platform. A buy-side firm or corporate asks several banks for prices at once (RFQ, request for quote), sees streamed prices, or uses an anonymous order book and algorithms (TWAP, Iceberg) [S342]. It also handles post-trade steps: confirmations, settlement instructions, reporting [S340].

Key term

FX Matching: LSEG's dealer-to-dealer venue, an anonymous central limit order book where banks trade with each other [S22, S303]. Liquidity provider (LP): a bank or trading firm that quotes prices others can trade on.

Key term

ADV (average daily volume): total value traded divided by trading days. LSEG's main FX volume KPI: $525bn in 2025, $561bn in H1 2026 [S301, S302]. STP (straight-through processing): a trade flows from execution to the client's booking and settlement systems with no manual re-keying. FXall offers STP via "Trade Notification" [S340].

Key term

TCA (transaction cost analysis): measuring how much a trade really cost against a benchmark, to prove best execution. FXall's version is Trade Performance Reporting, to "evaluate the cost and effectiveness of your execution strategies" [S340]. Post-sale activity: everything after the contract is signed: onboarding, permissions, connectivity, renewals, billing queries.

Bullet 2: "Or research analysis into global markets which could have a focus on debt listings, valuations, and shareholder and geographic analysis."
Market research and intelligence for London Stock Exchange plc's primary markets, most likely in Fixed Income (debt) or Equity Primary Markets.
LSEG unitLondon Stock Exchange plc, inside the Digital & Securities Markets CGU. Fixed Income Primary Markets runs debt listings on the Main Market, the International Securities Market (ISM) and the Sustainable Bond Market; Equity Primary Markets handles IPOs, secondary listings and the Private Securities Market [S15, S16]. A DCM job ad confirms a "market research and intelligence" team inside capital markets [S15]. Reported That this is the intern's home is Inferred.
Day to dayDebt listings: tables of bond admissions by issuer type (sovereigns and agencies, banks, corporates, emerging-market issuers), currency, use of proceeds (green, social, sukuk) and region; target lists of issuers who borrow in Europe but have never listed in London. Valuations: how a sector trades in London against New York. Shareholder analysis: who owns London-listed peers and how much of it is international. Geographic analysis: sizing the Americas, Gulf or India pipeline [S15, S16]. Inferred
CounterpartiesMostly internal: origination managers who pitch to "treasurers, heads of funding, origination and syndication professionals, capital markets lawyers and investors" [S15]. The team works with "FIG, SSA, EM issuers, bankers, law firms and advisors" [S15].
Good looks likeAccurate, sourced data with a clear "so what" for the origination banker. The business is judged on admissions, capital raised and listing revenue; Equities revenue was £412m in 2025 [S22]. Inferred for the KPI list.
ToolsLSEG Workspace and LSEG's own data, Excel, PowerPoint; possibly Python or SQL, which the sibling Business Analyst internship names alongside Tableau and Power BI [S5]. Inferred
Structural factLondon's debt market is an international venue. LSEG says Fixed Income Primary Markets serves "1,300 global borrowers in over 60 countries that raise $500-600 billion annually" and calls ISM and the Sustainable Bond Market "key engines of growth" [S15]. Reported (a job ad, not audited). Equity listings are a competitive fight with New York; LSEG is widening the offer with the Private Securities Market, Digital Markets Infrastructure and LSE 24 [S23, S24].
Control angleThis is the seat where inside information lives. The team can see planned IPOs and bond admissions before they are public. See the compliance section below.
Key term

ISM (International Securities Market): LSE's market for debt sold to professional investors. It is "a UK MTF and is operated by the Exchange as a Recognised Investment Exchange"; admission "is determined by the Exchange", and ISM securities "are not admitted to the Official List maintained by the FCA" [S346]. LSE markets it on speed: comments within three days of first submission and two days after that ("3+2") [S347].

Key term

Listing (or admission) particulars: the disclosure document a bond issuer publishes so investors know what they are buying. On ISM they are called admission particulars; the Exchange's approval "is not an approval or verification" of them, and exempt issuers do not need them [S346]. Main Market debt involves the FCA and a prospectus or listing particulars; 2026 rules now refer to POATR [S346, S347].

Bullet 3: "Or Delivery of business intelligence, strategic initiatives, and operational improvements"
Business management in its purest form: COO offices, PMOs and transformation teams across Markets.
LSEG unitNo single team. Live postings show the CDSClear Transformation function at LCH SA, a Markets Operations and Controls COO office, a Post Trade Solutions PMO and a Markets Operations Transformation PMO [S12, S18, S4]. Confirmed that these teams exist. A cross-Markets strategy team is Inferred: no public page names one, and a search for "chief of staff" roles found nothing relevant [S319].
Day to dayRefresh an MI dashboard (volumes, revenue per client, onboarding times); write one section of a steering committee pack; keep the RAID log; map a manual process and propose automation; benchmark a competitor's launch. Inferred The Business Manager posting describes "high-quality executive materials" and "consistency in KPIs, MI, and performance reporting" [S18].
CounterpartiesInternal: business heads and COOs, Finance, Technology, Risk and Compliance. The CDSClear programme manager coordinates "Risk, Operations, Product, Technology, Client Services, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Shared Services" [S12].
Good looks likeNumbers leadership trusts; decisions taken on time; projects delivered "on time, within budget and within agreed scope" [S12].
ToolsExcel, PowerPoint, Power BI or Tableau, project trackers, the GRC system for controls [S5, S19]. Inferred for this team.
Structural factThe operating engine of Markets sits largely offshore. 19 of 45 open Markets roles are in Taguig City, Manila, mostly operations, onboarding, PMO and control roles [S4]. LSEG cut engineering headcount from about 15,100 to 14,200 in 2025 while raising in-house engineers from 49% to 60% [S22, S300]. "Operational improvements" in London usually means working with a team in Manila, Colombo or Bengaluru. Inferred
Key term

COO office: the team around a Chief Operating Officer that runs the business's machinery: budgets, headcount plans, KPIs, governance packs, change programmes. LSEG's Markets version is described as "a critical enabler to the COO by driving business performance, governance, and execution discipline" [S18].

Key term

PMO (programme management office): the team that tracks a large change programme: plans, budgets, risks and decisions. RAID log: its core tracker of Risks, Actions, Issues and Decisions. MI (management information): regular data packs that tell managers how the business is performing.

Bullet 4: "Or Risk teams, which involves monitoring and analysing risks, and interpreting data in readiness for the delivery of risk projects or reporting."
First-line risk work, most likely at LCH or Post Trade Solutions. Know which of three kinds of "risk" you mean.
LSEG unitThree kinds of risk sit in Markets [S28, S19, S10]: (1) CCP financial risk at LCH Ltd and LCH SA: margin, default fund, collateral; (2) operational risk in the first line, e.g. the PTS Operational Risk Manager who keeps "the PTS control library within the GRC system" [S19]; (3) market integrity: Market Supervision monitors trading on LSE and Turquoise for abuse under MAR [S10]. Which one hosts interns is Inferred.
Day to dayPull and clean margin or exposure data; reconcile risk reports; write commentary on why a metric moved; collect control evidence on a monthly cycle ("Monitor the timely submission of evidence (e.g., monthly/quarterly)") [S19]; analyse incident logs; help draft a committee or regulatory report. Inferred
CounterpartiesClearing members (large banks) and their clients; internal risk committees; second-line Group Risk under CRO Balbir Bakhshi; Internal Audit; regulators [S23, S19]. The PTS role must "Work with second-line risk, compliance, and internal audit during reviews" [S19].
Good looks likeNo surprises: accurate, on-time reporting; issues found and escalated early; remediation tracked to closure [S19].
ToolsGRC (governance, risk and compliance) system, Excel, risk MI packs, incident logs [S19]. Python or SQL for data work is Inferred.
Structural factAt a clearing house, risk and revenue move together. SwapClear cleared a record $1,941trn of interest rate swap notional in 2025 and holds over 90% of the cleared market [S22, S23]. Net Treasury Income (interest earned on margin cash) rose 12.6% in H1 2026, "driven by strong growth in cash collateral balances supported by elevated market volatility" [S24]. Volatility lifts revenue and default risk at the same time.
Key term

CCP (central counterparty): a clearing house that "sits in the middle of trades as the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer" [S304]. If a member defaults, the CCP takes over its positions. LCH has managed nine member defaults, all within the initial margin it held [S351].

Key term

Margin: collateral a member must post. Initial margin covers the likely loss if the member defaults; LCH sets it at 99.7% confidence (99% for Listed Rates) [S351]. Default fund: a pool all members pay into, used only after the defaulter's own margin and LCH's own capital. Notional: the face value a derivative is based on, not money that changes hands.

How you will work

"Joining as an intern will allow you to be an individual contributor, and assist the product lifecycle, and work as a team to develop specialist skills."
Means You will own a deliverable (an analysis, a deck, a tracker, an MI pack), not shadow. "Product lifecycle" reflects LSEG's "product-led operating model" [S22]. Reported What good looks like One finished piece of work with your name on it that someone uses after you leave. Inferred Use it Interns on Higherin describe exactly this: a Post Trade intern "Working in Quantile with the marketing team. Testing our systems ... Working with Acadia with benchmarking" [S41].
"To allow us to place you in the right area, during the recruitment process we will get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business."
Means The matching mechanism described above. Every stage is partly a placement interview [S2]. Use it Give the assessors data: name the seat you lean towards and why, and show you would be useful in the others. Inferred
"To be eligible, you must be a penultimate year undergraduate student due to complete all the requirements of your course summer 2028."
Means Correct for a June 2027 start. The careers page's "summer 2027" is stale; trust the JD [S1, S37]. Confirmed
"These are real roles. Our 9 weeks summer interns play a part in the success of our organisation, just like they would do as a graduate."
Means Interns sit in live teams with real deadlines. Testimonials agree: Higherin reviewers rate LSEG internships 4.8/5 (five reviews), with a Capital Markets intern saying "I acquired financial knowledge across private, primary and secondary markets" [S41]. Reported Glassdoor snippets mention "real responsibilities" but also a programme that "could have been better organised by HR" [S42]. Reported

What we are looking for

"We are passionate about recruiting people who want to understand the full breadth of our organisation, how it fits together, how it functions - and are interested in playing a part of our development, as it grows and diversifies."
Testing Whether you understand LSEG as a set of linked but separate businesses. Show it One sentence on how they fit: the 2025 merger of Capital Markets and Post Trade into Markets; RepoAgent, built by Post Trade Solutions and Tradeweb together, which LSEG cites as "the strength of collaboration within Markets" [S22]; FXall and LCH data now inside Workspace [S300]. Then one sentence on the limits: LCH must clear on open, non-discriminatory terms and cannot favour LSEG venues [S305].
"You should have a demonstrable interest in financial markets, which you've built through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities."
Testing Evidence, not enthusiasm. Show it A habit (for example, reading LSEG's quarterly KPIs: FX ADV, SwapClear notional, UK value traded [S301, S302]) plus one thing you did with it. Candidate CV details are not known to this pack: see the CV part for a method.
"A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions."
Testing Can you go from a number to a recommendation? Show it Example from public data: FX revenue £272m on $525bn average daily volume in 2025 gives a rough revenue capture rate, a metric LSEG does not publish [S301]. Inferred Say clearly it is your own metric. Seat All four; heaviest in bullets 2 and 3.
"Individuals who are able to connect the dots and think strategically."
Testing Second-order thinking. Show it "Volatility raises FX volumes and LCH's margin balances, but it also raises default risk, so the same event is good news for revenue and a test for risk" [S23, S24]. Inferred for the linkage.
"The environment we work in is fast paced, you'll need to demonstrate focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands."
Testing How you behave when priorities collide. Figure 8 shows a rule for that. Show it A story where the brief changed mid-way and you re-planned without dropping quality.
"People who can collaborate with others, using their strong communication skills in the process."
Testing Partnership, one of LSEG's four values. Every seat is a coordinating seat: the CDSClear programme spans nine functions [S12], and London teams work daily with hubs in Manila, Colombo and Bengaluru [S4]. Show it A story where you got something done through people who did not report to you.
"Ideal candidates will have the rights to work in the UK without restrictions for the duration of the programme."
Means "Ideal", not "must". If this affects you, check with Early Careers before the assessment centre. Inferred
"You will stand out to us if you can demonstrate and recognise that what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it."
Means A values test. Strengths interviews will probe how you got a result, not just the result [S2]. Map your stories to the four values in LSEG's own words [S307].
ValueLSEG's definition [S307]What or how?Story that proves it
Integrity"We stand by our principles and deliver on our promises. We earn trust by acting responsibly."BothYou hit a deadline without cutting a corner; or you flagged your own mistake early.
Partnership"Our open model is integral to how we do business. We forge long-term relationships; we work together to solve evolving needs and deliver strategic outcomes."HowYou got a result through people you did not manage. Note "open model" echoes LCH's open-access rule [S305].
Excellence"Our breadth of capabilities sets us apart, globally. We achieve industry-leading outcomes by combining unique, diverse perspectives and knowledge across markets."WhatA measurable outcome that came from combining different views or skills.
Change"We embrace change. We combine human ingenuity, technology, risk management, and insight to create the products and services that lead and shape the industry."HowYou changed a process, adopted a tool, or adapted when the plan broke, and managed the risk of doing so.
Don't say this

"I always deliver results whatever it takes." In a firm that runs a clearing house and an exchange, "whatever it takes" is the wrong answer. The JD has told you that how matters as much as what.

Headcount: how big is the team around you?

LSEG does not publish headcount by division, or intern intake numbers [S23, S57]. The estimates below are ours. The method is shown so you can defend it or drop it.

EstimateRangeMethod
Markets division staff, worldwide5,000 to 9,000 Inferred, low confidenceGroup headcount was 28,516 at 31 Dec 2025 [S23]. Markets carried £1,357m of £3,711m divisional operating costs, about 37% [S22]. 37% of 28,516 is about 10,400. That is a ceiling: Markets costs include Tradeweb's high US pay and non-staff costs, and the 14,200 engineers sit in a central function serving all divisions [S22]. Discounting for both gives 5,000 to 9,000.

How the work splits

Three splits matter for an intern.

  • London versus the hubs. 19 of the 45 open Markets roles are in Taguig City, Manila: operations, onboarding, PMO and control roles [S4]. India holds 8,541 of LSEG's 28,516 staff, the UK 5,043 [S300]. London keeps product, client, regulatory and leadership roles. Your "operational improvement" project will probably involve a team you meet on video. Inferred
  • Business versus the centre. Risk ownership is assigned per principal risk to named executives: central counterparty risk to the Head of Markets; technology to the CIO; data to divisional heads and the COO [S302]. First-line teams inside Markets own their risks; Group Risk provides "Coverage (Data and Analytics, Markets, Post Trade and Operations)" [S314].
  • Client coverage. A new Group Head of Sales and Account Management (Chris Coleman, January 2026) suggests account management is being pulled towards a central model [S306]. Inferred for the implication. Ask about it.

Why have a business management function at all? Figure 6 shows the mechanism. Markets is a set of separate regulated companies plus central functions. Without someone who owns the numbers and the calendar, every party has to coordinate with every other party.

Figure 7 follows one request through the team. It is an FX client issue because that seat has the most moving parts, but the shape (log, triage, route, fix, confirm, learn) is the same for a strategy question.

The scarce resource in any business management team is analyst time. Interns hit this in week two, when two people ask for something by the same day. Figure 8 gives you a rule to use and, in interview, a strengths answer about competing priorities.

Internal clients and external counterparties, concretely

Inside LSEG

  • Business heads of each unit: LSE plc, LSEG FX, LCH Ltd, LCH SA, Post Trade Solutions [S28, S32].
  • The COO office and PMOs: Markets Operations and Controls; CDSClear Transformation; Markets Operations Transformation PMO in Bengaluru and Manila [S4, S12, S18].

  • Finance (budgets, forecasts), Technology (delivery), Legal and Compliance (sign-off) [S12].
  • Group Risk (second line) and Internal Audit (third line) [S19, S300].
  • Other divisions: Data & Analytics and FTSE Russell, which use Markets data. The DCM team works with "Issuer Services, FTSE Russell, Admissions, Regulation, RNS, LSEG FX and Data & Analytics" [S316].

Outside LSEG

  • Banks as FX liquidity providers, as clearing members of LCH, and as part-owners of Post Trade Solutions (11 banks hold 20%) [S17, S300].
  • Buy-side firms: asset managers and hedge funds on FXall; clients clearing through members at LCH [S17, S304].
  • Corporate treasurers hedging currency on FXall [S17].
  • Issuers: sovereigns, banks, corporates and emerging-market borrowers listing debt; companies listing equity [S15, S16].
  • Advisers: DCM and ECM bankers, capital markets lawyers, nominated advisers for AIM [S15].
  • Regulators: the FCA (LSE plc as an RIE; UK MTFs), the Bank of England (LCH Ltd), the Central Bank of Ireland (EU FX MTF), the ACPR in France (LCH SA) [S13, S304, S341, S105].

Why this matters

If you are asked "what would success look like for you in nine weeks?", answer in the team's currency. In seat 1: "a review pack the account manager used with a client, and one recurring issue closed for good". In seat 4: "evidence in on time, and commentary my manager did not have to rewrite". Inferred

MK1025KMThe compliance and control dimension

Markets is the most regulated corner of LSEG. LSE plc is an RIE supervised by the FCA; LCH Ltd is a Recognised Clearing House supervised by the Bank of England; the FX venues are MTFs licensed in the UK and Ireland [S13, S304, S341]. As an intern you will see information that could move markets or that a client has trusted LSEG with. The rules below are bright lines: there is no grey area for an intern, because the answer is always "stop and ask".

Key term

MAR (UK Market Abuse Regulation): the law against insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation. Inside information is "information of a precise nature, which has not been made public" that is "likely to have a significant effect on the prices" if it were (Article 7) [S349].

Key term

Insider list: a record issuers and their advisers must keep of "all persons who have access to inside information", with the reason and "date and time" of access, kept for "at least five years" (MAR Article 18) [S348]. If you work on a live deal, your name may go on one.

Key term

Three lines of defence: "Accountability for risk management ... sits within the first line of defence, independent oversight and challenge with the second line and objective, independent assurance with the third line" [S300]. First line is the business (you); second is Risk and Compliance; third is Internal Audit.

Key term

STOR (suspicious transaction and order report): a report a venue files with the regulator when trading may be abusive. Market Supervision files them for LSE and Turquoise trading "as outlined in the UK Financial Conduct Authority's Code of Market Conduct and MAR" [S10].

Bright lineThe ruleWhere it bitesWhat you do
Inside information and insider listsMAR Articles 7, 17 and 18 [S349, S350, S348]. LSEG's Code of Conduct bans trading on "confidential, proprietary, inside and/or material non-public information" and requires need-to-know [S307].Seat 2: planned IPOs and bond admissions; any seat that sees results before publication.Do not trade, tip or hint. Ask whether you are on an insider list. Keep pipeline names out of shared decks.
Issuer pipeline confidentialityThe Exchange reviews ISM admissions itself; announcements go out via RNS as Dealing Notices [S346, S347]. RNS staff need "discretion, and ability to respect confidentiality at all times" [S20].Seat 2; also anyone near Issuer Services or RNS.Never name a pipeline issuer outside the team, including to friends or on LinkedIn.

If unsure which side you are on, ask. Inferred

LCH must not favour LSEG venues, and information barriers let rival venues talk to LCH "assured of the confidentiality of those discussions from LSEG" [S305].Seat 4, and seat 3 if your project spans LCH and a venue.Never pass member positions or rival venues' data to LSEG venue teams.

Say this in the interview (unprompted)

"Because LSE plc is a Recognised Investment Exchange and LCH is a systemic clearing house, I'd expect to see information I can't share, whether that's a pipeline issuer, a client's flow or a member's positions. My default would be need-to-know: use published or aggregated data unless my task needs more, and ask before I share anything across teams."

Don't say this

Naming a company you believe is about to list in London, or claiming to know anything about LSEG's pipeline. Do not cite a Bank of England fine on LCH or a named outage from memory: none was found in our research.

MK1002KM
Part 2

The firm from the inside

LSEG as an operating model: who pays it, what it keeps, who it answers to, and where the Markets division you would join sits in the machine.

This part treats LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) as a machine you could draw on a whiteboard, not as a brochure. Each section answers one plain question: where did it come from, how does money come in and go out, who has signed up to what, how is risk controlled, what has grown, why the share price fell, what the leaders say comes next, and where the bodies are buried. Every figure carries a source marker; the source table sits in Part 15.

In one breath: LSEG sells trusted information (data, indices, screening) on multi-year subscriptions, and market plumbing (venues and clearing houses) paid per trade or per unit of risk. You would join the plumbing side, Markets: about 40% of revenue and the fastest-growing division in H1 2026 [S70, S71].

MK1028KMA. Origins and the founding insight

The first product was data, not trading

In 1698, at Jonathan's Coffee House in London, John Castaing began publishing a list of stock and commodity prices called "The Course of the Exchange and other things" [S78] Confirmed. That is the founding insight worth remembering: the business that became LSEG started by selling prices. People paid for a trusted number. Trading rules came later, in 1801, when "the first regulated exchange comes into existence in London" [S78].

Today LSEG calls itself "a leading financial markets infrastructure and data provider" [S74]. In a sense the group has come full circle: the bulk of its income is again from selling trusted information, with the trading and clearing machinery as the second engine Inferred.

Key term

Financial market infrastructure (FMI): the shared systems that let markets work: exchanges (where buyers meet sellers), clearing houses (which guarantee trades), settlement systems and data feeds. If an FMI stops, many firms stop with it, which is why FMIs are tightly supervised.

From coffee house to FTSE 100 group

Four shifts made the modern group Inferred framing: club to company (1986 Big Bang; listed on its own market in July 2001) [S78]; exchange to group (Borsa Italiana, 2007) [S78]; trading to clearing (majority of LCH, 2013, the deal that made LSEG systemically important) [S78]; and exchange to data and index giant (FTSE Group 1995, Frank Russell 2014, Refinitiv 2021, about $27bn) [S78, S84]. Refinitiv brought the Workspace desktop (then Eikon), real-time data, FXall and FX Matching, and the majority stake in Tradeweb [S300]. LSEG is now a FTSE 100 company, ticker LSEG [S70].

Source uncertain

Dates the research did not re-verify: demutualisation (around 2000), FTSE becoming wholly owned (reported as December 2011), the Refinitiv announcement (reported as August 2019) and David Schwimmer's start as CEO (2018) [S78]. The history page itself omits the 2021 Borsa Italiana sale. Use the years, not the exact days, for these.

Why this matters

The two failed combinations in the table below (Deutsche Börse 2017, HKEX 2019) share one lesson: LSEG's clearing assets are so important that regulators and the board treat any change of control as a public-interest question [S80, S82] Inferred. That is why LCH is run at arm's length with its own board, and why "open access" keeps coming up.

Mission and purpose, in their own words

Quote these exactly; they are the wording the research team actually read.

  • Purpose (Annual Report 2025, published early 2026): "Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth." [S74] The JD repeats it word for word.
  • David Schwimmer, 12 Dec 2022 (Microsoft deal): "This strategic partnership is a significant milestone on LSEG's journey towards becoming the leading global financial markets infrastructure and data business, and will transform the experience for our customers." [S79]
  • Annual Report 2025 on the model: "When other exchange groups focused on vertical integration of trading and clearing, we championed open access" [S300].
  • Results statements, 26 Feb and 30 Jul 2026: "Our customers believe our solutions are more valuable in an AI world, not less." [S72, S70]
  • Schwimmer, 30 Jul 2026 call: "As we've said before, our sector moves slowly. Given the range and complexity of issues to address, this is a marathon, not a sprint, and LSEG is the best running partner." [S71]

Values, from the JD and the Code of Conduct: Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change. Partnership is defined as "Our open model is integral to how we do business" [S307], which is the open-access idea in values language Inferred.

Key term

Total income excl. recoveries: LSEG's headline revenue. "Recoveries" are fees it collects for other firms' content (for example other exchanges' prices) and passes on, so they are stripped out.

Key term

Organic growth (constant currency): growth with acquisitions, disposals and exchange-rate moves removed. It answers "did the existing business sell more?" This is the number analysts watch.

Key term

EBITDA: earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Roughly the operating profit before paying for past investment. "Adjusted" strips out one-offs. The margin is EBITDA divided by income.

Key term

Recurring revenue: income that repeats without a new sale each time, such as subscriptions and licences. It is valued highly because it is predictable.

Since the FY2025 results LSEG reports four divisions [S72, S70]. Markets was formed by merging the old Capital Markets and Post Trade divisions [S72, S76].

Second, the highest-margin pound in the group is an index licence; the lowest is a desktop seat, which needs heavy content costs and engineering [S70] Inferred.

The JD names five businesses. Mapped onto the reported lines Inferred: London Stock Exchange and Turquoise sit in Equities; LSEG FX is the FX line; Tradeweb is most of Fixed Income, Derivatives & Other, which at £864m is 45% of Markets income in H1 2026; LCH and post-trade spread across OTC Derivatives, Securities & Reporting, Non-Cash Collateral and Net Treasury Income, together £1,244m in FY2025 and £681m in H1 2026 (36% of Markets).

Key term

Net treasury income (NTI): clearing members post cash as margin. LCH invests it very safely and keeps part of the interest after paying members their share. It rises with margin balances and interest rates.

Key term

Non-controlling interest (minority): when LSEG controls a firm it does not fully own (Tradeweb 50.9%), it reports 100% of its revenue, then subtracts the other owners' share of profit lower down: £334m in 2025 [S72, S74].

The trace: from a customer's pound to dividends and buybacks

Follow one pound; Figure 11 draws the same chain to scale [S70, S72, S74] Inferred chain:

  1. A customer pays. A bank pays for Workspace seats and data feeds (D&A). An ETF issuer pays FTSE Russell a fee tied to the fund's assets. A bank pays for World-Check. A trader pays per trade on LSE, Turquoise, FXall or Tradeweb. A clearing member pays clearing fees to LCH and posts margin, on which LCH earns treasury income.
  2. Cost of sales (£1,113m in 2025) mostly pays for third-party content and revenue shares, such as the SwapClear surplus share to founding banks. Gross profit: £8,233m.
  3. Operating costs (£3,711m adjusted, 71% people) leave adjusted EBITDA of £4,523m, a 50.3% margin.
  4. Investment and claims: capex of £919m (10.2% of income), tax at about 24%, interest, and the minorities' share (Tradeweb's other owners above all).
  5. Equity free cash flow of £2.4bn (guided at least £2.7bn for 2026) funds dividends (£718m cash in 2025) and buybacks (£2.1bn), within a target of 1.5x to 2.5x net debt to EBITDA (1.8x at Dec 2025, 2.1x at June 2026).
Key term

Capex (capital expenditure): money spent on long-lived assets, mostly software and platforms here. It does not hit EBITDA, but it does use cash. LSEG wants it down from 10.2% of income to about 8% by 2029 [S72].

Key term

Share buyback: the company buys its own shares and cancels them, so each remaining share owns more of the profits. It returns cash without committing to a higher dividend every year.

Key term

AEPS (adjusted earnings per share): profit per share excluding one-offs and acquisition amortisation. FY2025: 420.6p, +15.7% [S72].

How the money has grown

Income excl. recoveries rose from £7,428m in 2022 to £8,986m in 2025, with organic growth between 6.3% and 7.7% every year and the EBITDA margin rising from 47.8% to 50.3% [S73, S77, S76, S72]. Adjusted EPS rose from 272.4p (2021) to 420.6p (2025) and the dividend from 107.0p (2022) to 150.0p (2025) [S73, S77, S72]. Staff numbers rose more slowly than income: 27,386 at end 2024, 28,516 at end 2025 [S74].

Source uncertain: headcount

The Annual Report gives 28,516 employees at 31 Dec 2025 [S74]. The JD says "25,000 people across 65 countries" and the May 2026 investor deck says "over 26,000 people in 65 countries" [S303]. The FY2025 results line "reduced headcount from 15,100 to around 14,200" refers to engineering, not the whole group [S300]. In interview say "about 28,500 at the end of 2025, per the annual report" and do not quote the JD figure as current.

Key term

Revenue surplus share: SwapClear's founding banks were promised a slice of its surplus revenue. LSEG paid £1.2bn to shrink that slice, which lifted group EBITDA margin by about 100bps straight away [S72].

Key term

Activist investor: a fund that buys a stake and then pushes management publicly or privately for changes, such as buybacks, disposals or strategy shifts.

Why this matters: the partnership pattern

LSEG keeps signing deals where customers co-own the infrastructure: founding banks in SwapClear, 11 banks in Post Trade Solutions, the user community in Turquoise (15.8% minority) [S72, S300]. The bargain is "use LSEG, but keep a seat and a share" Inferred. It wins trust and flow; the cost is value leaking to minorities (Tradeweb 49.1%, PTS 20%, Turquoise 15.8%, LCH 5.6% at end 2025) and payments like the £1.2bn [S300, S301].

Source uncertain: LCH ownership

LSEG reached 94.2% of LCH Group after its 2024 purchase [S121]; the Annual Report shows 94.4% at end 2025 after a small October 2025 top-up [S300]; a July 2026 agreement (up to 1.05% more, €70m) takes it above 95% on completion [S70]. Say "about 94%, going above 95%". Never say 82.6%.

MK1031KMD. The risk and control architecture

LSEG is not one regulated firm. It is a set of separately licensed companies, each with its own regulator, board and capital. Regulation forces that: a clearing house takes on the risk of every member defaulting, so its money must be ring-fenced from the exchange's [S304] Inferred rationale.

Who supervises what

EntityLegal statusMain supervisorNotes and source
London Stock Exchange plcRecognised Investment Exchange (RIE) under Part XVIII of FSMA 2000FCARuns Main Market, AIM and the ISM (an MTF it operates as an RIE) [S95, S300, S346] Reported
Turquoise Global Holdings LtdInvestment firm operating an MTFFCA (UK); Dutch AFM for Turquoise Europe B.V., Amsterdam84.2% owned [S95, S300] Reported
LSEG FX (FXall, Matching)UK MTF; EU MTF in IrelandFCA; Central Bank of Ireland[S341] Confirmed
LCH Ltd (London)Recognised Clearing House (CCP)Bank of EnglandBoE non-objection needed for board appointments; own board, audit, risk and resilience committees [S304, S94] Confirmed
LCH SA (Paris)CCPACPR (French prudential regulator); registered with US CFTC and SECBoE has an MoU to rely on French authorities [S105, S94] Reported
TradewebSeparately listed on Nasdaq (TW)Not covered in this researchLSEG 50.9% economic, c.89.9% voting [S74, S137]
Source uncertain

The AMF's role at LCH SA was not verified, and LCH SA's regulators were read from search snippets only [S105]. Say "LCH SA is supervised in France, by the ACPR among others" rather than listing bodies you cannot back up.

Key term

RIE (Recognised Investment Exchange): the UK legal status of a full regulated exchange, granted and supervised by the FCA. The London Stock Exchange is one.

Key term

MTF (Multilateral Trading Facility): a trading venue run by an investment firm under lighter rules than an exchange. Turquoise and FXall's venues are MTFs.

Key term

CCP (central counterparty): a clearing house that becomes buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer. If one side defaults, the CCP still pays the other. LCH is LSEG's CCP group.

Key term

Initial margin: collateral a member posts up front to cover the loss LCH could suffer closing out that member's positions if it failed. Variation margin moves daily with prices.

The LCH default waterfall, in order

LCH's own words: "The collateral and default fund contributions of the defaulting Clearing Member are utilised first, followed by the CCP's own funds and then by the default fund contributions of non-defaulting Clearing Members." [S93]

#LayerWhose moneySizing rule or figure
1Defaulter's initial marginThe failed memberSet to 99.7% confidence for most services (99% for Listed Rates), above regulatory minimums of 99% (listed) and 99.5% (OTC); "multiple intraday margin calls" [S93, S351]
2Defaulter's default fund contributionThe failed member"Defaulter-pays" principle [S93]
3LCH's own capital ("skin in the game")LCH, so ultimately LSEG25% of LCH's minimum regulatory capital [S93]
4Other members' default fund contributionsSurviving members, sharedSized by stress tests to cover "multiple defaults in extreme market circumstances" [S74]

Scale: total margin and default fund collateral across LSEG's CCPs was £277bn at 31 Dec 2025 (cash £91bn, non-cash £186bn), peaking at £303bn during 2025 (£334bn in 2024). The £90bn cash portfolio was 99.95% invested securely, with a weighted average maturity of 82 days [S74]. Track record: LCH says it has "managed 9 member defaults and, in all cases, losses were within the initial margin held" [S351]; in the 2008 Lehman default SwapClear handled a $9trn book using about 35% of Lehman's initial margin [S354].

Key term

Default fund: a pot every clearing member pays into, used only after the defaulter's own margin and contribution and the CCP's own capital are exhausted. It mutualises extreme losses.

Key term

Skin in the game: the CCP's own money placed in the waterfall ahead of other members' funds, so management loses first if its risk models are wrong.

Three lines of defence and the group risk framework

"LSEG operates a three lines of defence model, providing appropriate segregation of duties and clear roles and responsibilities, including Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit." [S74]

  • First line: the business owns its risks. Example: a "First Line Business Continuity Management team at LCH Ltd" running switch tests and recovery-site tests [S318].
  • Second line: Risk and Compliance give independent oversight and challenge. Group Risk has central teams (policy, tooling, cyber, third-party risk) and coverage teams for divisions including Markets [S314].
  • Third line: Internal Audit gives independent assurance [S74].

An Enterprise Risk Management Framework and a Group Risk Taxonomy feed risk appetite statements the Board approves each year. Committees include the Board Risk Committee, the Board Audit Committee and an executive Group Executive Risk Committee with sub-committees for financial, model, and technology and cyber risk [S74]. Each principal risk has a named executive owner: central counterparty risk sits with the Head of Markets, technology and cyber with the CIO, regulatory change with the General Counsel and CEO [S302].

Key term

Three lines of defence: the people who take a risk manage it (1st), a separate team checks them (2nd), and auditors check both (3rd). The JD's "risk teams" track lives mostly in the first and second lines.

Why this produces stability Inferred

The waterfall puts the defaulter's money first, so members have a reason to manage their own risk. LCH's capital comes next, so its managers carry real downside. Mutual funds are a last resort sized by stress tests. Commercially, stability comes from high retention (92.8% subscription revenue retention in H1 2026), multi-year data contracts and a mix of data and transaction income: the Annual Report calls this "all-weather growth" [S70, S74].

MK1032KME. Strategy and business mix

What has grown

  • Group: organic growth of 5.8%, 6.3%, 7.1%, 7.7%, 7.1% for 2021 to 2025, then 8.4% in H1 2026, with Q1 2026 at 9.8%, which LSEG called a record [S73, S70, S75].
  • Markets: Schwimmer says annual growth "has averaged almost 10%" over five years: "There have been strong years and really strong years, but no weak years." [S71]
  • FTSE Russell: ETF assets tracking its indices rose from $1.43trn (end 2024) to $1.83trn (end 2025) to $2.19trn (June 2026); 44 new equity ETFs in 2025, a record [S72, S70].
  • Tradeweb: ADV $2.62trn in 2025 (+16.9%) and $3.18trn in H1 2026 (+24.8%) [S72, S70].
  • SwapClear: $1,941trn notional cleared in 2025 (+21.2%) and $1,165trn in H1 2026 (+29.4%) [S72, S70].
  • Slow part: Workflows (the Workspace desktop) grew only 3.1% in 2025 and 2.8% in H1 2026, against 7.5% for Data & Feeds [S72, S70].
Why this matters for a Markets intern

Markets is the volume-driven, volatility-sensitive engine. H1 2026 was helped by "elevated market volatility" [S70]; the war involving Iran drove a spike in trading across asset classes [S223] Reported. A good interview question to ask: how much of the 11.9% is structural (new clients, products) and how much is cyclical? Inferred

New: an AI pricing framework

In H1 2026 LSEG set out how it will charge for AI use: a recurring subscription to license its datasets for AI models; a recurring charge for MCP access, with usage bands to come; and AI Search priced into the annual Workspace price review up to a usage cap, with Deep Research as a premium add-on [S70]. LSEG also says it will stop reporting ASV as a KPI at the end of 2026 [S72].

Key term

ASV (Annual Subscription Value): the yearly value of all subscription contracts at a date. Its growth (6.1% at June 2026) signals where subscription revenue is heading [S70].

Key term

MCP (Model Context Protocol): an open standard for connecting AI applications to data sources. LSEG uses it to pipe licensed data into customers' AI tools.

MK1033KMF. LSEG as a public company: the derating, told straight

LSEG is listed on the London Stock Exchange, ticker LSEG, and is in the FTSE 100 [S70]. Its own share price is the market's running verdict on the strategy. Over 2025 and early 2026 that verdict turned sharply negative, even while the business kept growing.

The sequence

  1. Peak: a close of 12,095p on 5 Feb 2025 [S90].
  2. 31 Jul 2025, H1 2025 results: shares fell 7.9% on the day as growth in subscription value (ASV) slowed; Bloomberg headline: "LSEG Shares Plunge on Slowing Growth in Subscription Value" [S90, S102, S103] Reported.
  3. 3 Feb 2026, the AI scare: down 12.8% in one day (8,234p to 7,180p) as worries that large language models, "like Anthropic's Claude", would let customers bypass terminals and aggregated data triggered a software selloff. Low close 7,170p on 4 Feb 2026, about 41% below the peak [S90, S88].
  4. 11 Feb 2026, Elliott: reports that the activist had built a stake; shares rose as much as 7%, settling 2.3% up. The stock had "fallen by more than 35% in the past 12 months" [S86, S87].
  5. 26 Feb 2026, FY2025 results: £3bn buyback plan and new 2027 to 2029 targets; close up 9.1% [S90, S72].
  6. 11 Jun 2026: Reuters: shares up 27% since the Elliott news but 23% below the 2025 peak; about 18 times forward earnings, about 30% below Moody's and 40% below MSCI; 90% of 20 analysts rate it buy [S88] Reported.
  7. 18 Jun 2026, Redburn: Rothschild & Co Redburn cut to neutral, target £120 to £104, putting about 30% of EBITDA at risk in a "realistic base case"; close down 7.0% [S89, S90].
  8. 30 Jul 2026, record H1: guidance raised, yet the close fell 6.4% (9,198p to 8,606p) as investors weighed the timing of AI monetisation [S90, S108].
  9. 5 Oct 2026: about 8,216p intraday [S90].
Source uncertain

Results day, 30 Jul 2026: Yahoo closes show a 6.4% fall [S90]; Reuters wrote that shares "fell 3.1% on the day" [S223], likely at a different time of day. Say "fell on the day despite a record half". Market value: about $52bn per an aggregator [S148], roughly £40bn on our own share-count estimate Inferred; check before quoting.

The two sides of the argument

The bear case

Redburn: shifting to "modular, API- and AI-driven data consumption may prove structurally deflationary for parts of the model" [S89]. UBS's Michael Werner: "There is still a 'show me' story for AI. It's one thing to have usage, it's another to start charging people." [S88] Workflows growth is under 3% [S70].

The bull case

Schwimmer: "90% of our data revenues come from real-time or data that is proprietary." [S71] About 98% of revenue comes from proprietary data, IP and market infrastructure [S73]. MCP customers rose from 60 trialling (Feb 2026) to over 200 engaged (Jul 2026) [S72, S70]. Markets, untouched by the AI worry, grew 11.9% [S70].

Key term

Derating: the share price falls further than profits, so the multiple investors pay for each pound of earnings shrinks. LSEG fell to about 18 times forward earnings (share price divided by next year's expected earnings per share) [S88].

Say this in the interview: "why join a stock that fell 40%?"

"The share price and the business told different stories. From the 2025 peak to the February low the shares fell about 41%, but over the same period income grew 7% and H1 2026 was a record half. The fall was about one fear: that AI tools shrink the value of terminals and aggregated data. The division I'm applying to, Markets, is mostly exchanges and clearing, the plumbing that AI trading still has to run through, and it grew 11.9% with a 58.6% margin. So I see the derating as a debate about one part of the group, and I'd rather join the part that's growing fastest while that debate is being settled."

Don't say this

"The market has got it wrong" or "the stock is cheap." You do not know, and interviewers at a listed company are careful about share price talk. Talk about the business, not the price.

No CEO or Chair change was found as of 5 Oct 2026; David Schwimmer is CEO, Michel-Alain Proch CFO, Don Robert Chair [S70, S74]. The one board change: Amit Zavery, President, COO and Chief Product Officer of ServiceNow, joins as a non-executive director on 1 Dec 2026 [S92], reportedly to support the "LSEG Everywhere AI strategy" [S259].

What leadership says is coming

  • "More valuable in an AI world." The title of both the FY2025 results and Q1 2026 presentations [S73, S75]. The claim: AI needs data, compute and models; compute is an arms race, models are commoditising, so trusted licensed data gains value [S71].
  • LSEG Everywhere: AI-ready data delivered wherever customers work. Partnerships with Anthropic, Databricks, Microsoft Copilot Studio, OpenAI, Rogo and Snowflake (2025), then Amazon Quick and Google Gemini (H1 2026). MCP customers: over 60 trialling (Feb 2026), over 150 connected or onboarding (Apr 2026), over 200 engaged (Jul 2026) [S72, S75, S70].
  • Microsoft: Workspace in Teams, Excel and PowerPoint add-ins, Open Directory (20+ customers onboarded), Autex and DMI on Azure [S72, S70]. Reuters reports some investors find the rollout disappointing [S88] Reported.

Two quotes to hold: "Our Markets businesses had an exceptional first half, achieving double-digit growth through sustained investment. With our plans for LSE 24 and growing momentum of transactions on the Private Securities Market, we are opening up significant new market opportunities." (Schwimmer, 30 Jul 2026) [S70]. And Julia Hoggett: "LSE 24 will help support deeper liquidity, greater efficiency and broader participation in our markets" [S227].

Inference from hiring Inferred

Live job ads show where effort is going [S313 to S319]: FX account managers asked to "identify upsell, cross-sell, and new business opportunities across FX trading, workflow, data"; FX venue onboarding in Manila; a business programme manager for CDSClear coordinating risk, operations, product, technology, legal and finance; first-line business continuity at LCH Ltd; debt capital markets origination tasked with "market research and intelligence, competitive analysis". Add the strategy themes (forward-deployed engineers, AI pricing, 80+ Post Trade Solutions customers added in H1 2026, new venues: PSM, LSE 24, DiSH) [S70], and a Markets intern is most likely to meet: customer onboarding and analysis for FX, launch support for new venues, debt-listing and shareholder research, and risk reporting. That maps onto the JD's four tracks.

Part 3 goes deeper on teams. Here is what the research shows about the centre that every front-line business draws on.

Why this matters

LSEG says "As our different businesses have continued to become more closely integrated, potential reputational exposure has increased" [S302]. MK1003KM
Part 3

Why LSEG is built this way

LSEG is a set of separately licensed businesses held together by shared data, technology and customers, and kept apart on purpose where trust depends on it.

MK1038KMThe short answer, and how to use this part

Part 2 explained what LSEG sells and how the money flows. This part answers the harder interview question: why is it put together like this? An interviewer who asks "why LSEG?" or "how does the Markets division fit with the rest of the group?" is checking whether you can connect the dots, which is the JD's own phrase. The answer has four parts, and each needs a mechanism, not an adjective.

QuestionOne-line answerThe proof to quote
1. Why separate regulated businesses?Regulators require it, and open access only works if LCH cannot favour LSEG's own venues. That neutrality is what pulls in flow from everyone.LCH articles: "No exchange will be favoured over any other" [S305]
2. How do they work together?Through data, distribution and technology: venue data feeds products, Workspace carries FXall and LCH data, Microsoft runs the platform. Not through clearing favours.RepoAgent (Post Trade Solutions + Tradeweb, Nov 2025) [S301]
3. What do customers get?Liquidity, default protection, netting, margin efficiency, trusted data and access to capital. They accept the fees because the alternatives cost more in capital and risk.Lehman 2008: $9trn book handled using about 35% of Lehman's initial margin [S354]
4. What sits behind the front line?28,516 employees, 30% in India, 14,244 engineers, about 9,200 contractors. Central functions (risk, technology, sales, legal) wire into Markets through named owners and coverage teams.Group Risk has a "Coverage" team for Markets [S314]
Key terms for this part

RIE (Recognised Investment Exchange): the UK legal status of a full stock exchange, supervised by the FCA. London Stock Exchange plc is one. MTF (Multilateral Trading Facility): a trading venue run under lighter rules than an exchange; Turquoise and the LSEG FX venues are MTFs. CCP (central counterparty): a clearing house that becomes the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so one bank's failure does not spread. LCH is LSEG's CCP group. Open access: a CCP clears trades from any venue on the same terms, rather than only from its owner's venues. Vertical silo: one group owns the venue, the CCP and often the settlement system, and trades flow straight down inside the group.

MK1039KMQ1. Why a group of separate regulated businesses

From the outside, LSEG looks like one company. Legally, it is a parent holding a set of separately licensed businesses, several with outside owners. The ownership table below is the starting point. Part 2 covers what each business earns; here the point is the shape.

Business (legal entity)What it is, and its licenceLSEG stakeWho else owns it
London Stock Exchange plcRIE running the Main Market, AIM and the International Securities Market [S300, S346]100%None
Turquoise Global HoldingsEquity MTF, "majority owned by LSEG in partnership with the user community since 2010" [S300, S321]84.2%User banks, 15.8%
LCH Group (LCH Ltd, UK; LCH SA, France)CCPs: SwapClear, ForexClear, RepoClear, EquityClear, CDSClear. LCH Ltd is a Recognised Clearing House supervised by the Bank of England [S304]About 94% [S300, S121]Remaining minorities; LSEG agreed in July 2026 to take its stake above 95% [S72]
Tradeweb MarketsRates, credit, equities and money-market venues; listed on Nasdaq [S300, S303]50.9% economic; c.89.9% of votes [S300, S137]Public shareholders, 49.1% of economics
Post Trade SolutionsCompression and optimisation for uncleared derivatives [S300, S301]80%11 banks, 20% (bought for £170m, Oct 2025)
LSEG FX (FXall, FX Matching)Dealer-to-client and dealer-to-dealer FX venues; EU MTF supervised by the Central Bank of Ireland, UK MTF by the FCA [S341]100%None (came with Refinitiv)
Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell, Risk IntelligenceSubscription businesses [S303]100%None

There are seven mechanisms behind this shape. The first four explain why the businesses are kept apart. The last three explain why LSEG still wants to own them all.

Mechanism 1: regulation forces separate entities with their own capital and boards

A CCP, in LCH's own words, "sits in the middle of trades as the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer. If either party defaults on the trade, the Company owns the defaulter's risk" [S304]. That risk has to be fenced off. LCH Ltd has its own board and its own audit, remuneration, risk and operational resilience committees, and the Bank of England supervises it [S304]. The exchange is an RIE supervised by the FCA; the FX MTFs are licensed separately in Ireland and the UK [S341]. Confirmed

The logic: if a problem in one business could drain capital from another, a failure at a data business could weaken the CCP that guarantees trillions of dollars of swaps. Separate entities with separate capital stop that. Inferred

Mechanism 2: open access is written into LCH's constitution

When LSEG bought control of LCH.Clearnet in 2012 to 2013, the UK competition authority (the OFT) recorded that an open-access provision, "considered a core operating principle", would go into LCH's Articles of Association, the company's legal rulebook [S305]:

The clause to know by heart

"LCH.Clearnet's services must be offered on terms that are fair, reasonable, open and non-discriminatory, and on a basis such that LCH.Clearnet's risk is adequately controlled. No exchange will be favoured over any other and LSEG's trading services users will not be favoured over any other exchange's users." [S305] Confirmed

LCH Ltd still describes itself as "operating through an open access model that clears for major exchanges and platforms as well as a range of over-the-counter ('OTC') markets" [S304]. LSEG's 2025 Annual Report puts it as strategy: "When other exchange groups focused on vertical integration of trading and clearing, we championed open access" [S300]. So LSEG cannot run LCH as a captive that only serves its own venues. It chose not to, and it is legally bound not to.

Mechanism 3: horizontal, not a vertical silo

The OFT described the two ways to build a CCP: "stand-alone companies such as LCH.Clearnet or vertically integrated with a trading venue such as Deutsche Börse/Eurex Clearing" [S305]. Deutsche Börse uses the same words about itself: its plans "are based on the Group's vertically integrated business model ... The broad coverage of the entire value chain continues to be a key success factor" [S127]. Figure 19 shows the two shapes side by side.

In a silo, the venue and its CCP pull each other along: trade on Eurex and you clear at Eurex Clearing. In LSEG's horizontal model, LCH competes for flow from any venue, and LSEG's own venues get no privileged route in. Confirmed for the descriptions; the competitive logic is Inferred.

Mechanism 4: user governance keeps the banks inside

Before 2013, LCH was "owned 83 per cent by its clearing members and 17 per cent by trading venues" [S305]. The banks that use a CCP are also the ones whose money is at risk if another member fails, so they want a say. The 2012 deal kept that say:

  • LSEG appointed only 4 of 17 directors at the start, alongside user directors, venue directors and independent non-executives [S305].
  • Important "push matters" needed "60 per cent of votes cast, which must consist of at least 25 per cent of user shareholders" [S305].
  • Today "representatives of clearing members sit on the Company's Board", and the LCH Ltd Board Risk Committee includes clearing member and client representatives, "with no one constituent of the Risk Committee having a majority" [S304].
  • Product Advisory Groups and Risk Working Groups let participants comment on "risk policies, models and frameworks" [S304].
Source uncertain

The 4-of-17 board and the 60%/25% voting rule are from the 2012 OFT decision. LSEG now owns about 94% of LCH, so those exact numbers have probably changed. What is confirmed for 2025 is the member seats on the board and the risk committee rule [S304]. Quote the 2012 rules as history, not as today's governance.

Mechanism 5: the bank-partnership model is repeated on purpose

LSEG keeps building the same deal: customers co-own or share in the infrastructure they use.

WhereThe partnershipSource
SwapClear"Founded in collaboration with clearing members 25 years ago". Founding banks got about 30% of the revenue surplus (€0.2bn in 2024). LSEG paid £1.2bn to cut this to 15% for 2025 and 10% from 2026 to 2045, while extending the deal.[S304, S301] Confirmed
Post Trade Solutions11 banks took 20% in Oct 2025, "replicating the original LCH model that continues to prove so successful for LCH and its customers".[S301] Confirmed
TurquoiseFounded by banks; LSEG keeps a user minority (15.8%).[S321, S358, S300] Reported history
TradewebBefore its IPO a group of dealer banks "collectively held a 46% ownership interest".[S320] Reported, search snippet

The bargain for the banks is: use LSEG's infrastructure, but keep a seat and a share. For LSEG, the bargain buys loyalty and volume, at a price. Inferred

Mechanism 6: venues create data, and data is what LSEG sells most

LSEG's investor deck has a page called "Our integrated offering creates more value" with four panels: "Creating our own data flywheel", "Fully integrated workflow", "End-to-end offering" and "Integrated enterprise offering" [S303]. A flywheel here means a loop where each part speeds up the next: trading creates prices, prices become data and indices, and data products bring customers back to trade.

The concrete evidence:

  • Turquoise: "All data generated from the trading systems operated by Turquoise is collated and developed before being distributed via vendors or directly to end-users" [S358].
  • FTSE Russell has switched "the price source for a number of our indices to Tradeweb" [S300], and the deck lists fixed income indices "sourced from Tradeweb" [S303].
  • LSEG says "~98% of group revenues derived from proprietary data, IP and market infrastructure" [S303].

Open access helps the flywheel: the more venues clear at LCH, the more LCH data exists to sell into Workspace. Inferred

Mechanism 7: the Refinitiv logic

The 2021 Refinitiv deal brought in FXall and FX Matching, the Workspace desktop, real-time data, and the majority stake in Tradeweb [S320, S300]. LSEG's stated pitch: "The combination of our trade lifecycle and data value chains is unmatched. We increasingly combine the two to develop differentiated products" [S303]. A trade lifecycle is the chain from pre-trade data to execution, clearing, settlement and reporting; a data value chain is the chain from raw prices to cleaned data, analytics and indices. Refinitiv gave LSEG the second chain at scale, to sit beside the first.
