The macro and political backdrop

  • A war involving Iran in H1 2026 caused an energy price shock and "a spike in trading activity across all major asset classes" [S223]. The Bank of England refers to "the energy shock" [S241]. This is the main reason exchange and clearing volumes were so high in H1.
  • New Prime Minister and Chancellor. Andy Burnham became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 [S242] Confirmed. John Healey replaced Rachel Reeves as Chancellor [S243, S244] Reported. Reeves gave the 14 July Mansion House speech just before she left [S245].
  • Autumn Budget on 28 October 2026 [S243]. The bond market is pressing the new Chancellor: gilt yields near their highest in almost two decades mean higher government borrowing costs.
  • Inflation is sticky. CPI was 3.1% in August and the Bank expects slightly above 4% in early 2027 [S241]. The next rate move could be up, not down.

LSEG in four sentences

  • LSEG had a record first half, and Markets (your division) was the growth engine at +11.9% [S221].
  • The share price is still far below its February 2025 peak because investors fear AI tools will undercut its data business; it fell 12.8% in one day on 3 February 2026 [S90, S224].
  • The activist hedge fund Elliott arrived in February and LSEG has since run record buybacks: £2.1bn in H1 at an average £88.39, and up to £1.35bn more by February 2027 [S221, S226].
  • Markets is betting on "always on" and "digital": LSE 24, tokenised shares, the digital gilt and the Private Securities Market [S221, S227, S228, S246].
Don't say this

"Rachel Reeves is the Chancellor." She was replaced in July 2026 [S244]. The Chancellor delivering the 28 October Budget is John Healey.

Source uncertain: the share price

Two share-price figures sit in the research. WS2 has about 8,216p intraday on 5 October 2026 from Yahoo Finance daily data, with a close of 8,090p on 2 October [S90]. WS5 has "about 8,090p" from a MarketBeat search snippet [S258], which is low confidence. They are consistent (one is Friday's close, the other Monday's intraday), but neither was checked live. The results-day fall also differs: Reuters reported a 3.1% fall during the day [S223], while the daily close was down 6.4% [S90]. Check the live price on the morning of any interview and quote it as "around".

MK1074KMLSEG group and its share price

1. Record half, guidance raised, but the shares fell

LSEG H1 2026 Interim Results and Interim Report, 30 Jul 2026 [S220, S221]; Reuters via Global Banking & Finance Review, 30 Jul 2026 [S223] Confirmed

What happened. LSEG's income for January to June 2026 was £4,799m, up 8.4% on an organic basis (stripping out currency moves and acquisitions). Its adjusted EBITDA margin, the share of income left after running costs, rose to 52.7% from 49.5%. Adjusted earnings per share rose 17.2% to 244.9p and the interim dividend rose 17% to 55.0p [S221]. All four divisions grew: Data & Analytics +5.1%, FTSE Russell +9.1%, Risk Intelligence +9.7%, Markets +11.9% [S221]. LSEG raised full-year growth guidance to 7.0% to 7.5%. Yet the shares fell, because analysts had expected about 7.8% [S223]. Citi's Andrew Lowe wrote "Guidance may disappoint"; RBC's Ben Bathurst said AI vulnerabilities had been "overblown" [S223].

Two details that matter for Markets. First, LSEG agreed in July to buy up to 1.05% more of LCH Group for €70m, taking its stake above 95% [S221]. Second, LSEG cut the share of SwapClear surplus revenue paid to its founding banks from about 30% to 15% for 2025 and 10% from 2026 to 2045. That lifted the margin, but LSEG warns the year-on-year uplift "will largely reverse in Q4 2026" because of when the 2025 benefit was booked [S221].

Why it matters to LSEG. The results show the business is growing faster than at any time in five years, while the share price is still being judged on the AI question rather than on the numbers Inferred. The Q4 margin reversal is a known, flagged item: if it appears in the press after the full-year results, it is not a surprise.

Why it matters to your seat. BI and strategy Risk Your division is the growth engine of the group. But part of that growth came from war-driven volatility, which can fade Inferred. Strategy teams will be asked how much of H1 is repeatable.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Markets grew 11.9% in a very volatile half. How much of that is structural, from new clients and products like Forward First Fixing, the Private Securities Market and Post Trade Solutions, and how much is cyclical volatility? How does the business plan for a calmer second half?" Position you could take: the volume surge is cyclical, but products that save clients time (FFF) or create new markets (PSM) keep growing when volatility falls, so those are the lines to watch.

Figure 32 puts the year on one page. Read it top to bottom: the dots show how crowded July was, and the shaded band shows that the volume surge happened in H1, before the political change.

2. Elliott, the AI sell-off and the buyback

RTE, 26 Feb 2026 [S222]; Reuters via Global Banking & Finance (snippet) [S226]; Resultsense summary of Reuters analysis, 12 Jun 2026 [S224]; Bloomberg headline only [S225] Reported

What happened. In early February 2026 LSEG shares fell almost 13% in one day after Anthropic launched Claude Cowork plug-ins, which sparked fears that AI tools would let customers bypass LSEG's data products [S224]. The daily close was down 12.8% on 3 February [S90]. On 11 February the activist hedge fund Elliott's stake became public [S223]. An activist investor buys a stake and then publicly pushes management to change strategy. Elliott asked for a portfolio review and a £5bn buyback [S226]. On 26 February LSEG announced a £3bn buyback [S222]. By 12 June the shares were up 27% from the Elliott news but still 23% below the 2025 peak, and 90% of analysts rated LSEG a buy [S224]. BofA's Hubert Lam: "They are part of the AI ecosystem rather than competing against it" [S224]. On 1 December 2026 Amit Zavery, President of ServiceNow, joins the board to support the "LSEG Everywhere" AI strategy [S259] Reported.

Why it matters to LSEG. The company has to prove it is an AI winner, not an AI loser, and pay cash back to shareholders while it does so. Elliott sees the roughly 51% Tradeweb stake as a possible source of cash [S226]; LSEG says it has no plans for asset sales Reported, snippet.

Why it matters to your seat. BI and strategy Markets research Shareholder analysis is in the JD. Elliott is a live case study of who owns a listed company and how they apply pressure.

Source uncertain: the size of Elliott's ask

Reuters (via S226) reports a £5bn buyback ask; RTE wrote "$5 billion" [S222]. The Bloomberg article is paywalled and was not read [S225]. Say "a buyback of around five billion" and do not commit to a currency.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Elliott argued the group is worth more in pieces. From the Markets side, what would be lost if the Tradeweb stake were sold?" Both sides: keeping Tradeweb gives LSEG data, Workspace integration of Tradeweb dealer pricing [S221] and the biggest line in Markets; selling would raise cash and might shrink the "conglomerate discount" investors apply to mixed groups. Suggested position: keep it, because Tradeweb is the largest single line in your division and its data feeds the rest of the group Inferred.

MK1075KMMarkets division momentum

Figure 33 (after the LCH story) shows where the 11.9% came from. Every line grew, but clearing and Tradeweb grew fastest. Notice that volumes (panel B) grew far faster than revenue (panel A). That gap is normal: big clients get volume discounts, and fees are not charged per dollar of notional Inferred.

3. LCH: record clearing, with EMIR 3 in the background

LSEG Interim Report H1 2026 [S221] Confirmed; EMIR 3 commentary from Eurex, J.P. Morgan and others [S257] Reported

What happened. A clearing house (CCP) stands in the middle of a trade so that if one side goes bust, the other still gets paid. LCH's SwapClear cleared US$1,165 trillion of interest rate swap notional in H1, up 29.4%. Client trades rose 23.8% to 3.283m. ForexClear (FX clearing) cleared US$33.3 trillion, up 45.2%, with 41 members. OTC Derivatives revenue rose 13.6%. LSEG added more than 80 Post Trade Solutions customers and launched TradeAgent with 11 customers live [S221].

The policy threat. Under the EU's EMIR 3 rules, since 25 June 2025 large EU firms must hold an "active account" at an EU clearing house (in practice Eurex) for euro and zloty interest rate derivatives and clear a representative number of trades there. The first reports were due by 31 July 2026. Roughly 80% of euro interest rate derivatives are cleared outside the EU, mainly at LCH; Eurex has about 20% [S257].

Source uncertain

The 80% / 20% split comes from search snippets and partly from Eurex, LCH's competitor, which has an interest in the number [S257]. Use it as "roughly four-fifths" and attribute it.

Why it matters to LSEG. SwapClear is a crown jewel. Any EU rule that forces business to Frankfurt is a strategic risk. So far, volumes are still at records [S221] Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. Risk BI and strategy Risk teams watch margin and member exposures; strategy teams watch whether euro volume is leaking to Eurex.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "With the first active-account reports in, has the requirement moved meaningful euro swap volume to Eurex, or is it mostly a box-ticking exercise?" Suggested position: H1 records suggest the threat is slow-moving; the bigger date is the end of EU equivalence for UK CCPs on 30 June 2028 [S160].

4. LSEG FX: Forward First Fixing records and Euromoney wins

LSEG FX update, 19 May 2026 [S238]; LSEG FX updates page [S239]; Interim Report [S221] Confirmed; FX Markets snippet [S240] Reported

What happened. A "fixing" is a benchmark exchange rate set at a fixed time, such as the WM/Reuters 4pm London fix, which LSEG owns [S221]. Asset managers often must trade at the fix. Forward First Fixing (FFF) on FXall lets them pre-arrange the forward part of those trades electronically, hours ahead. FFF passed US$1.5tn of cumulative volume, with a US$82bn daily peak on 31 March 2026, 30+ asset manager and corporate clients and 18 partner banks. LSEG is waiving FFF brokerage fees for the rest of 2026, and cites a 90%+ cut in manual processing for its largest client [S238]. Q2 2026 was another record quarter at over US$330bn [S221]. Across LSEG FX, average daily volume was US$561bn in H1 (+5.8%) and FX revenue £145m (+7.6%). US Streaming FX Spot ran its first trades on AWS Outposts with about 70% lower latency [S221]. LSEG won Euromoney 2026 World's Best FX Venue and Best Venue for FX Spot, did the first Deposits trade on FXall and integrated LoopFX [S239]. A "Split Risk" credit-intermediated forwards service is in preparation [S240].

Why it matters to LSEG. FX revenue grew slower than the rest of Markets. Products that remove a manual job for a client are how FX wins share without relying on volatility Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. FX customers The JD's first bullet is "Solve problems for our FX customers". FFF is the best example in this pack of exactly that: a client pain point (manual processing), a product, and a measured result.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "At what point does adoption justify switching FFF fees on, and how would you avoid losing clients when you do?" Both sides: waiving fees speeds adoption and builds a habit; but every month free makes it harder to charge later. Suggested position: switch on fees in tiers once the largest clients depend on the workflow, and lead with the operational savings rather than the price.

5. Tradeweb Q2 2026: record volumes, AI and prediction markets

Tradeweb results release, Business Wire via Nasdaq.com, 30 Jul 2026 [S237] Confirmed

What happened. Tradeweb is an electronic marketplace where large investors trade bonds, swaps and similar products. LSEG owns about 51% of it [S226]. Q2 revenue was US$558.9m (+9.0%) and average daily volume US$3.0 trillion (+18.2%), with records in rates futures, US high-yield credit, convertibles, swaps, options and repo. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 54.4%. CEO Billy Hult highlighted Tradeweb AiEX adoption, TARA (an AI credit research assistant), European credit portfolio trading and a deeper partnership with Kalshi, a prediction-markets firm [S237]; Tradeweb also took a minority stake in Kalshi [S221]. A snippet reports August ADV of US$2.8tn (+13.7%) Reported, snippet.

Why it matters to LSEG. Tradeweb drives the largest single line in Markets (£864m in H1) [S221], and it is the asset Elliott points to [S226].

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research BI and strategy Debt markets research and competitor tracking both run through Tradeweb data.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Is owning 51% of a separately listed Tradeweb a strategic advantage, through Workspace integration and data, or a valuation discount the market will keep pushing on?" Suggested position: an advantage today because it is growing faster than the group; the debate becomes real only if growth slows.

6. LSE 24: a new 24-hours-a-day, five-days-a-week venue

LSEG press release, 21 Jul 2026 [S227]; Interim Report [S221] Confirmed

What happened. London Stock Exchange will launch LSE 24, a separate trading venue running 17:00 to 07:50, Monday to Friday, with a 30-minute pause from 18:30 to 19:00. Client testing is due by the end of 2026. Exchange Traded Products (funds that trade like shares) come first in H1 2027, then equities, subject to regulatory approval. The Main Market keeps its 08:00 to 16:30 hours. LSEG says the venue supports "digital, algorithmic and agentic trading" [S227, S221]. Julia Hoggett, CEO of LSE plc: "LSE 24 will help support deeper liquidity, greater efficiency and broader participation in our markets" [S227].

Why it matters to LSEG. It captures Asian and US investor hours and gives tokenised products a home (Story 11). The risks are thin overnight liquidity and wider spreads, the gap between buy and sell prices Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. BI and strategy Risk The JD says interns "assist the product lifecycle". A venue going from announcement to client testing to launch during your internship is exactly that, and a new venue needs new risk monitoring.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "What would you measure in the first six months to decide whether LSE 24 is working: share of ETP volume traded overnight, number of participants, spread quality, or new international clients?" Suggested position: participants and spreads first, because volume follows only if trading costs overnight are acceptable.

MK1076KMLondon listings and PISCES

7. Airtel Money prices London's biggest IPO in years

Airtel Africa RNS via Investegate, 1 Oct 2026 [S232] Confirmed; Reuters, 23 Sep 2026 [S231]; PitchBook via Yahoo, 28 Sep 2026 [S230] Reported

What happened. An IPO (initial public offering) is when a company first sells shares to the public on a stock exchange. Airtel Money, the mobile-money arm of London-listed Airtel Africa, set its IPO price at £1.96 a share, valuing it at £5.3bn (about US$7.0bn). Existing shareholders sell 270m shares plus up to 27m over-allotment shares (extra shares the banks can sell if demand is strong). It joins the Main Market with admission expected on 14 October 2026, with about 16.5% to 17.5% of shares in public hands [S232]. The company raises no new money: this is a "secondary" sale by existing investors [S231]. Reuters said it could be London's largest IPO since 2021 at about US$800m [S231]. Early valuation talk was US$8bn to 9bn [S230, S231], so it priced below that Inferred. CEO Ian Ferrao: "We believe in London and I think it's going to be a good home for us" [S231].

Why it matters to LSEG. London has had more companies leave than join for years [S230]. A large African fintech choosing London is a proof point for the 2024 listing rule reforms and the stamp duty holiday on new listings Inferred. The exchange earns admission fees, annual fees and trading revenue; FTSE Russell may add the shares to UK indices, which creates index-fund demand Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research This is "shareholder and geographic analysis" in real life: who the early investors were (TPG, Mastercard, QIA [S231]) and why an Africa-focused issuer picked London.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Airtel Money priced below its early talk. Is the bigger risk for London's IPO recovery valuation, where issuers feel New York pays more, or supply, where private equity owners use continuation funds instead of IPOs?" Suggested position: supply, because PitchBook names several big names that delayed or chose other routes (Story 8), and price can be fixed by more deals but supply cannot be forced.

8. The UK IPO market is recovering, slowly

EY, 8 Jul 2026 [S229] Confirmed; PitchBook via Yahoo Finance, 28 Sep 2026 [S230] Reported

What happened. In H1 2026 there were 7 UK IPOs (3 Main Market, 4 AIM, the junior market) raising £577m, up 215% on H1 2025's £183m. Q2 alone had 5 listings raising £564m. Q1 was hit by the Middle East conflict and AI and tech valuation resets [S229]. PitchBook notes AS Watson, Loveholidays and Visma all pushed back London IPO plans, and the RAC chose a continuation vehicle instead [S230]. EY's Scott McCubbin: "the focus is shifting from 'if' to 'when'" [S229].

Policy support now in force. The new prospectus regime (POATRs) has applied since 19 January 2026, with simpler debt disclosure and "Access Bonds" for retail investors [S254]. Companies listing from 27 November 2025 get a three-year stamp duty (SDRT) holiday [S255]. FTSE Russell cut the minimum free float for non-UK companies from 25% to 10% from June 2026 [S253].

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research BI and strategy Debt listings sit in the same team. The POATRs changes to debt disclosure and retail "Access Bonds" are directly relevant to the debt listings work in the JD Inferred.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Proceeds are up from a very low base. Which leading indicator best separates a genuine recovery from a one-off: intention-to-float announcements, pricing versus the range, or how shares trade after listing?" Suggested position: post-IPO performance, because it decides whether the next issuer's investors come back.

9. PISCES gets real trades: Wayve's US$85m auction

Crowdfund Insider, 13 Jul 2026 [S235] Reported; Interim Report [S221] Confirmed; first auction [S236]

What happened. PISCES is a new UK framework that lets private (unlisted) companies hold occasional auctions for their shares: a halfway house between private and public. LSE runs it as the Private Securities Market (PSM). The first auction, for a Tradable Private Equity company holding shares in Oxford Science Enterprises, was announced on 20 February with its first trading event on 25 March 2026 [S236]. In July UK self-driving AI company Wayve ran a US$85m auction so employees could sell vested shares [S235]. LSEG says the PSM "successfully hosted its first transactions, with an encouraging pipeline building" [S221].

Why it matters to LSEG. It builds relationships with fast-growing private companies before they are ready to IPO, a possible future listing pipeline Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research BI and strategy Shareholder analysis for private companies, and measuring whether a new product is working.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Could PISCES delay IPOs, because companies get employee liquidity without listing? How would you measure whether it feeds or cannibalises the Main Market?" Suggested position: it can do both; track how many PSM companies later list, and how long after.

MK1077KMDigital and tokenisation

10. Mansion House and the digital gilt: HSBC and LSEG link up

Mondo Visione (speech text), 14 and 15 Jul 2026 [S245]; Ledger Insights, Jul 2026 [S246]; Interim Report [S221] Confirmed

What happened. Rachel Reeves' last Mansion House speech covered ISA and advice reform, pensions investing an extra £10bn in private markets, stablecoins, tokenised deposits, and the UK becoming the first G7 country to issue a digital sovereign bond "by early next year" [S245]. A depository is where ownership of securities is recorded; a digital one records it on a distributed ledger, allowing near-instant settlement. On 13 July HSBC Orion became the first firm approved to go live as a Digital Securities Depository in the Bank of England's Digital Securities Sandbox. HSBC and LSEG signed an MoU (memorandum of understanding) for a link: HSBC Orion as the issuer-side depository, LSEG's depository as the investor-side one. The digital gilt, called DIGIT, is due by Q1 2027 [S246, S221].

Why it matters to LSEG. It puts LSEG in the plumbing of tokenised government debt, alongside its Digital Markets Infrastructure (DMI) and the new Digital Settlement House (DiSH) [S221].

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research BI and strategy Debt listings and digital markets research meet here.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Why do you think LSEG chose to be the investor-side depository rather than compete to be the issuer-side one for DIGIT?" Suggested position (Inferred): the investor side is where LSEG's existing client relationships are, and it keeps LSEG in the flow of every future digital issue, not just one.

11. London Stock Exchange launches tokenised equity structures, with Payward

LSEG press release, 1 Sep 2026 [S228] Confirmed

What happened. A token is a digital record of ownership held on a blockchain. A tokenised share represents a real share but can move between digital wallets and potentially trade around the clock. LSE is launching UK tokenised equity structures, including xStocks (tokens backed one-for-one by listed shares). It intends to list xStocks and trade them on LSE 24 in 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Payward is the partner for connecting regulated infrastructure to digital-native distribution [S228]. Julia Hoggett: tokenisation "must develop in a way that preserves the trust, rights and role of regulated markets" [S228].

Source uncertain

Payward is described in WS5 as the parent of the Kraken crypto exchange, but that comes from general knowledge and was not checked in the research sweep. Say "Payward" and let the interviewer add the rest.

Why it matters to LSEG. It ties three threads together: LSE 24, DMI and the Digital Securities Depository. It is also defensive, because ICE (owner of NYSE) and OKX plan a venue for 24/7 tokenised US stocks Reported, snippet Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. BI and strategy Risk New product launches need both a business case and a risk framework.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "How do you protect shareholder rights and market integrity when a tokenised share trades at 3am on a crypto-native channel? Is the regulated venue the moat?" Suggested position: yes; the regulated venue is what makes a token trustworthy, which is exactly Hoggett's line.

MK1078KMPolicy, regulation and the macro picture

12. Bank of England holds at 3.75%; three members vote to hike

Bank of England Monetary Policy Summary, 17 Sep 2026 [S241] Confirmed

What happened. Bank Rate is the Bank of England's base interest rate; it drives mortgage, savings and borrowing costs. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 6-3 to hold at 3.75%. Greene, Mann and Pill wanted 4%. CPI inflation was 3.1% in August and is projected at about 3.75% in Q4 2026 and slightly above 4% in early 2027. The Bank also set out a plan to run its gilt holdings down to zero, unwinding £368bn by the end of 2034, about £46bn a year on average [S241].

Why it matters to LSEG. Rate uncertainty drives hedging (swaps cleared at LCH) and FX trading. LCH also earns Net Treasury Income on cash collateral, which grew 12.6% in H1 [S221]; that income rises and falls with interest rates Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. FX customers Risk Sterling moves on rate expectations, and risk reporting needs this context.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Higher-for-longer rates helped Net Treasury Income at LCH. Is that a revenue line LSEG wants investors to value, given it falls if rates fall?" Suggested position: treat it as useful but cyclical, and judge Markets on fee income.

13. A global bond sell-off squeezes the Budget

London Business News, 25 Sep 2026 [S243] Reported; IG and TechTimes snippets [S244]

What happened. A gilt is a UK government bond. When its yield goes up, the government pays more to borrow. The UK 10-year gilt yield rose to 5.38%, close to the previous week's peak, with yields "climbing towards their highest level in almost two decades". The 30-year US Treasury yield reached 5.444%, the highest since 2004 [S243]. Nigel Green of deVere: "Britain's budget is being written in the bond market right now" [S243].

Source uncertain

Search snippets say rising yields cut the Chancellor's fiscal headroom (spare room under his own borrowing rules) from £23.6bn to roughly £13bn [S244]. These are snippets only. Do not quote the numbers; say "headroom has shrunk".

Why it matters to LSEG. Volatile rates markets increase trading and hedging, which helps Tradeweb and SwapClear. Higher gilt volatility also raises margin calls at clearing houses, a risk issue for LCH Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. Risk FX customers Risk teams monitor exactly these moves; FX client teams see sterling volatility around Budgets.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "If gilt volatility stays high into the Budget, does it show up first in SwapClear sterling volumes or in Tradeweb gilt trading, and how does the Risk team think about margin spikes for clients?" Suggested position: this question shows the "connect the dots" skill the JD asks for: one macro event, two businesses, one risk.

14. The UK bond consolidated tape goes live; T+1 is coming

Etrading Software, WatersTechnology and The TRADE snippets [S248] Reported; UK Accelerated Settlement Taskforce [S247]

What happened. A consolidated tape is one combined feed of trade prices for a product, so investors see the whole market rather than one venue. ETS Connect UK, authorised by the FCA on 20 May 2026, launched the UK bond tape on 22 June 2026, combining post-trade bond data from all UK venues and reporting services [S248]. Separately, the UK moves to T+1 settlement (trades settle the next business day instead of two days later) on 11 October 2027 [S247], with interim milestones on same-day allocations and confirmations by December 2026 Reported, snippet.

Why it matters to LSEG. LSEG is both a data seller and a venue operator. A public tape competes a little with paid data but improves bond transparency, which can attract more trading Inferred. T+1 squeezes post-trade processes at LCH and across venues Inferred.

Why it matters to your seat. Markets research BI and strategy Risk Debt market transparency, and an operational change landing in your graduate year.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "Does the bond tape help or hurt LSEG overall, given it owns venues that contribute data and sells data products?" Suggested position: a small net positive for Markets, because more transparent bond markets trade more, and Tradeweb benefits from that.

MK1079KMPeers and competitors

15. The US moves to 23-hour trading; rivals do deals

WilmerHale client alert, 29 Sep 2026 [S251] Confirmed; Deutsche Börse and Euronext snippets [S249, S250] Reported

What happened. The US Securities and Exchange Commission conditionally approved 23-hours-a-day, five-days-a-week trading on five US exchanges (24X, Cboe EDGX, MEMX, Nasdaq, NYSE Arca). Overnight trading is expected to start on 6 December 2026, with an 8pm to 4am New York time session [S251]. ICE and OKX plan a venue for 24/7 tokenised US stocks Reported, snippet. Among European peers, Deutsche Börse agreed a roughly €5.3bn deal for fund platform Allfunds in January, completing in H1 2027 [S249], and Euronext posted record Q2 revenue of €511.0m (+9.9% like-for-like) and rebranded Athens Exchange as Euronext Athens [S250].

Why it matters to LSEG. Extended hours is now a race. If US shares trade overnight from December, global investors may expect the same from London Inferred. LSE 24 is LSEG's answer.

Why it matters to your seat. BI and strategy Competitor tracking is the heart of business intelligence work.

Your question or opinion

Ask: "With US 23x5 trading from December 2026 and LSE 24 starting with ETPs in H1 2027, does London risk being second, or is starting with ETPs a deliberate lower-risk sequence?" Suggested position: deliberate. ETPs already have market makers who can quote prices overnight, so liquidity is easier to build than for single shares Inferred.

MK1082KMReading list and a 15-minute routine

You do not need a paid subscription to stay current. The reading list in the research compresses to the table below; "Access" is the researcher's best understanding as of 5 October 2026 and some items were not checked.

SourceGood forAccessUse for
LSEG Investor Relations and Media CentreResults, trading statements, financial calendar, launches [S220, S227, S252]FreeAll tracks
LSEG FX updates pageFXall, Matching, FFF, awards [S238, S239]FreeFX customers

londonstockexchange.com: new issues, PSM pagesIPOs, debt listings, PISCESFreeMarkets research

Three reading-list warnings

Treat share prices from aggregator sites as low confidence and check the live price on the day. Many free sites republish Reuters copy with their own "takeaways" added; quote only the Reuters text. Reuters supplies news into LSEG Workspace, so mention that relationship if you quote it in an LSEG interview [S223]. For a paywalled article, quote only the headline and date unless you have read it.

The 15-minute daily routine

Minutes 0 to 5: LSEG itself

Scan LSEG press releases and RNS. On the first working day of each month, add Tradeweb's monthly volumes. Write one line: "What did LSEG announce, and which division?"

Minutes 5 to 10: the market

One Reuters LSEG or exchanges story, then City AM's markets page. Note one number: the gilt yield, sterling, or an IPO price. Ask: "Would this raise or lower volumes at LCH, Tradeweb or FXall?"

Minutes 10 to 15: one specialist

Rotate: Monday The TRADE, Tuesday FX Markets headlines, Wednesday Global Custodian, Thursday Ledger Insights, Friday Bank of England or FCA news. Finish by writing a one-sentence opinion.

Adapted from the draft reading list, which suggests about 20 minutes a day (10 daily, plus specialist sources twice a week and regulators weekly). Event days override the routine: on 22 October (Q3 statement) and 28 October (Budget), spend the 15 minutes on that event alone [S252, S243].

The habit that pays off

Keep a running note of the "one-sentence opinions" from the routine. By the video interview you will have twenty or more, and the strengths-based format rewards candidates who sound like they enjoy following markets, not ones who crammed the night before.

MK1008KM
Part 8

Forming your own view

Eleven live arguments about LSEG, each with both sides in numbers, the signpost that would change your mind, and a position you can defend in a minute.

Interviewers at LSEG are not testing whether you can recite the annual report. The JD asks for people who can "connect the dots and think strategically" and "analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions" (JD). The fastest way to show both is to hold a view on a live question, back it with one number, and name the risk to your own view. This Part gives you eleven such questions, each with the bull case (good for LSEG), the bear case (bad for LSEG), a signpost to watch and a suggested position in a purple Your opinion goes here box. Change the suggestions if the evidence persuades you: an opinion you argued yourself into sounds different from one you memorised.

MK1083KMThe argument map: where to spend your preparation

Not every argument deserves equal effort. Figure 34 places the eleven arguments on two axes: how much the question matters to LSEG's value and strategy, and how settled the evidence is today. Top-left (big and open) is where a reasoned opinion earns most credit; top-right (big and settled) is where you need the facts cold.

MK1084KMHow to form and defend a view in 60 seconds

Key term

Bull case / bear case: the optimistic and pessimistic arguments about a company or decision. Analysts use the words for any two-sided debate, not just share prices. Signpost: a specific, dated piece of evidence that would tell you which side is winning. Naming one is what separates an opinion from a guess.

Every answer in this Part follows the same five-step shape. Learn the shape once and you can use it on any question, including ones not in this pack.

StepWhat you sayTimeWorked example (Argument 11)
1. ClaimYour answer in one sentence. Pick a side.5 s"Markets is the part of LSEG I would bet on for the next two years."
2. MechanismWhy it is true: the cause, not an adjective.15 s"Its revenue comes from trading and clearing volumes, and from customers who post margin, so it grows when markets are busy and it is not the part AI tools threaten."
3. NumberOne figure, with its date.10 s"In H1 2026 it grew 11.9%, against 5.1% for Data & Analytics, at a 58.6% margin." [S70]
4. RiskThe best argument against you, said by you first.15 s"Some of that came from volatility around the Iran war, and a 140bp margin boost from the SwapClear deal reverses in Q4." [S223, S70]
5. What you'd watchA dated signpost.10 s"So I'd watch the Q3 statement on 22 October: if Markets still grows high single digits in a calmer quarter, the structural case holds." [S91]
Say this in the interview

"My view is X, because Y. The number that persuades me is Z. The best argument against me is W, so the thing I'd watch is V." Five sentences, under a minute, and every one carries information.

Don't say this

"There are pros and cons on both sides." This is the most common non-answer in assessment centres. It tells the interviewer you read both sides and could not decide. Decide, then show you know what would change your mind.

Two rules make the method work under pressure. First, the mechanism carries the answer. "LSEG is well positioned" is an adjective; "LCH must clear for rival venues on non-discriminatory terms, so banks trust it with their swaps" is a mechanism [S305]. Second, conceding the risk makes you more credible, not less. Interviewers at an infrastructure firm spend their days managing risk. A candidate who names the risk to their own view sounds like a colleague.

MK1085KM1. AI: threat or gift to LSEG's data business?

Why it is live. On 3 February 2026 LSEG shares fell 12.8% in a single day, as worries that large language models "like Anthropic's Claude" could let customers bypass terminals triggered a software sell-off [S90, S88]. From a 12,095p peak (5 Feb 2025) to a 7,170p close (4 Feb 2026), the fall was about 41% [S90] Inferred. LSEG's response is the title of its own results deck: "More valuable in an AI world" [S73]. This is the single biggest debate about the company, and you will almost certainly be asked about it.

Key term

MCP (Model Context Protocol): an open standard for plugging AI tools into data sources. LSEG uses it so that a customer's AI assistant can pull LSEG's licensed data directly [S72]. EBITDA: earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; a rough measure of operating profit. Workflows: the part of Data & Analytics that sells desktop seats on Workspace, LSEG's terminal.

Bull case: AI is a giftBear case: AI is a threat
The data is proprietary. Schwimmer: "90% of our data revenues come from real-time or data that is proprietary" [S71]. An AI model cannot invent a live price or a clearing house's trade record. About 98% of group revenue comes from "proprietary data, IP and market infrastructure" [S73].Redburn's 30%. Rothschild & Co Redburn (18 Jun 2026) said about 30% of EBITDA faces downside in a "realistic base case", concentrated in "workflow and aggregation-driven revenues", and called API and AI consumption "structurally deflationary for parts of the model". Shares fell 7.0% that day [S89, S90] Reported.
Customers are connecting. MCP customers went from over 60 trialling (Feb 2026) to over 150 (Apr) to over 200 engaged (Jul) [S72, S75, S70]. Workspace AI Search has 17,000 active users and Deep Research 7,000 [S70].The desktop is already slow. Workflows grew only 3.1% in 2025 and 2.8% in H1 2026, against 7.5% for Data & Feeds [S72, S70]. If AI agents do the work a human did on a terminal, seat counts are what shrink.
LSEG distributes through the AI firms, not against them. "LSEG Everywhere" partnerships with Anthropic, Databricks, Microsoft, OpenAI, Rogo and Snowflake, then Amazon Quick and Google Gemini [S72, S70]. BofA's Hubert Lam: "They are part of the AI ecosystem rather than competing against it" [S224].Usage is not revenue. UBS's Michael Werner: "It's one thing to have usage, it's another to start charging people" [S88]. Even after record H1 2026 results the shares fell 6.4%, with coverage citing AI monetisation timing [S90, S108].
Customers are signing longer. In Q4 2025 major institutions signed long-term contracts worth £1.9bn, up to 7 years [S72]. Burton-Taylor: market data spend rose 6.5% to a record $49.2bn in 2025 [S188].The industry view is two-sided. Oliver Wyman: enterprise AI threatens about $12bn (9%) of FMI revenue, mostly undifferentiated analytics and data [S185]. Blue Whale's Stephen Yiu: "I don't believe the risk of disruption from AI is minimal" [S88].
A pricing plan exists. H1 2026 set out a framework: subscriptions to license datasets for AI models, a recurring MCP access charge with usage bands, AI Search priced into Workspace up to a cap, Deep Research as a premium add-on [S70].The valuation says "not proven". About 18x forward earnings in June 2026, against about 24x on average since Refinitiv; about 30% below Moody's and 40% below MSCI [S88, S89] Reported.
What would change your mind
  • Q3 trading statement, 22 Oct 2026 [S91]: does Data & Analytics growth hold above 5%, and does Workflows stabilise?
  • FY2026 results (Feb 2027): whether the AI licence and MCP charges show up as named revenue. A useful line: "The test is whether new AI charges show up in subscription growth and gross sales by the full-year results" [S70] Inferred.
  • A warning sign: LSEG says it will retire ASV (annual subscription value, the forward-looking subscription KPI) at the end of 2026 [S70]. That may be sensible, but sceptics will read it as less visibility. Watch what replaces it.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: AI is a net gift to LSEG's proprietary and real-time data, and a real threat to the desktop seat. The two are different businesses inside one division. The Markets division, where this internship sits, is largely outside the blast radius: AI does not replace a clearing house or a regulated venue.

One sentence: "AI makes the data more valuable and the terminal less necessary, so I'd judge LSEG on whether data and feeds growth outruns the slowdown in Workspace seats."

Defend it with: 90% of data revenue is real-time or proprietary [S71]; Workflows at 2.8% growth [S70]. Concede: the pricing is not yet proven, which is why the shares trade at a discount.

MK1086KM2. Should LSEG break up or sell parts?

Why it is live. On 11 February 2026 reports emerged that Elliott, the activist hedge fund, had built a stake [S86]. It reportedly pushed for a portfolio review and a £5bn buyback [S226] (RTÉ wrote "$5 billion", so the currency differs between sources [S222]). LSEG announced a £3bn buyback on 26 February [S72]. Reported reasoning: Elliott reportedly does not want a sale or spin-off of the exchange [S86], but it sees the Tradeweb stake as a possible source of cash [S226] Reported.

Key term

Conglomerate discount: when a group of businesses is valued by the market at less than the sum of what each would be worth on its own, often because investors cannot see each part clearly. Non-controlling interest (minority interest): the share of a subsidiary's profit that belongs to its other shareholders. LSEG consolidates 100% of Tradeweb's revenue but owns only about 50.9% of its economics [S74].

Bull case for selling or splittingBear case: keep it together
The market already prices the parts. Tradeweb has its own Nasdaq listing and a market value of about $22.3bn [S148], against about $52.3bn for all of LSEG [S148] Reported. A stake that visible is easy to turn into cash for buybacks.The joins are where the new revenue is. FXall functionality is largely in Workspace; Tradeweb pricing streams are next [S302]. FTSE Russell now uses Tradeweb as the price source for some indices [S300]. RepoAgent was built by Post Trade Solutions with Tradeweb [S301]. Each of these is harder if Tradeweb is sold.
Value leaks to minorities anyway. Adjusted non-controlling interests were £334m in 2025 and £194m in H1 2026, growth "mainly reflecting strong performance of the Tradeweb business" [S72, S70].Tradeweb is growing fastest. Revenue $2,052m in 2025, up 18.9% [S137]; ADV $3.2trn in H1 2026, up 24.8% [S70]. Selling your fastest-growing asset to fund buybacks is hard to explain to long-term holders Inferred.
A discount exists. About 18x forward earnings vs about 40% more for MSCI [S88]. A simpler group might be easier to value Inferred.The flywheel is the strategy. LSEG's own pitch: "The combination of our trade lifecycle and data value chains is unmatched" [S303]. Trading creates data; Turquoise sells its trade data through vendors [S358].
Management is open to it. Schwimmer: "We're always evaluating our business, and if there's anything that it makes sense to consider, that is something that we're always thinking through" [S223].The buyback already answers the activist. Over £8bn of buybacks since 2022 including those planned to Feb 2027 [S70]. Schwimmer reports "good, constructive dialogue with Elliott" [S223].
What would change your mind
  • Any Elliott letter or stake change after the H1 results. None was verified as of 5 Oct 2026 [S223].
  • Progress on Tradeweb in Workspace: if dealing between Tradeweb and Workspace goes live and shows usage, the "keep" case strengthens [S302].
  • Whether the valuation gap to MSCI and Moody's narrows as AI fears fade. If it closes without a sale, the break-up case weakens.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Keep the Markets businesses together, including Tradeweb. The integration work (Workspace, FTSE Russell pricing, RepoAgent) only pays off with control, and selling the fastest-growing asset to buy back shares swaps growth for a one-off. Accept that LSEG will keep using buybacks to answer the activist.

One sentence: "I'd keep Tradeweb, because the integration into Workspace and FTSE Russell only works with control, and the buyback programme already returns cash without selling the growth."

Concede: if the Workspace integration stalls, the strategic case for holding a minority-leaking stake gets weaker every year.

MK1087KM3. Is London's listings market fixable?

Why it is live. London lost 88 companies from its main market in 2024, the most since 2009 [S145, S200] Reported. The government and FCA have since rewritten the rules. Airtel Money, priced on 1 October 2026, is the biggest test so far [S232]. This matters for the JD's research track ("debt listings, valuations, and shareholder and geographic analysis").

Key term

UKLR: the UK Listing Rules, in force 29 July 2024, which replaced the premium and standard segments with one category for commercial companies [S150]. POATRs: the Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regulations, which replaced the UK prospectus regime on 19 January 2026 [S151]. PISCES: a sandbox that lets private companies' shares trade at occasional auctions; LSE's version is the Private Securities Market (PSM) [S152].

Bull case: it is being fixedBear case: the problem is deeper
The rules changed. The FCA called UKLR "the most significant changes to the UK's listing regime in over 3 decades" [S150]. POATRs in force 19 Jan 2026 [S151]. Three years' stamp duty relief for new listings from 27 Nov 2025 [S182].The base is tiny. London raised £2.1bn from 23 IPOs in 2025 [S142]; Hong Kong raised HK$286.9bn from 119 [S134]. Proceeds percentages look big because the starting point was so low.
Proceeds are rising. 2025 proceeds up 170% on £777.7m in 2024 [S142]; H1 2026: 7 IPOs raising £577m, up 215% on £183m [S229].Big names keep delaying. PitchBook: AS Watson, Loveholidays and Visma pushed back London plans, and the RAC chose a continuation vehicle instead of an IPO [S230] Reported.
Airtel Money chose London. Priced at £1.96, a £5.3bn market value, admission expected 14 Oct 2026 [S232]. Reuters: possibly London's largest IPO since 2021 at about $800m [S231]. CEO: "We believe in London" [S231].But below early talk, and no new money. Early valuation talk was $8bn to $9bn [S230, S231]; it priced at about $7.0bn [S232]. Existing shareholders are selling, so the company raises nothing [S231].
A pipeline before IPO. PSM held its first auction on 25 Mar 2026 [S154]; Wayve ran an $85m employee-share auction [S235]. FTSE Russell cut minimum free float for non-UK companies from 25% to 10% [S253].PISCES might delay IPOs. If staff can sell shares on PSM, a company has less reason to list Inferred. The PISCES sandbox expires on 5 June 2030 unless made permanent [S152].
Savers are being nudged. Cash ISA limit falls to £12,000 from 6 April 2027 [S183]; Mansion House Accord: 10% of default pension funds in private markets by 2030, half in the UK [S181].Listings are a small revenue line. Equities (trading plus listing) was £412m of a £3,467m Markets division in 2025 [S72]. Even a full fix moves group revenue only a little Inferred.
What would change your mind
  • Airtel Money's first weeks of trading from 14 Oct 2026 [S232]. A strong aftermarket helps the next issuer price in London.
  • Autumn Budget, 28 Oct 2026 [S243]: any change to stamp duty or ISAs under the new Chancellor, John Healey.
  • Visma in 2027 [S194]: a roughly €19bn tech company choosing London would be a stronger signal than any rule change.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Fixable, and improving, but not fixed. The rule changes remove excuses; they do not create demand. The underrated story is debt: LSE's International Securities Market and Sustainable Bond Market serve issuers who never make the IPO headlines, which is why the JD names "debt listings" rather than IPOs.

One sentence: "The rules are no longer the problem; demand is, so I'd judge recovery by how the next three large IPOs trade after listing, not by the number of rule changes."

Concede: Airtel Money priced below early talk and raised no new money for the company [S231, S232].

MK1088KM4. Will 24-hour trading matter?

Why it is live. On 21 July 2026 LSEG announced LSE 24, a separate venue running 17:00 to 07:50 London time, Monday to Friday, with a 30-minute pause from 18:30 [S227]. Client testing is due by the end of 2026 and exchange-traded products (ETPs, such as ETFs) launch first in H1 2027, then equities, subject to regulatory approval [S227]. In the US, the SEC has conditionally approved 23-hour trading on five exchanges, expected to start on 6 December 2026 [S251].

Bull case: it mattersBear case: it is a sideshow
Investors are global. LSE 24 captures Asian and US investor hours Inferred. Julia Hoggett: it will "support deeper liquidity, greater efficiency and broader participation" [S227].Overnight liquidity is thin. Few market makers, wide spreads, and the risk that a bad overnight price damages trust in the venue Inferred.
Competitors are moving. US 23x5 from 6 Dec 2026, 8pm to 4am ET session [S251]; ICE and OKX reportedly plan a 24/7 venue for tokenised US stocks [S251] Reported. Not moving would be the risk.London goes second. US exchanges start in December 2026; LSE 24 ETPs arrive in H1 2027 [S251, S227].
It is a platform for new products. LSE intends to list xStocks (tokenised versions of listed shares) and trade them on LSE 24 in 2027 [S228]. LSEG describes LSE 24 as supporting "digital, algorithmic and agentic trading" [S227].Revenue will start small. ETPs first means a narrow product set; the Main Market keeps 08:00 to 16:30 [S227]. UK equities revenue is a minor line in group terms [S72] Inferred.
Mixed trading model. LSE 24 will draw on both order-book and request-for-quote functionality [S196], which suits a market with fewer participants.Operational strain. Longer hours mean longer support, surveillance and risk monitoring Inferred.
What would change your mind
  • How many firms join client testing by end-2026 [S227].
  • US experience after 6 Dec 2026: what share of volume trades overnight, and how wide spreads are [S251].
  • In the first six months: share of LSE-listed ETP volume traded overnight, number of participants, spread quality, new international clients Inferred.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: It matters strategically more than financially. Starting with ETPs is sensible sequencing: lower risk, a natural fit for overseas and retail investors, and a ready home for tokenised products. Early revenue will be small; the cost of not having it, once US markets run overnight, would be larger.

One sentence: "LSE 24 is a defensive option more than a revenue line, and starting with ETPs lets London learn from the US launch before it moves single stocks overnight."

MK1089KM5. Open access: strength or leak?

Why it is live. When LSEG took control of LCH in 2012-13, the competition regulator (the OFT) recorded that open access would go into LCH's articles: services "must be offered on terms that are fair, reasonable, open and non-discriminatory... No exchange will be favoured over any other and LSEG's trading services users will not be favoured over any other exchange's users" [S305]. That neutrality is why the whole market uses LCH. It also means customers can leave, and one did: Euronext moved its cash equity clearing out of LCH SA.

Key term

Open access vs vertical silo: in a vertical silo, an exchange group owns the trading venue and its clearing house and keeps the trades in-house (Deutsche Börse describes its "vertically integrated business model" [S127]). Under open access, the clearing house clears trades from any venue on equal terms, and the venue can use any clearing house.

Bull case: open access is the moatBear case: open access lets value walk out
Neutrality wins the flow. SwapClear has over 90% of cleared interest rate swap notional outstanding (LSEG's figure) [S303]; $1,941trn notional cleared in 2025, up 21.2% [S301]. In GBP SONIA swaps the share was 99.995% in Q1 2026 [S140] Reported.Euronext left. Securities & Reporting revenue fell 3.0% on "the final impact of the termination of the Euronext clearing agreement", and Net Treasury Income fell on "loss of business from Euronext" [S301].
Netting rewards one big pot. The more trades sit at one clearing house, the more they offset and the less margin each member posts Inferred. That is why members stay even when they could leave.The silo is gaining in euros. Eurex's share of EUR swaps rose to 13.5% in Q3 2025 from 8.4% a year earlier; LCH fell to 86.5% from 91.6% [S139] Reported.
It is LSEG's identity. "When other exchange groups focused on vertical integration of trading and clearing, we championed open access" [S300]. LSEG's value "Partnership" is defined as "Our open model is integral to how we do business" [S307].Politics can force a leak. EU EMIR 3 requires some EU firms to hold an "active account" at an EU clearing house from 25 June 2025 [S161]. The EU Commissioner said the aim is "reducing our exposure to UK CCPs" [S160].
Regulators trust neutrality. The EU extended equivalence for UK clearing houses to 30 June 2028 [S160].LSEG venues get no advantage. Under open access LCH must not favour LSEG venues [S305], so LSEG cannot bundle clearing to win trading.
What would change your mind
  • The first EMIR 3 active-account reports, due by 31 July 2026: did euro swap volume actually move to Eurex? [S257] Reported.
  • Clarus quarterly CCP share data for EUR swaps [S139]: a steady climb above 15% for Eurex would be a warning.
  • The EU decision on UK clearing house equivalence before 30 June 2028 [S160].
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: A strength, and the leak is the price of it. Euronext's exit cost a few per cent of one revenue line; neutrality is what earns SwapClear its dominant share. The real threat is political (EMIR 3), not commercial.

One sentence: "Open access is why banks trust LCH with over 90% of cleared swaps; losing Euronext's equity clearing was the price of that trust, and a fair one."

Concede: Eurex's euro share has risen [S139]. If you are asked, say you would watch whether that is policy-driven box-ticking or real migration.

MK1090KM6. Is market data too expensive?

Why it is live. On 29 February 2024 the FCA published its wholesale data market study. It found "users may be paying higher prices for the data they buy than if competition was working more effectively", in markets "concentrated, usually with no more than three key providers" [S309]. It also said "we have not found evidence that firms cannot access the wholesale data they need" and made no referral to the competition authority [S309]. LSEG is one of the three biggest data vendors [S188].

Bull case for LSEG: the price reflects valueBear case: customers overpay
No significant intervention. FCA's Sheldon Mills: "We do not believe the case has been made for significant interventions" [S165].The regulator's own finding. Users "may be paying higher prices... than if competition was working more effectively" [S309]. Operating margins of key providers reportedly rose from about 30% to over 60% over 2017-22 [S165] Reported.
Quality is improving. Customer-raised data quality issues fell 51% while content volumes rose 113% over four years [S301].An advocacy report goes further. Market Structure Partners claimed some exchanges earned an extra £4.93bn from data fees since 2008, citing Turquoise turnover down 61% (2020-22) while data revenue rose 16.5% [S310]. LSEG said the report "contains multiple errors" and retail data "has always been free" [S311].
Customers stay and sign longer. Subscription revenue retention 92.8% [S70]; £1.9bn of long-term contracts signed in Q4 2025 [S72].Cheaper alternatives are arriving. UK bond consolidated tape live 22 Jun 2026 [S155]; equity tape to start "in 2027 or early 2028" [S157].
Tapes share income back. The equity tape provider must share income with data contributors [S157], which may include LSE and Turquoise Inferred.Desktop prices are high. A Bloomberg Terminal was reported at $31,980 a year from 2025 [S323] Reported, low confidence; LSEG competes at the same end.
Source uncertain

The £4.93bn figure comes from a report commissioned by an advocacy firm and reported by The TRADE [S310]; LSEG disputes it [S311]. The 30% to 60% margin figure came from a search snippet of the FCA study, not the full annex [S165]. Quote both as claims, not facts.

What would change your mind
  • Any FCA follow-up on "fair, reasonable and transparent terms" [S165].
  • How the new AI and MCP usage charges are priced [S70]: usage bands could look like fairer pricing, or like a new toll.
  • Take-up of the bond tape and the equity tape procurement in early 2027 [S157].
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Prices are high relative to the cost of producing data, but they reflect what customers are willing to pay for accuracy and trust, and the regulator chose transparency over price control. LSEG's risk is reputational, not regulatory: if customers feel squeezed, they help build alternatives.

One sentence: "The FCA found customers may overpay but chose not to intervene, so the pressure on LSEG will come from customers and consolidated tapes, not from a price cap."

This is a good moment to show the customer view: "If I were an FX client, I'd want to know what I'm paying for that I can't get from the bond tape."

MK1091KM7. Tokenisation: hype or real?

Why it is live. On 1 September 2026 London Stock Exchange announced UK tokenised equity structures, including xStocks (1:1 backed tokenised versions of listed shares), and a partnership with Payward to connect regulated infrastructure to digital-native distribution [S228]. In July, HSBC Orion became the first firm approved to go live as a Digital Securities Depository in the Bank of England's sandbox, with LSEG's depository as the investor-side link for the UK's first digital gilt (DIGIT), due by Q1 2027 [S246, S221].

Key term

Tokenisation: representing a security as a digital token on a shared ledger (a blockchain), so ownership can move and settle almost instantly [S246]. Depository: the record of who owns which securities. Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS): a Bank of England and FCA regime for testing this; it opened on 30 September 2024 [S168].

Bull case: it is realBear case: it is mostly hype
The state is issuing. Rachel Reeves's Mansion House speech (14 Jul 2026) committed to the UK being the first G7 country to issue a digital sovereign bond "by early next year" [S245].The numbers are forecasts. Morgan Stanley and Oliver Wyman's $2.3trn of tokenised real-world assets by 2030 is a base case, mostly collateral mobility [S191] Reported.
LSEG is building plumbing. Digital Markets Infrastructure launched Sept 2025, six fund providers onboarded; Digital Settlement House launched H1 2026; Digital Securities Depository planned H2 2026 [S72, S70].Trust has to be built. The Bank of England frames it cautiously: the technology can be adopted, but trust must be earned [S184]. Hoggett herself: tokenisation "must develop in a way that preserves the trust, rights and role of regulated markets" [S228].
Collateral is the killer use. The Bank of England is consulting on "permitting tokenised assets as eligible collateral for CCPs" [S184]. LCH holds £277bn of member collateral [S74], so faster collateral movement matters directly Inferred.It could disintermediate incumbents. Oliver Wyman: tokenisation could shift 35% of current FMI revenue (about $45bn) to new token-native infrastructure [S185].
Rivals are moving. ICE and OKX reportedly plan 24/7 tokenised US stocks [S251] Reported.Early and small. xStocks trading on LSE 24 is planned for 2027, subject to approval [S228]. No revenue figure exists yet.
What would change your mind
  • DIGIT issuance by Q1 2027 [S246]: does it settle cleanly through the HSBC and LSEG link?
  • The Bank of England's decision on tokenised collateral at clearing houses [S184].
  • Regulatory approval for xStocks on LSE 24 [S228].
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Real in the plumbing, hype at the retail edge. Tokenised gilts and collateral solve a genuine problem (moving collateral fast between clearing houses and banks). Tokenised shares for retail are early. LSEG's sensible bet is to be the regulated venue and depository whichever way it goes, which is exactly the Payward and HSBC structure.

One sentence: "Tokenisation is real where it speeds up collateral and settlement, and LSEG's smart move is to be the regulated infrastructure underneath it rather than compete with crypto venues."

MK1092KM8. Will T+1 hurt or help?

Why it is live. T+1 means a trade settles (cash and securities change hands) one business day after the trade, rather than two. HM Treasury published a draft statutory instrument on 20 November 2025 to make T+1 standard in the UK "from 11 October 2027" [S158]. The EU moves on the same day [S159]. That is during your graduate year if you convert.

Bull case: it helps LSEGBear case: it hurts
Less risk in the system. One day less between trade and settlement means less time for a counterparty to fail, and potentially lower margin needs Inferred.Less time to fix mistakes. Breaks that were fixed on day two now need fixing the same day. Expect more settlement fails at first Inferred.
LSEG sells the fix. RepoAgent (Post Trade Solutions with Tradeweb) "helps banks and clients reduce settlement fails in the repo market" [S301]. Tighter deadlines make that product more valuable Inferred.Operating cost and strain. LCH, venues and their clients must adapt processes and systems [S158] Inferred.
UK and EU align. The same date on both sides avoids cross-border mismatches [S158, S159].Interim deadlines. T+0 allocations and confirmations milestones are reported for December 2026 [S247] Reported, snippet.
Source uncertain

Only the draft statutory instrument is confirmed [S158]. Whether the final instrument has been made in 2026 was not verified. Say "planned for 11 October 2027".

Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: A short-term operational headache and a long-term help. LSEG's Markets businesses make money from volume and from solving post-trade pain, and T+1 creates pain that customers will pay to remove.

One sentence: "T+1 cuts risk but squeezes operations, and LSEG wins if products like RepoAgent help clients hit the tighter deadline."

Best used for the Risk rotation: "Risk teams will want daily data on settlement fails in the months either side of 11 October 2027."

MK1093KM9. Was the £1.2bn SwapClear deal good value?

Why it is live. SwapClear was "founded in collaboration with clearing members" [S304], and its founding banks were entitled to about 30% of SwapClear's "revenue surplus". In October 2025 LSEG paid £1.2bn (£921m in 2025 and £250m in 2026) to cut that share to 15% for 2025 and 10% from 2026 to 2045, while extending the arrangement [S301]. It is the cleanest business case in this Part, and the kind of analysis the BI rotation does.

£1.2bn
Paid to founding banks, 2025-26 [S301]
30% to 10%
Banks' surplus share, 2026 to 2045 [S301]
+100bp
Immediate uplift to group EBITDA margin [S72]
€0.2bn
2024 surplus figure quoted by LSEG [S120]

A back-of-envelope payback (your own working, label it as such)

  1. LSEG says the change improved group EBITDA margin by 100bp [S72]. 1% of £8,986m income is about £90m a year Inferred.
  2. That fits a banks' share of roughly €0.2bn being cut by half for 2025 (30% to 15%) [S120] Inferred.
  3. From 2026 the share falls to 10%, so LSEG keeps about two-thirds of what it used to pay: roughly €0.13bn a year at 2024 size Inferred.
  4. Over 20 years (2026 to 2045) that is about €2.7bn before growth and before discounting, against £1.2bn paid. Payback is roughly a decade at 2024 size, and faster if SwapClear keeps growing (notional cleared +21.2% in 2025 [S301]) Inferred.
Source uncertain

LSEG's wording is "c.30% of SwapClear's revenue surplus which in 2024 amounted to €0.2 billion" [S120]. It can be read as the banks' share being €0.2bn, or the whole surplus being €0.2bn. The 100bp margin uplift is consistent with the first reading, which the working above uses. The arithmetic also mixes pounds and euros. Present it as a method, not a valuation.

Bull case: good valueBear case: expensive
Immediate and lasting. +100bp group margin and 2 to 3% accretive to adjusted EPS in 2025 [S72].Part of the boost is timing. In H1 2026, 140bp of the margin gain came from this change, and LSEG says the year-on-year uplift "will largely reverse in Q4 2026" [S70].
Keeps the banks inside. The banks still get 10% to 2045, so they keep a reason to clear at SwapClear [S301]. The same model was repeated when 11 banks bought 20% of Post Trade Solutions for £170m [S301].Banks keep a cut for 20 years. LSEG paid £1.2bn and still shares 10% of the surplus until 2045 [S301].
Bought at a record. SwapClear cleared a record $1,941trn and 13.4m trades in 2025 [S301, S304]; $1,165trn in H1 2026, +29.4% [S70].Bought ahead of a policy risk. EMIR 3 aims to pull euro clearing to the EU [S161]; equivalence currently ends on 30 June 2028 [S160].
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Good value, if SwapClear keeps its share. LSEG effectively prepaid for a larger slice of a growing business while keeping its banks inside the tent. The risk is political (euro clearing), not commercial.

One sentence: "On my rough maths it pays back in about a decade at 2024 volumes, faster with growth, and it keeps the founding banks committed to 2045; the risk is EU policy on euro clearing."

A strong question to ask the interviewer: "How does the Markets team decide when user ownership is worth the cost?"

MK1094KM10. Bloomberg vs LSEG in FX and data

Why it is live. Bloomberg is the largest market data vendor; LSEG is second [S129, S188], and LSEG itself describes its position as "#2 financial desktops" [S303]. In FX, Bloomberg's FXGO is the platform LSEG's FXall competes with most directly [S149]. Bloomberg is private, so most of its numbers are self-reported.

Key term

D2C and D2D: dealer-to-client platforms, where banks quote prices to asset managers and corporates (FXall, FXGO), and dealer-to-dealer platforms, where banks trade with each other (LSEG's FX Matching) [S303].

Bull case for LSEGBear case: Bloomberg wins
LSEG owns the whole FX workflow. FXall (D2C) with 2,400+ institutional clients and 200+ liquidity providers [S340], FX Matching (D2D), and ForexClear, which cleared $48.1trn notional in 2025, up 31.4% [S301]. Bloomberg has no clearing house or exchange [S120] Inferred.Bloomberg's FX volume claim is bigger. FXGO reported ADV above $830bn in March 2025 [S149] vs LSEG FX $525bn for 2025 [S120]. The measures are not like-for-like (different counting and periods).
Recognised in 2026. Euromoney 2026 World's Best FX Venue and Best Venue for FX Spot [S239].Bloomberg also wins awards. Euromoney named FXGO the world's best multi-dealer platform in 2025 [S149].
Solving specific client pain. Forward First Fixing passed $1.5trn cumulative volume, with a 90%+ cut in manual processing for the largest client [S238]; over $330bn in Q2 2026 alone [S221].Bloomberg bundles. FXGO sits inside the Terminal, so the desktop sells the venue Inferred. LSEG is still moving FXall into Workspace [S302].
Open distribution. LSEG sells data into other people's tools: Microsoft Teams and Excel, Snowflake, Databricks, AI assistants via MCP [S72, S70]. Bloomberg's model is built around its own terminal [S129] Inferred.Workspace is the weak spot. Workflows growth was 2.8% in H1 2026 [S70]; LSEG is the challenger on desktops by its own account [S303].
What would change your mind
  • Adoption of FXall inside Workspace. LSEG says "a large proportion of FXAll's functionality" is now there [S302]; the question is whether clients move.
  • Whether LSEG switches on fees for Forward First Fixing after waiving them for the rest of 2026 [S238].
  • A like-for-like FX venue market share source. None was found in this research.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: LSEG will not out-Terminal Bloomberg, and it should not try. It wins by owning the full FX chain (client venue, interbank venue, clearing, settlement link) and by delivering data wherever customers already work, including inside AI tools.

One sentence: "Bloomberg wins the desk; LSEG can win the workflow, because it runs trading, matching and clearing in FX and sends its data into whatever tool the client uses."

For the FX customer rotation, this is the debate to know well. Do not claim LSEG bundles ForexClear with FXall: open access makes that unlikely and no LSEG statement says so.

MK1095KM11. Is Markets the hidden engine of LSEG?

Why it is live. The public debate about LSEG is about AI and data. But the CEO told analysts in July 2026: "Remember that Markets is 40% of LSEG revenue" [S71]. Markets (London Stock Exchange, Turquoise, Tradeweb, LSEG FX, LCH and Post Trade Solutions) is the division this internship sits in.

40%
Markets share of group revenue, H1 2026 (£1,920m of £4,799m) [S71, S70]
+11.9%
Markets organic growth H1 2026; fastest division [S70]
58.6%
Markets EBITDA margin H1 2026, vs 42.3% for D&A [S70]
~10%
Average annual Markets growth over five years, "no weak years" [S71]
Bull case: it is the engineBear case: it is riding a cycle
Growth, every year. Schwimmer: "There have been strong years and really strong years, but no weak years" [S71]. FY2025 Markets +8.9% vs D&A +5.0% [S72].Volatility did the work. Reuters: "The Iran war prompted a spike in trading activity across all major asset classes" [S223]. LSEG's own FX commentary credits "elevated market volatility" [S221].
Margin now beats data. 58.6% vs 42.3% for D&A in H1 2026 [S70]. Only FTSE Russell (68.1%) is higher [S70].A one-off flatters the margin. 140bp of the H1 group margin gain came from the SwapClear deal and "will largely reverse in Q4 2026" [S70].
Structural products, not just volume. 80+ Post Trade Solutions customers added in H1 2026; FFF records; first PSM transactions [S221].Rate-sensitive income. Net Treasury Income (interest earned on members' cash collateral) was £143m in H1 2026, up 12.6% [S70], and falls if rates fall Inferred.
Least exposed to the AI fear. No AI model replaces a clearing house or a regulated venue [S120] Inferred.Leakage. Tradeweb drives much of the growth, but about half its economics belong to other shareholders [S300]. Redburn also flags Markets cyclicality [S89].
What would change your mind
  • Q3 trading statement, 22 Oct 2026 [S91]: growth in a calmer quarter is the test of "structural vs cyclical".
  • Q4 2026: the size of the margin reversal LSEG has warned about [S70].
  • The Bank of England's rate path (held at 3.75% on 17 Sep 2026, 6-3 vote with three for a rise) [S241], for Net Treasury Income.
Your opinion goes here

Suggested position: Yes, Markets is the engine, and it is under-discussed because the AI debate is louder. Separate it into two parts in your head: a cyclical part (volume, volatility, interest rates) and a structural part (new clients, new products, clearing share). Interview answers that make that split stand out.

One sentence: "Markets is 40% of LSEG and its fastest-growing part, and the useful question is how much of the 11.9% would survive a quiet quarter."

This is the best argument to use in a "Why LSEG?" answer, because it shows you know where the division you are joining sits in the group (see Part 12).

MK1096KMUsing these arguments in each stage

You will not get to deliver eleven opinions. Pick two or three you are most comfortable with, and match them to the stage and the rotation you are asked about.

MK1009KM
Part 9

The interview process, question bank and questions to ask

Four stages, what each one tests, how to prepare in the four weeks before the deadline, 58 questions with answer scaffolds, and ten questions that show you did the reading.

MK1097KMThe process at a glance

LSEG runs the same four-stage process across its business early careers postings: application, an untimed online assessment, a recorded strengths-based video interview, and a half-day virtual assessment centre [S260, S261, S262] Confirmed. The same wording appears on the FTSE Russell Business Graduate Programme and the Business Analyst Summer Internship, so this is a standard process, not something built for this role [S261, S262].

4

Key term

Rolling review: applications are read as they arrive, not all at once after the deadline. LSEG says applications "are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, so we strongly encourage you to complete all required assessments as early as possible" [S266]. In practice, places can fill before 30 October. Applying in the first half of October is safer than applying in the last week Inferred.

MK1098KMStage 1: the application and CV

What is confirmed

  • You apply on Workday with an application and a resume (CV). The posting went live on 21 September 2026 and closes on 30 October 2026, but "may close early" [S260] Confirmed.
  • "Please review all the graduate programme opportunities and make one application." If you apply more than once, LSEG reviews only the first [S260]. Pick this posting deliberately. Do not apply to the Business Analyst internship as a backup.
  • Eligibility: penultimate-year undergraduate due to finish in summer 2028; LSEG says ideal candidates have the right to work in the UK without restrictions for the programme [S260].
  • Hybrid working, 3 days a week in the office at 5 Canada Square [S260].

What the screen is probably looking for

LSEG does not say how CVs are screened. The safest reading is that the screen checks the JD's own list Inferred. The JD asks for a "demonstrable interest in financial markets, which you've built through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities", "a curiosity for data", the ability to "connect the dots and think strategically", "focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt", and collaboration with "strong communication skills" [S260]. It adds one line that matters for every later stage: "You will stand out to us if you can demonstrate and recognise that what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it" [S260].

JD ask [S260]Where to show it on your CVWorked placeholder (replace with your own)
Interest in financial marketsA line under education or a "Interests" line with a specific activity[Society role] "Wrote fortnightly market note for [society], [n] readers; covered [topic]."
Curiosity for dataAny project where you cleaned, counted or charted something[Module or job] "Built a spreadsheet of [x] records to find [y]; result: [z]."
Connect the dotsA bullet that links two things (cause and effect)"Linked [customer complaints] to [rota gaps]; proposed [change]."
Focus, resilience, flexibilityPart-time work alongside study; a setback you recovered from"Worked [n] hours a week during term while achieving [grade]."
