"How" as well as "what"Bullets that say how you did it, not just the outcome"Kept [stakeholder] updated weekly, which [effect]."
Why this matters

Your CV is also the raw material for stages 3 and 4. Every bullet should be a story you can tell for 90 seconds. If a bullet cannot survive "tell me more about that", cut it or rewrite it Inferred.

MK1099KMStage 2: the Immersive Online Assessment

What it is

LSEG calls it an "untimed Immersive Online Assessment" designed "to give you an insight into what it's like to work at LSEG" [S260]. Its hints page describes "an interactive assessment designed to help us understand your strengths, potential and approach to solving real-world challenges", and tells you to visit an "Assessment Preparation Hub" first [S264] Confirmed.

Key term

Immersive assessment: an online test built as a story. You play a new joiner, read emails and data, and answer questions as the day unfolds. There is no separate "maths test" and "verbal test"; the numbers sit inside the story [S289]. Situational judgement test (SJT): a question that gives you a work scenario and asks what you would do, or how you would rank possible actions.

Who probably runs it: Cappfinity

The words "Assessment Preparation Hub" on LSEG's page link to hub.preparationplus.com. That page's HTML title is "Cappfinity Preparation Hub" and its description reads "Powered by Cappfinity" [S264, S265]. So LSEG's partner for this stage is very likely Cappfinity (formerly Capp) Inferred, high confidence. LSEG does not name the vendor in text.

Source uncertain

Three test-prep sellers say LSEG uses SHL timed numerical, verbal and logical tests, and one mentions a telephone interview [S286, S287, S288]. One unverified snippet claims a shift to Aon and SHL [S299]. These do not match LSEG's own 2026 wording (untimed, immersive, video) and may describe older cycles or other roles. The live Cappfinity link is the stronger evidence for the 2027 cycle. Practical answer: prepare mainly for an immersive strengths simulation, with a little timed numerical practice as insurance.

What it probably looks like

This is Cappfinity's general format, from a third-party guide that does not mention LSEG [S289] Reported:

  • One storyline set in a realistic role, with situational "strengths" questions.
  • Numerical and verbal tasks built into the story (for example, read a short data table in an email, then answer a question about it).
  • Sometimes a written or short video task.
  • Sections "often generously timed or untimed".
  • Some questions ask both what you would do and how much you would enjoy doing it.

One Glassdoor snippet from an LSEG graduate candidate describes a "Behavior Assessment with personality, behavior and logic tests without time limit", with mainly behavioural questions that were "very well-crafted" [S291] Reported, anecdote.

How to prepare

Do thisWhy
Use the Cappfinity Preparation Hub linked from LSEG's page before you start [S264].It is the official route and has technical guidance.
Answer as yourself, not as the ideal candidate.Strengths tests compare answers across many items. Faking one profile across a long test is hard and shows as inconsistency Inferred [S289].
Read every email, attachment and table in the scenario.The numbers you need sit inside the story [S289].
Use the untimed format: do it in one quiet sitting with a calculator and paper."Untimed" removes the speed penalty, so accuracy is what counts Inferred.
Rank actions with three filters: the client, the rules, the team.LSEG's values put Integrity first ("We earn trust by acting responsibly") [S271]. The answer that protects clients and follows process usually beats the heroic shortcut Inferred.
Do 2 or 3 short numerical sets (percentages, growth rates, reading tables).Insurance against the SHL claims, and useful for the AC case [S286].
Complete it soon after the invite, within the deadline in the email.Review is first-come, first-served; deadlines come in the invitation [S266, S269].
Don't do this

Do not pick "I would really enjoy this" for every task. A real person dislikes some work. Steady, honest preferences read better than a wall of maximum scores Inferred.

MK1100KMStage 3: the strengths-based video interview

Format, from what candidates report

LSEG confirms the style and themes: strengths-based questions about "your experiences, motivations, strengths and what inspires you about a career at LSEG" [S260, S264] Confirmed. The mechanics come only from anecdotes:

  • About 8 questions, no overall time limit, "unlimited time to prepare", but "only one attempt to record an answer of 1-2 minutes" (Glassdoor, graduate programme) [S291] Reported, anecdote. The count may differ by year or track.
  • The invite tended to arrive about a day after the online assessment; waiting 2 to 3 days with no invite was seen by some as a bad sign (TheStudentRoom, 2026 graduate threads) [S293] Reported, low confidence.
  • Cappfinity describes its own video product as "fully asynchronous", meaning you record alone and someone reviews later [S290]. Whether LSEG uses Cappfinity for the video too is not stated Inferred, medium confidence.
Key term

Strengths-based interview: an interview that asks what you are naturally good at and what gives you energy, not only what you have done. The idea is that people perform best in work that uses their strengths and that they enjoy. Competency interview: the older style, asking for past evidence of set behaviours ("Tell us about a time you..."), usually answered with STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

How Capp-style assessors are thought to score energy and authenticity

Neither LSEG nor Cappfinity publishes a scoring rubric in the sources read. What follows is inferred from Cappfinity's own format material and its example prompts ("How do you feel when you are looking at data?", "How do you deal with setbacks?", "How do you stay motivated?") [S289, S290] Inferred.

SignalWhat it probably looks like on videoHow to produce it honestly
EnergyPace picks up, detail increases, you use "I" and present tense when describing the thing you enjoy.Only claim energisers you can talk about for two minutes without notes. Detail is the tell, not volume.
AuthenticityAnswers sound remembered, not recited. Small specifics (a date, a number, what someone said).Prepare bullet prompts, never scripts. Record practice answers and delete any that sound read.
Self-awarenessYou can name what drains you and how you manage it.Pick a real drain that is not central to the role (see C2).
ConsistencyYour strengths match across the online test, the video and the AC.Decide your 3 or 4 core strengths now and let all stories point to them.
Motivation for LSEGA specific reason, tied to one business or fact, not "a global leader".One fact per answer is enough: for example Markets income £1,920m in H1 2026, up 11.9% [S285].

Recording checklist

  • Test camera, microphone and connection the day before.
  • Camera at eye level, face lit from the front, plain background.
  • Use the untimed preparation window to jot 3 bullet prompts, then look at the camera, not the notes.
  • Aim for 90 seconds. The reported window is 1 to 2 minutes [S291].
  • Answer first, in one sentence. Then one example. Then the link to LSEG.
  • If you stumble, keep going. A small recovery looks human; you only get one take [S291].
  • Smile where it is natural, especially when talking about what you enjoy.
  • Do all questions in one sitting so your energy stays even.
Say this in the interview

For "What inspires you about a career at LSEG?" (LSEG's own theme [S264]): "I get most energy from understanding how a system works end to end. LSEG is one of the few places where you can see a trade from the venue, through clearing at LCH, to reporting, inside one group. The internship lets me see that from the inside." Then give your own example of enjoying a system or process.

MK1101KMStage 4: the virtual assessment centre

Confirmed: half a day, virtual, "several different types of exercises", details sent with the invite, and "a chance to get to know LSEG, meet our people and discover more about the opportunity" [S260, S264] Confirmed. Business Management does not list a technical test, unlike the analyst or engineering tracks [S260].

Likely exerciseWhat has been reportedWhat it testsHow to prepare
Group exercise"Small teams to solve a business case or scenario" [S286]. Tech-track anecdote: 4 candidates, about 30 min reading a pack, then about 30 min discussion with 2 assessors listening; each person given a factor (ESG, economic, political, technological) to argue; assessors watched group behaviour more than content [S292].Listening, building on others, time-keeping, reaching a decision together.Practise a 30-minute group discussion with friends. Assign one person to watch only behaviour and give feedback.
Case study"Analyse a business scenario, review data, and propose solutions" [S286]. Tech-track anecdote: 30 minutes to review a long pack about a fictional website [S292].Finding the signal in a lot of material, prioritising, a clear recommendation.Practise reading a 10-page pack in 20 minutes and writing a one-page recommendation: answer first, 3 reasons with numbers, risks, next steps.
InterviewA final interview with "senior managers or team leaders" [S286].Motivation, values, depth on one business, questions you ask.Use the question bank below; pick 2 questions to ask from the list at the end of this Part.
Meet our peopleLSEG says the AC includes a chance to "meet our people" [S264].Probably informal, but treat it as observed Inferred.Have one genuine question about each person's day-to-day work.
Source uncertain

The detailed AC anecdote is from the technology graduate scheme, not the business track, and the dates of the Glassdoor reviews are unknown [S292]. The test-prep description [S286] is generic. Treat the exercise list as likely, not certain, and read the invite email carefully.

Virtual AC habits that help

  • In the group exercise, say other people's names when you build on their points ("Building on Priya's point about cost..."). It shows listening on camera, where body language is hard to read Inferred.
  • Offer to keep time early. It is a real contribution and it is visible Inferred.
  • In the case, state the recommendation in the first 20 seconds of your presentation. A summary without a decision is a common way to lose marks (see H2).
  • Keep a printed one-page fact sheet (H1 2026 Markets numbers, the five businesses, the four values) beside your screen for the interview, but do not read from it.

Why this matters

A notable gap: the London Business Management and Sales Graduate Programme (R0123406) was not on the board on 5 October 2026, while New York's version was [S263]. It may have closed or paused Inferred. That is a hint that LSEG postings can fill and close fast. Apply early.

MK1103KMAfter the internship: the graduate programme

The JD says the internship "has been crafted to simulate our Business Graduate Programme" and that interns play a part "just like they would do as a graduate" [S260]. So the target after the summer is a return offer onto that programme Inferred.

What the Business Graduate Programme looks like

  • 12 months; the current intake starts September 2027 [S268].
  • Two business pathways: Commercial and Business Analyst [S268].
  • An 8-week group project, offsite skills training and AI upskilling [S268].
  • FTSE Russell's version: "a 12-month development journey", global induction, a mid-point offsite called "Ignite", 5 study days; graduates join permanently [S261].

What is known about conversion

  • LSEG won the ISE Best Graduate Development Programme Award 2024 [S270].
  • ISE reported an "8-fold increase in programme participants in one year", a "42% increase in intern conversions in one year" and a "35% increase in offer acceptance rate" [S270]. These are relative changes from 2024, not rates.
  • The actual intern-to-graduate conversion rate and the intake size are not published [S270].
Don't say this

"I know 42% of interns convert." That is wrong: 42% is the rise in conversions in one year, not the share of interns who convert [S270].

MK1106KMHow to use the question bank

The 58 questions below come from the themes LSEG names for each stage, common strengths-style prompts, and the JD's four exposure areas [S260, S264, S289]. LSEG has not published its questions Inferred. Each item has four parts:

  • Testing: what the assessor is really scoring.
  • Structure: a shape for the answer. A scaffold, not a script. In a strengths format, answers that sound learned score worse than answers that sound real [S289] Inferred.
  • Weave in: one LSEG fact you can use if it fits, with its source. One fact per answer is enough.
  • Trap: the common way to lose marks.

MK1107KMQuestions A to B: motivation and Markets

A. Motivation and why LSEG (6)

Q1 (A1). Why LSEG?
Testing whether your interest is specific and real, and whether you see LSEG as more than "the stock exchange". Structure (1) one concrete moment that got you interested in market infrastructure; (2) one thing about LSEG's model you find interesting; (3) what you want to learn in 9 weeks and how it links to your next step. Weave in the Markets Division "combines the Group's flagship trading and clearing businesses" (LSE, Turquoise, LSEG FX, Tradeweb, LCH) with risk, collateral and reporting capabilities [S273]; LCH must clear on "fair, reasonable, open and non-discriminatory" terms, even for rival venues [S305]. Trap talking only about prestige or the building; reciting the purpose statement with no personal link; confusing LSEG with LSE (the university).
Q2 (A2). Why this internship and not an investment bank?
Testing self-awareness, and whether infrastructure is a choice, not a fallback. Structure what draws you to the "plumbing" (venues, clearing, data) over deal-making; one example of you enjoying systems, process or client service; what this internship lets you see (the trade lifecycle end to end). Weave in the JD: interns "help customers across the trade life cycle", across clearing and reporting [S260]. Trap criticising banks; giving "work-life balance" as the main reason.
Q3 (A3). What do you know about the business areas an intern could join?
Testing whether you read the JD and can describe each business in one plain sentence. Structure name the five (LSE, LSEG FX, Tradeweb, Turquoise, LCH) [S260]; one line each; the two that interest you most and why. Weave in H1 2026 Markets income £1,920m, up 11.9% at constant currency [S285]; Markets is about 40% of group revenue [S71]. Trap a list of names with no understanding; a fixed preference so strong you seem inflexible (LSEG places you using what it learns) [S260].
Q4 (A4). What inspires you about a career at LSEG?
Testing energy and motivation; this is LSEG's own wording for the video stage [S264]. Structure one thing that energises you; a short story that shows it; a link to a specific LSEG activity. Weave in LSE 24, a planned venue running 17:00 to 07:50, with ETPs first in H1 2027, subject to approval [S278]; the Private Securities Market's first transactions in H1 2026 [S285]. Trap "fast-paced and dynamic" with nothing behind it.
Q5 (A5). Where do you see yourself after this internship?
Testing whether you are likely to convert and stay. Structure you hope to return on the Business Graduate Programme; show you know its shape; stay open on the exact area. Weave in 12 months, Commercial and Business Analyst pathways, an 8-week group project [S268]; "Ignite" mid-point offsite and 5 study days on the FTSE Russell version [S261]. Trap naming a different employer as your long-term plan.
Q6 (A6). Tell us about yourself.
Testing concise communication and a link to the role. Structure present (degree, one interest), past (two relevant experiences), future (why this role now). 60 to 90 seconds. Weave in the JD's "demonstrable interest in financial markets ... through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities" [S260]. Trap reading your CV line by line.

B. Why this division: Markets (5)

Q7 (B1). Which of LSE, LSEG FX, Tradeweb, Turquoise or LCH would you most like to join, and why?
Testing specific interest plus flexibility. Structure first choice with a reason tied to a skill; a second choice; say you are open. Weave in (pick one) FX revenue £145m in H1 2026, up 7.6%, with average daily volume $561bn [S285]; ForexClear notional cleared $33,311bn, up 45.2% [S285]; UK equities average daily value traded £6,671m, up 33.5% [S285]. Trap picking a business you cannot describe.
Q8 (B2). The JD mentions solving problems for FX customers. What are an FX client's goals?
Testing client empathy and basic FX. Structure who the clients are (asset managers, corporates, banks); what they want (good price, low cost, reliable execution, a clean audit trail); how a venue helps. Weave in Forward First Fixing did over $330bn in Q2 2026, a record [S285]; LSEG cites a 90%+ cut in manual processing for its largest FFF client [S238]. Trap talking about FX as retail speculation.
Q9 (B3). How would you approach research into debt listings, valuations, and shareholder and geographic analysis?
Testing analytical thinking and knowing what a debt listing is. Structure define the question; pick data sources; describe the analysis; say how you would present it. Weave in the JD's exact words [S260]; Airtel Money's Main Market IPO, priced 1 Oct 2026 at £1.96 a share, about 16.5% to 17.5% in public hands [S232], as a live example of shareholder analysis. Trap overclaiming technical skills.
Q10 (B4). What do risk teams in a market infrastructure business do?
Testing why risk matters at a clearing house or venue. Structure monitor (exposures, margin, operational risk); analyse (data, stress); report and deliver projects. Weave in JD: "monitoring and analysing risks, and interpreting data in readiness for the delivery of risk projects or reporting" [S260]; LSEG runs a "three lines of defence model" [S74]. Trap treating risk management as compliance only.
Q11 (B5). What is the difference between a trading venue and a clearing house, and why might one group own both?
Testing joined-up thinking: the JD asks you to "connect the dots" [S260]. Structure a venue matches buyers and sellers; a clearing house stands between them after the trade; owning both supports end-to-end workflow, but LCH runs on open access. Weave in CEO on the Q1 2026 call: "straight through FXall execution capabilities into ForexClear" [S284]; LCH's open-access rule: "No exchange will be favoured over any other" [S305]. Trap claiming LSEG sells venue and clearing as a bundle (no LSEG statement says so, and open access makes it unlikely) [S305].

MK1108KMQuestions C: strengths

General scaffold for every strengths question: a genuine answer about what you enjoy and do well, then a short real example, then how often you use it [S289, S290] Inferred. Short, honest, specific. These questions have no "right" answer, only consistent and believable ones.

Q12 (C1). What energises you?
Testing real motivators, and whether they fit a fast, client-facing, data-heavy role. Structure name the thing; why; a recent example; how it would show up at LSEG. Weave in the JD's "curiosity for data" and "connect the dots" [S260]. Trap answering what you think they want; "I love challenges" with no detail.
Q13 (C2). What drains your energy?
Testing self-awareness and honesty. Structure a real drain; how you manage it; why it will not stop you doing the job. Weave in nothing from LSEG; this answer is about you. Trap a fake weakness ("perfectionism"); naming something central to the role, such as talking to clients.
Q14 (C3). How do you stay organised when you have lots going on?
Testing planning and focus; the JD asks for "focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt" [S260]. Structure your system; a time it was tested; what you changed afterwards. Weave in story slot 6 (pressure). Trap listing apps with no example.
Q15 (C4). Tell us about a time you learned something new quickly.
Testing learning speed, which you need to get up to speed on market structure in 9 weeks. Structure context; how you learned (sources, people, practice); proof you got it; what you would do differently. Weave in how you taught yourself what a CCP does while preparing for this role (see F1). Trap choosing something trivial.
Q16 (C5). What do you enjoy more: starting a task or finishing it?
Testing natural preferences; no correct answer [S289] Inferred. Structure honest preference; example; how you cover the other side. Weave in the JD's "instant reaction and long-term vision are equally important" [S260], if you want a link. Trap "both equally" with no detail.
Q17 (C6). How do you feel when you are looking at a big set of data?
Testing data curiosity (JD) [S260]; this is close to a Cappfinity example prompt [S289]. Structure honest reaction; what you do first; an example where you found something useful. Weave in story slot 2 (data). Trap claiming expertise in tools you have barely used.
Q18 (C7). When are you at your best in a team?
Testing collaboration and role awareness; LSEG's Partnership value [S271]. Structure your natural role; example; how you adapt when the team needs something else. Weave in Partnership: "We forge long-term relationships; we work together to solve evolving needs" [S307]. Trap always being "the leader".
Q19 (C8). How do you react when plans change at short notice?
Testing resilience and adaptability. Structure first reaction (honest); how you reset; a real example. Weave in "Heightened market volatility and geopolitical uncertainty drove exceptional clearing activity" in Q1 2026, then Q2 moderated [S285]; the JD's "instant reaction and long-term vision" [S260]. Trap claiming you never feel stress.
Q20 (C9). What would your friends say you are naturally good at?
Testing self-insight, and consistency with your other answers. Structure one strength; one example from outside study; one link to the role. Weave in nothing needed. Trap a list of five adjectives.
Q21 (C10). Do you prefer lots of things at once, or one thing in depth?
Testing fit with being "an individual contributor" who also works "as a team" [S260]. Structure preference; example; how you cope with the other mode. Weave in the JD's four exposure areas, which range from fast client work (FX) to deeper research (debt listings) [S260]. Trap an answer that contradicts what you said in Q14.

MK1109KMQuestions D to E: behavioural and commercial

D. Behavioural and competency (6)

Use STAR, but keep the Situation to two sentences. Spend most of the time on what you did and the result. Expect follow-ups in a live interview: "What would you do differently?"

Q22 (D1). Tell us about a time you solved a problem for a customer or user.
Testing client focus; the FX role is customer facing [S260]. Structure the customer's goal; the problem; your action; the result; what you learned. Weave in link to the JD's "maintain relationships with existing customers ... and deal with post sale activity" [S260]. Trap a story where you only escalated.
Q23 (D2). Tell us about a time you used data to change someone's mind.
Testing analysis plus communication. Structure question; data; insight; how you presented it; outcome. Weave in the JD's "analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions" [S260]. Trap no actual numbers.
Q24 (D3). Tell us about a time you worked with someone difficult.
Testing maturity and the Partnership value [S271]. Structure situation; your understanding of their view; what you did; outcome; the relationship after. Weave in nothing needed. Trap blaming the other person.
Q25 (D4). Tell us about a time you failed.
Testing resilience and honesty; the JD says "what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it" [S260]. Structure the failure (own it); what you did next; what changed. Weave in nothing needed. Trap a disguised success.
Q26 (D5). Tell us about a time you improved a process.
Testing fit with "strategic initiatives, and operational improvements" in the JD [S260]. Structure what was inefficient; your idea; how you got buy-in; measurable change. Weave in FFF as LSEG's own example of a process fix for clients (90%+ less manual processing for its largest client) [S238]. Trap an improvement with no evidence.
Q27 (D6). Tell us about a time you met a tight deadline.
Testing prioritisation and calm. Structure the deadline; trade-offs you chose; result; what you would change. Weave in story slot 6. Trap missing the deadline and not owning it.

E. Commercial awareness (7)

Q28 (E1). What is a recent LSEG development that interests you?
Testing real reading beyond the careers page. Structure what happened; why it matters for customers; one risk or open question. Weave in (choose one) LSE 24: announced 21 Jul 2026, client testing by end 2026, ETPs first in H1 2027 [S278]; tokenised equity structures and a Payward partnership, 1 Sep 2026 [S228]; HSBC and LSEG depository link for the DIGIT digital gilt by Q1 2027 [S285, S246]. Trap a story you cannot discuss for two minutes.
Q29 (E2). How does LSEG make money in its Markets business?
Testing the business model. Structure trading fees (equities, FX, fixed income via Tradeweb); clearing fees (LCH); post-trade and reporting services; net treasury income on collateral. Weave in H1 2026: Equities £230m, Fixed Income, Derivatives & Other £864m, FX £145m, OTC Derivatives £355m, Securities & Reporting £124m [S285]. Trap saying LSEG earns money when share prices go up.
Q30 (E3). Why did Markets revenue grow so strongly in early 2026?
Testing linking macro events to the business. Structure volatility drives trading and hedging; more hedging means more clearing; volumes moderated in Q2; separate the cyclical from the structural. Weave in "Heightened market volatility and geopolitical uncertainty drove exceptional clearing activity" [S285]; structural growers: FFF, Post Trade Solutions (80+ customers added in H1), the Private Securities Market [S285]. Trap assuming volatility is always good; it can stress risk systems and clients.
Q31 (E4). What challenges does the London Stock Exchange face?
Testing a balanced view. Structure competition for listings and trading; regulation; LSEG's response (new venues, private markets, digital). Weave in UK IPO proceeds in H1 2026 were £577m from 7 IPOs, up 215% from a low base [S229]; US exchanges plan 23-hour trading from 6 Dec 2026 [S251]; LSE 24 is London's answer [S278]. Trap only negative headlines; made-up IPO numbers.
Q32 (E5). How is AI changing financial market infrastructure?
Testing forward thinking with a sense of risk. Structure data delivered into AI tools; automation of workflows; risks (governance, resilience). Weave in LSE 24 is designed to support "digital, algorithmic and agentic trading" [S227]; the Q1 2026 call mentioned customers accessing data through MCP servers [S284]. Trap hype with no control or risk angle.
Q33 (E6). Who are LSEG's competitors in Markets?
Testing a market map. Structure by business: other exchanges and MTFs for equities; other FX venues; other clearing houses; electronic bond platforms. Weave in Deutsche Börse ties Eurex trading to Eurex Clearing, a "vertical" model, while LSEG chose open access [S305, S300]; EU rules require some euro swap clearing at an EU CCP, in practice Eurex [S257]; US exchanges moving to 23x5 [S251]. Name only competitors you have checked yourself. Trap inventing market shares.
Q34 (E7). What is tokenisation and why does LSEG care?
Testing curiosity and plain explanation. Structure define it simply (a digital record of ownership on a shared ledger); one LSEG example; one risk. Weave in LSEG's Digital Settlement House (DiSH), Digital Securities Depository, six fund providers on Digital Markets Infrastructure [S285]; Julia Hoggett: tokenisation "must develop in a way that preserves the trust, rights and role of regulated markets" [S228]. Trap crypto speculation talk.

MK1110KMQuestions F to G: markets basics and data

F. Markets knowledge for beginners (8)

Practise each of these to "explain it to a friend in 30 seconds" level. Plain words beat jargon.

Q35 (F1). What does a central counterparty (CCP) do?
Testing the core LCH idea. Structure after a trade, the CCP becomes buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer; it collects margin (collateral); if a member defaults it uses that member's margin and default fund first, then its own funds, then other members' default fund [S93]. Weave in LCH says it has "managed 9 member defaults and, in all cases, losses were within the initial margin held" [S351]; Daniel Maguire led the unwinding of Lehman's LCH-cleared bond and repo portfolio from 1 Sep 2008 [S273]. Trap saying a CCP removes all risk.
Q36 (F2). What is a spot FX trade versus a forward?
Testing basics for the FX desk. Structure an exchange of currencies; spot settles quickly (typically two business days for most pairs); a forward settles on a future date at a rate agreed today; used for hedging. Weave in LSEG FX average daily volume $561bn in H1 2026 [S285]. Trap mixing up FX venues and banks.
Q37 (F3). What does it mean to list a bond on the London Stock Exchange?
Testing the "debt listings" area in the JD [S260]. Structure the issuer admits debt securities to a market; gains visibility and investor access; must meet disclosure rules; investors gain transparency. Weave in LSE delivers "international equity, fixed income, exchange-traded funds, and investment vehicles" [S278]; a new UK prospectus regime applies from 19 Jan 2026, including "Access Bonds" for retail [S254]. Trap confusing listing with trading volume.
Q38 (F4). What is the difference between an exchange and an MTF like Turquoise?
Testing market structure. Structure both are regulated venues where many buyers and sellers meet; an exchange also runs listings; an MTF (multilateral trading facility) trades shares listed elsewhere; Turquoise is pan-European. Weave in LSEG calls Turquoise a "pan-European trading venue" [S277]; LSEG owns 84.2% [S300]. Trap saying Turquoise lists companies.
Q39 (F5). What is an interest rate swap and why clear it?
Testing SwapClear basics. Structure two parties swap fixed for floating interest payments; used to hedge rate risk; clearing cuts bilateral risk and is required for many trades. Weave in SwapClear notional cleared $1,165trn in H1 2026, up 29.4% [S285]. Trap confusing notional (the reference amount) with money at risk.
Q40 (F6). What does Tradeweb do?
Testing knowing the biggest Markets revenue line. Structure electronic marketplaces for rates, credit, equities and money markets; moves bond trading from phone to screen. Weave in Tradeweb average daily volume $3.2trn in H1 2026, up 24.8% [S285]; LSEG is the majority owner, about 50.9% economic interest [S74], and Tradeweb is separately listed [S300]. Trap calling Tradeweb wholly owned.
Q41 (F7). What is an ETP, and why would LSE 24 start with them?
Testing whether you read the LSE 24 release. Structure exchange-traded products give exposure to an index or asset; investors in other time zones want them; London is a big ETP centre. Weave in the release calls ETPs "a natural starting point" given London's position as "a leading international ETP hub" [S278]. Trap confusing ETPs with mutual funds.
Q42 (F8). What is the trade lifecycle?
Testing the JD's own framing. Structure pre-trade (data, price); execution (venue); clearing (CCP); settlement; reporting. Map each to an LSEG business: LSE, Turquoise, Tradeweb or FXall to trade, LCH to clear, regulatory reporting after [S273, S284]. Weave in JD: "across the trade life cycle, ensuring compliance and efficiency in clearing and reporting obligations" [S260]. Trap skipping clearing or reporting.

G. Data and analysis (4)

Q43 (G1). Here is a table of monthly volumes by venue. What stands out?
Testing numeracy and picking the signal; likely in the online test or AC case Inferred [S264, S289]. Structure the biggest change; a possible cause; the extra data you would want; one recommendation. Weave in practise on real figures: ForexClear +45.2% against FX revenue +7.6% in H1 2026 [S285]. Why might clearing volume grow faster than venue revenue? Trap describing every number.
Q44 (G2). How would you measure whether a new product launch is working?
Testing metrics thinking. Structure the objective; leading and lagging measures (customers live, volume, revenue, retention); a review point. Weave in TradeAgent launched with 11 customers live; Post Trade Solutions added 80+ customers in H1 2026 [S285]; FFF fees are waived for the rest of 2026 [S238], so revenue is the wrong first measure there. Trap revenue only.
Q45 (G3). Which tools have you used to analyse data?
Testing honesty and level. Structure tool; what you built; what it showed; what you want to learn next. Weave in the JD asks for "a curiosity for data", not a coding level [S260]. Trap overclaiming Python or SQL.
Q46 (G4). Estimate how many trades a day an equity venue might handle.
Testing structured estimation (possible, not reported). Structure state assumptions; build up step by step; sense-check; say what data you would use to verify. Weave in you could anchor on UK equities average daily value traded of £6,671m in H1 2026 [S285], then assume an average trade size and say it is an assumption. Trap refusing to estimate; presenting guesses as facts.

MK1111KMQuestions H to J: AC, values and ethics

H. Case and assessment centre style (4)

Q47 (H1). Group exercise: rank these factors (economic, political, ESG, technological) by impact on a business.
Testing collaboration more than content [S292] Reported. Structure agree the goal and a time plan; give your factor briefly; build on others by name; help the group decide; summarise. Weave in if technology comes up, LSE 24 and tokenisation [S278, S228]; if political, the Autumn Budget on 28 Oct 2026 [S243]. Trap talking over others; staying silent; arguing for your factor at any cost.
Q48 (H2). Case study: review an information pack and recommend a course of action.
Testing analysis, prioritising, a clear decision. Structure recommendation first; 3 reasons with numbers; risks and mitigations; next steps. Weave in only the facts in the pack; outside facts can look like you ignored the brief Inferred. Trap summarising the pack without a decision; running out of time.
Q49 (H3). A client is unhappy about a service outage. What do you do?
Testing client handling, integrity, escalation. Structure acknowledge; get the facts; escalate properly; keep the client informed; follow up and learn. Weave in LSEG's 19 Jul 2024 Workspace outage (RNS disrupted; LSE trading unaffected) shows why updates matter [S98]. Trap promising compensation you cannot authorise.
Q50 (H4). You have three urgent requests from different teams. How do you prioritise?
Testing judgement; also a classic immersive SJT format [S289] Inferred. Structure impact and urgency; clarify deadlines; communicate trade-offs; escalate if needed. Weave in client and regulatory deadlines first, because Integrity is about delivering "on our promises" [S271]. Trap trying to do everything alone.

I. Values: Integrity, Partnership, Excellence, Change (4)

LSEG states: "At LSEG, our values are Integrity, Partnership, Excellence, and Change" [S271]. Use its own definitions; assessors notice when you do.

Q51 (I1). Integrity ("We stand by our principles and deliver on our promises"). Tell us about a time you kept a promise when it was hard.
Testing reliability and ethics [S271]. Structure the promise; the obstacle; what you did; the cost; the result. Weave in "We earn trust by acting responsibly" [S271]. Trap a rule-breaking story framed as initiative.
Q52 (I2). Partnership ("We forge long-term relationships"). Tell us about a long-term relationship you built.
Testing relationship skills for the FX client role. Structure who; how you built trust over time; a moment it paid off. Weave in LSEG defines Partnership as "Our open model is integral to how we do business" [S307]; banks still co-own Post Trade Solutions (20%) [S300]. Trap a one-off networking event.
Q53 (I3). Excellence ("combining unique, diverse perspectives"). Tell us about a time a different view improved your work.
Testing openness and inclusion [S271]. Structure your first view; the other view; what changed; the result. Weave in nothing needed. Trap tokenism.
Q54 (I4). Change ("We embrace change"). Tell us about a change you drove or adapted to.
Testing adaptability, and a link to LSEG's innovation agenda [S271]. Structure the change; your response; outcome; what you learned. Weave in LSE 24, DiSH, the Digital Securities Depository [S278, S285]. Trap a change you resisted with no learning.

J. Ethics and compliance (4)

Q55 (J1). A friend asks about a listing you heard about at work before it is public. What do you do?
Testing understanding of inside information and confidentiality. Structure do not share; explain you cannot discuss work; report under policy if needed. Weave in LSEG's Code of Conduct: "If you witness or learn about inappropriate conduct ... you must follow the Speak Up Policy and not look the other way" [S307]. Do not quote rules you have not read. Trap "I would just give a hint".
Q56 (J2). A colleague's spreadsheet error went into a client report. What do you do?
Testing integrity and tact. Structure check; raise it privately and quickly; escalate if not fixed; focus on the client. Weave in LSEG's first line of defence owns risk "across the end-to-end product or service delivery" [S300]: that includes you. Trap ignoring it to avoid conflict.
Q57 (J3). Why does a market operator care so much about operational resilience?
Testing understanding of the systemic role. Structure markets and CCPs are critical infrastructure; outages hurt confidence; regulators expect resilience. Weave in the 8 Sep 2008 TradElect outage lasted over 7 hours [S100]; Maguire on LCH's new Chair: "deep expertise in governance, risk and operational resilience" [S276]. Trap treating it as only an IT topic.
Q58 (J4). A client offers you an expensive gift after you helped them. What do you do?
Testing awareness of conflicts of interest. Structure thank them; do not accept without checking policy; declare it. Weave in Integrity: "acting responsibly" [S271]. Trap accepting quietly.

Say this in the interview

A clean way in: "I read in the H1 report that [fact]. I was curious about [specific angle]. How does that look from where you sit?" It credits your source, shows the reading, and hands the floor back to them.

In a live interview you get signals. Use them to give the interviewer what they need, not to manage them. All points below are Inferred from the stage formats.

No manipulation tactics. Deliberate mirroring, flattery, or dropping the names of senior leaders you have never met will look false, and assessors are trained to notice Inferred. The aim of reading the room is to answer the question they are really asking.
