An answer that links growth to trust ("new products only work if clients trust the infrastructure") speaks the same language as the people who run the division.

MK1117KMReferencing a public statement appropriately

Say this in the interview

"In the LSE 24 release in July, LSEG said it wanted to give clients flexibility beyond normal trading hours. I wondered how you test demand for an overnight session before launch."

It cites the source (a release), uses the idea, and asks a question. The person's name is optional; the source is not.

Don't say this

"As Julia Hoggett said..." to someone who does not work on LSE, or "I saw Daniel Maguire worked at J.P. Morgan". Careers of senior people are not interview content. Comments on activists, share price or rumoured deals are also off limits Inferred.

  • Name the document, not the person, unless the interviewer works directly in that leader's area and the quote is on point.
  • Quote accurately or paraphrase. If you are unsure of exact words, say "LSEG said something like..." Never invent a quote.
  • Date it. "In the July release" shows currency and lets them correct you if things have moved on.
  • Turn it into a question. A public statement is a starting point for curiosity, not proof of insider knowledge.
  • Stay professional. Use only what leaders said in their roles. Nothing personal, nothing from social media.
MK1011KM
Part 11

The scenario playbook

One answer method, one priority order, and 36 rehearsed situations built from how LSEG Markets actually works, so a hard question meets a steady frame instead of a scramble.

Every later stage of this process puts you in a situation and watches what you do. The Immersive Online Assessment is very likely a Cappfinity-style simulation: one storyline, emails and data to read, and "what would you do" choices scored against a strengths model [S264, S265, S289] Inferred. The strengths video gives you one take of roughly one to two minutes per question, according to a candidate anecdote [S291] Reported. The virtual assessment centre includes group work, where (on another LSEG track) two assessors watched group behaviour more than content [S292] Reported.

Across all three, the assessor scores two things: what you would do, and how you hold yourself while you decide. The JD says it directly: they want people who "recognise that what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it" [S260]. This part gives you a fixed method so that the "how" stays calm even when the "what" is hard.

MK1118KMThe frame-holding method

Use the same four steps for every scenario, in every stage. In a live interview the whole answer runs 45 to 75 seconds. In the recorded video you can let the "Act" step run longer, up to about two minutes in total, but keep the shape.

Key term

Frame: the structure you hold an answer in. If you have a frame (steps, an order of priorities, a closing line), a hostile follow-up only moves you inside the frame. Without one, every follow-up feels like starting again. Situational judgement: a test format that describes a work situation and asks what you would do. It scores judgement, not knowledge.

Each step in detail

StepExact words to useWhat it does for youCommon mistake
1 Steady
0 to 5 s		"Let me check I have this right: you're asking what I'd do when the client can't connect and needs to trade before the fix."Buys three seconds, shows you listen, and sets the boundaries of the problem so a follow-up can't silently change it.Answering before the question finishes. Saying "Great question".
2 Sort
5 to 20 s		"Two things matter here: getting the client trading again, and not cutting corners on how. The second one sets the limits on the first."Shows judgement before action. Names the collision out loud, which is what the priority order below resolves.Listing six considerations. Saying "it depends" and stopping there.
3 Act
20 to 60 s		"First I'd log it with the incident team. Then I'd check whether it's one client or many. Then I'd call the client back by 8:20 with what we know."Concrete verbs, named owners, a time. One LSEG fact (for example, that outages are a named principal risk [S302]) shows you know where you are."I would communicate effectively with stakeholders." No verbs, no names, no times.
4 Close
60 to 75 s		"So the client hears from us when we said, the incident is logged, and nothing I promised is outside my control. Afterwards I'd ask what the root cause was."Restates outcome, owner and record. Ends the answer cleanly so the next question starts from strength.Trailing off: "...so yeah, something like that."
Say this in the interview

If you lose your place mid-answer, use the frame to find it: "So, to bring that together: first..., then..., and I'd make sure it's on record." It sounds deliberate, not lost.

MK1119KMThe priority order when good things collide

Most scenario questions are not about right versus wrong. They are about two good things that cannot both win: a client's speed against a check, a senior person's request against another's, helpfulness against confidentiality. Decide the order now, at your desk, so you never have to invent it on camera.

For LSEG Markets the order follows from what the businesses are. LSEG's venues and clearing houses are regulated market infrastructure: London Stock Exchange plc is a Recognised Investment Exchange, LCH Ltd is a Recognised Clearing House supervised by the Bank of England, and the FX venues are MTFs authorised by the FCA and the Central Bank of Ireland [S300, S304, S341] Confirmed. The Bank of England supervises CCPs to "protect and enhance financial stability in the UK" [S357]. LSEG names its own cyber risk as one that could "pose systemic risks" [S302]. A shortcut here is not a private matter between you and one client.

Why this order, tier by tier

  • Tier 1 beats everything because the firm's licence to operate is the product. LSEG's Integrity value reads: "We stand by our principles and deliver on our promises. We earn trust by acting responsibly" [S307]. The Code of Conduct prohibits trading on "confidential, proprietary, inside and/or material non-public information" [S307], and UK MAR defines inside information as precise, non-public and likely to have a significant effect on prices [S349].
  • Tier 2 beats process because fairness is written into LSEG's structure, not just its values. When LSEG took control of LCH, the OFT recorded that "No exchange will be favoured over any other and LSEG's trading services users will not be favoured over any other exchange's users" [S305]. LSEG's Partnership value begins: "Our open model is integral to how we do business" [S307]. In FX, the Global Code requires firms to "clearly and effectively identify and appropriately limit access to Confidential Information" (Principle 19) [S343].
  • Tier 3 beats speed because LSEG puts accountability for risk "within the first line of defence", with second-line oversight and third-line assurance [S300]. As an intern you are in the first line. Your job is to follow the control, escalate, and write it down, not to decide that a control does not apply today.
  • Tier 4 is still a duty. The JD says the division needs "instant reaction and long-term vision" [S260]. Never use the order as an excuse to be slow. The best answers say what you would do in the next ten minutes.
CollisionWinnerWhat you say
Client wants a trade amended now; amendments need the operations process3 over 4"I'll get it to the team who can amend it properly, and I'll tell you within the hour where it stands."
Loyal client asks what another bank is doing2 over 4"I can't talk about any other client, and you'd want the same for you. Here's what I can share."
Senior colleague asks you to backdate a log entry1 over 3"I can add a note today that explains the timing. I can't change the date it was done."
Issuer wants faster admission than the review window2 over 4"Every issuer gets the same review. I can make sure nothing on our side adds delay."
Manager wants a flattering chart for an external deck1 over 4"I'll show both periods with context so it holds up if a client checks."
Don't say this

"I'd just use my judgement." It sounds like you will make up the order on the day. Say the order: "Rules first, then fairness, then the process, then speed, and I'd push hard on speed inside those."

MK1120KMEight ways interviewers break a frame

Good interviewers push. They are not trying to catch you out for sport. They want to see whether your answer was a real decision or a memorised line. Each push below has a counter. The counter always does the same thing: it accepts the new information, then puts it back inside your frame.

How to tell a better reason from pressure

The hardest skill is knowing when to change your mind. Change it when the interviewer gives you a new fact ("the client is already approved for that route", "the control owner has signed a waiver"). Hold it when they give you only new pressure ("the MD is angry", "everyone else does it", "you'll lose the client"). Say which one it is: "That's new information, so I'd change step two" or "I understand that's uncomfortable, and I'd still do it this way." Assessors are often scoring exactly this distinction Inferred.

Changing your mind well

"That's a fair challenge. If the owner has already approved an exception, then yes, I'd use it and make sure it's logged. I'd change my answer on that point."

Changing your mind badly

"Oh, OK, then I suppose I would just do it." This tells the assessor that your first answer was a guess and that pressure works on you.

MK1121KMStaying calm physically

Your body leaks stress before your words do. Prepare the room and your breathing the way you prepare content.

Breathing

  • Before each question (or while the video prep timer runs): breathe in through the nose for four, out through the mouth for six. Twice. A longer out-breath slows you down.
  • When a hard follow-up lands: breathe out first, then say your Steady line. The out-breath is your three seconds.

Posture on video

  • Camera at eye level (books under the laptop). Face lit from the front, not a window behind you.
  • Sit back in the chair, then lean in slightly. Feet flat. Hands visible and still on the desk or moving gently with your points.
  • Look at the camera lens when making your main point and when closing, not at your own face on screen.

Notes

  • One index card behind or beside the camera: the four steps, the priority order, three numbers. Not a script: reading shows on camera.
  • For the virtual assessment centre: a blank sheet for notes during reading time, with your priority order written at the top.

Water and pace

  • A glass of water in reach. A sip is a legitimate two-second pause in a live interview.
  • Speak slower than feels natural. Pause at full stops. Under stress most people speed up by a third.
  • In the recorded video, the anecdote is one take per answer [S291] Reported. Use the untimed prep to sketch the four steps, not to write sentences.
Why this matters

In a strengths-based format, assessors watch for energy and authenticity as well as content [S264, S289]. Calm, unhurried delivery reads as confidence. A rushed, perfect script reads as rehearsal.

MK1122KMThe scenario ladder: 36 cards

Each JD duty line, plus the two behaviour lines, gets three scenarios: easy (do you know the basics), medium (two goods collide), hard (pressure or an ethical edge). Practise them aloud with the four-step protocol, timing yourself. The figure is the map; the cards follow in the same order.

How to read a card

Setup is the situation. Trap is the answer most candidates give. Say is a model answer in the four-step shape: adapt the words, keep the order. Why gives the LSEG fact behind it. Twist is the follow-up push, and Hold is how to keep your frame.

Line 1: Solve problems for FX customers and understand their goals

1E. "What can FXall do for us?"Easy
Setup A mid-sized asset manager is new to FXall. Their treasurer says: "We need to show our board we get good prices, and we spend too long on manual work."
Trap Reciting a feature list before you know which feature matters.
Say "Can I check I have the two goals right: evidence of good execution, and less manual work? For evidence, FXall's Trade Performance Reporting lets you evaluate the cost and effectiveness of your execution. For manual work, trades can flow straight through to your own systems by FIX API or your treasury system, with confirmations and settlement instructions handled on the platform. I'd suggest we agree one measure for each goal now and look at it together in three months."
Why FXall offers confirmations, settlement instructions, Trade Performance Reporting and STP (straight-through processing: no re-keying) [S340]. The JD asks you to "understand their business goals" [S260]. Leading with their goals, not your product, is the Partnership value: "we work together to solve evolving needs" [S307].
Twist "Just tell us which execution method is cheapest." Hold: "It depends on your trade sizes and currency pairs. FXall has request-for-quote, bank price streams, an anonymous order book and algorithms like TWAP [S342]. I'd rather show you your own data than give a general answer that's wrong for you."
1M. Too many rejected trades (last look)Medium
Setup A hedge fund client says one liquidity provider keeps rejecting their trades after quoting. "They're using last look against us. What are you going to do about it?"
Trap Agreeing the bank is cheating, or defending the bank. Either way you have judged a third party on one client's say-so.
Say "I take that seriously, so let me get the facts: which provider, which pairs, what times, how many rejects. Last look is a final chance for a provider to accept or reject a request at its quoted price, and the FX Global Code says providers using it should be transparent and disclose it to clients. So I'd pull your own Trade Performance Reporting so you can see the reject pattern, point you to that provider's last-look disclosure, and raise the pattern internally with the team that manages liquidity providers. I'll come back to you by Thursday with what I've found."
Why FX Global Code Principle 17 (Dec 2024) [S343]; GFXC guidance says last look "should not be used for purposes of information gathering" [S344] Reported. Reporting data comes from FXall [S340]. The split (provider owns disclosure, venue supplies data) is this pack's reading Inferred.
Twist "Just tell us which other banks don't do it." Hold: "Which providers you trade with is your choice, and I'll help you set that up. I can't rank providers using other clients' trading. Your data, yes; theirs, no."
1H. "Which bank should we send our flow to?"Hard
Setup A corporate treasurer wants you to name the best bank among FXall's providers and hints that FXall should rank banks using what it sees across all clients. "You see everything. Help us."
Trap Feeling helpful and giving a name, or hinting at what other clients see. Both break fair treatment (tier 2) and confidentiality.
Say "I want you to get the best result, and I'll do that with your data, not anyone else's. FXall has over 200 liquidity providers; your own execution reports will show which fill you well on your pairs and sizes. What I can't do is use other clients' trading to rank banks for you: that's confidential to them, in the same way yours is to you. If it helps, I'll walk your team through reading your own reports next week."
Why 200+ liquidity providers, 2,400+ institutional clients [S340]. FX Global Code P19 and P20: limit access to confidential information and do not disclose it externally [S343]. Code of Conduct: never disclose confidential information without a legitimate need to know [S307]. A venue that picks favourites among providers loses the trust that makes it a venue Inferred.
Twist "Another platform would do this for us." Hold: "Then I'd ask how they protect your data too. The rule that stops me sharing theirs is the rule that protects yours."

Line 2: Maintain relationships and keep customers informed

2E. Prepare a client business reviewEasy
Setup Your manager asks you to draft slides for a quarterly business review with a large FXall client next week.
Trap Ten charts of volumes with no story, and no link to what the client said they wanted last time.
Say "I'd start from the goals the client set last quarter. Then three sections: what they traded and how it changed; where their workflow had friction, such as rejects, breaks or support tickets; and two options for next quarter. I'd check every number against the source system before it goes in, and ask you which commercial topics, like new products, it's right to raise."
Why LSEG's FX Senior Account Manager ad says the role leads "business reviews" and should "identify upsell, cross-sell, and new business opportunities across FX trading, workflow, data, and related LSEG solutions" [S313]. A new Group Head of Sales and Account Management joined in Jan 2026 [S306].
Twist "Client cancelled. Send it by email instead." Hold: "I'd send a one-page summary with the three points and the numbers, and offer a 15-minute call. Same content, shorter."
2M. FXall outage: the client calls at 8:05Medium
Setup 8:05 London time. A client can't connect to FXall and has month-end hedges to do. They're angry and want a fix time.
Trap Guessing the cause, promising a fix time you don't own, or going quiet until you know more.
Say "I'd say: 'I hear you, and I'm on it now. I'll call you back by 8:20 with what we know, even if it isn't much.' Then I'd log it through the incident process straight away, check whether it's one client or many, and ask the support team whether there's an approved alternative route for them to trade. At 8:20 I call back, as promised. I won't guess the cause or promise a fix time I don't control."
Why LSEG's H1 2026 principal risks include technology risk, where "system outages... could impact customer access" [S302]. The 2024 Workspace outage disrupted RNS publication and drew market-wide attention [S98] Reported. In infrastructure, reliability is the brand Inferred.
Twist "Can't you just do the trade for me over the phone?" Hold: "I can't execute trades for you; that isn't my role. What I can do is find out in the next few minutes which approved routes are open to you."
2H. "Off the record, what is Bank X doing?"Hard
Setup Over coffee, a long-standing, friendly client asks: "Off the record, is [big bank] pulling back from emerging market FX? You must see it."
Trap A hint, a smile, or "I can't say, but...". A nod is disclosure.
Say "I'd say it plainly and warmly: 'I can't talk about any other client's activity, on or off the record, and you'd want me to say exactly the same about you.' Then I'd move to what I can offer: our published volume figures, public market data, or a look at their own trading."
Why FX Global Code P19 and P20 [S343]; Code of Conduct need-to-know rule [S307]. Confidentiality is part of how LSEG's structure was approved: information barriers so rivals can deal with LCH "assured of the confidentiality of those discussions" [S305].
Twist "Come on, just yes or no." Hold: "Even yes or no is information. The answer's the same, and I'd still like to help with what I can share."

Line 3: Deal with post-sale activity

3E. New price stream not showingEasy
Setup A client asked to receive a new bank's price stream on FXall last week. It still isn't showing.
Trap Promising "it'll be on today" without knowing who has to approve what.
Say "I'd find the request first. Permissioning on FXall runs through FXall Admin, the reference data and permissioning tool, as a price stream entitlement request. I'd check whether it was submitted, who still has to act, for example the bank agreeing to stream to this client, and tell the client today exactly what is pending and with whom."
Why LSEG's FX Venue Onboarding ad lists "Price Stream Entitlement requests" in "FXall Admin" [S317]. PriceStream is disclosed bank streams [S342]. That the bank must agree is this pack's reading of "disclosed" Inferred.
Twist "Can't you just switch it on yourself?" Hold: "I don't have that access and I wouldn't want it. Entitlement controls protect both you and the bank."
3M. Trade break at 4pmMedium
Setup A client's back office says the confirmation for a large EUR/USD forward shows a different value date from their record. Settlement is close.
Trap Telling the client which side is right, or trying to amend the trade yourself to be helpful.
Say "Steady: 'Let me take the trade ID and both versions.' Sort: the risk is settling on the wrong date, so time matters, and amendments must be controlled. Act: I'd send it straight to the operations team that owns confirmations, and make sure the counterparty bank is contacted through the proper channel. Close: I tell the client who is handling it and when they'll hear back, and I log it so we can see whether the same break keeps happening."
Why FX Global Code P46: confirm trades "as soon as practicable"; P48: "identify and resolve confirmation and settlement discrepancies as soon as practicable"; P45: amendments "in a carefully controlled manner" [S343]. FXall provides confirmations and STP [S340].
Twist "The bank says it's our error." Hold: "It might be. The fix is the same: find the source, correct it through the controlled process, and if it's ours, say so and fix the cause."
3H. Invoice dispute and an exit threatHard
Setup A client says this quarter's invoice is far higher than they expected and they will move to a rival venue unless it's fixed. They want a credit on this call.
Trap Offering a discount you have no authority to give, or blaming the billing team.
Say "I'd acknowledge it and not argue on the call. Then I'd get the invoice and the contract, find exactly which line they dispute, and check with billing whether it's higher usage, a fee change they were told about, or an error. I'd come back by a set time with the explanation. If it's our error, we fix it. Any credit or price change is for my manager to decide, and it has to be consistent with how we treat other clients."
Why FX revenue mixes transaction fees (about 75%) with recurring membership and data fees (about 25%) [S303], so a bill can rise with usage. LSEG is building a "unified revenue and billing platform" [S301]. LSEG FX fee schedules were not found in research.
Twist "Your competitor offered us half price." Hold: "I'll pass that on accurately today. I won't match a price on the call; I'll make sure the person who decides hears it."
Source uncertain

How LSEG FX handles billing queries, and its fee schedules, were not found in public sources. Treat 3H as a general method, not a description of LSEG's process.

Line 4: Research into global markets and debt listings

4E. ISM or Main Market? A one-page answerEasy
Setup Your manager asks for a one-page comparison for an overseas issuer choosing where to list a bond.
Trap Copying an old LSE brochure that still talks about the "UKLA" and the "Prospectus Directive".
Say "I'd set out three rows. Who it's for: the International Securities Market is for qualified, professional investors; the Main Market can serve a wider investor base. Who decides admission: on ISM, the Exchange; it isn't on the FCA's Official List. What document: ISM uses admission particulars, and exempt issuers don't need them. I'd use the January 2026 rulebook terms, because the older info pack predates the current regime, and I'd flag the timings as 'check current'."
Why ISM Rulebook (Jan 2026): MTF for qualified investors, admission "determined by the Exchange", not on the Official List, admission particulars not required for exempt issuers [S346]. The ISM info pack cites UKLA and the Prospectus Directive and is out of date [S347].
Twist "So which is better?" Hold: "It depends on who the issuer wants to sell to. I'd lay out the trade-offs and let the issuer decide with its advisers."
4M. "Can we list on ISM by Friday?"Medium
Setup Monday morning. An issuer's adviser emails: they want ISM admission on Friday. They haven't submitted draft particulars yet.
Trap Saying yes to keep them happy.
Say "I'd do the arithmetic first. The Exchange aims to comment within three days of a first submission and two days of later ones, and wants final documents and a signed ISM Form 1 by 9am one business day before admission. Submit today, and first comments could come by Thursday, with the final-documents deadline also Thursday at 9am. So Friday is at serious risk. I'd tell them that honestly, say what would have to be true for it to work, check with the admissions team whether the express route or an exemption applies, and give a realistic date."
Why "Competitive turnaround times (3+2)"; 9am one business day before; decision via a Dealing Notice on RNS [S347]; express route exists [S346]. The info pack is older than the 2026 rulebook, so current timings need checking.
Twist "Their CEO is very well known. Can't you push it through?" Hold: "Every issuer gets the same review. I can make sure nothing on our side adds delay and that they know exactly what we need."
4H. "Pick a window that looks better"Hard
Setup Your research for an external client presentation shows London listings are recovering from a low base. A senior colleague asks you to choose a time window that makes the trend "look stronger".
Trap Quietly cherry-picking, or refusing in a way that embarrasses them.
Say "I'd offer a version that is both strong and fair: 'Can I show the recent rise and the longer period side by side, with context? For example, 2025 UK IPO proceeds were up 170% to £2.1bn, but from a weak 2024. If we only show the flattering window and a client checks, we lose more than a slide.' Then I'd build it that way."
Why 2025: 23 UK IPOs raising £2.1bn, up 170% on £777.7m [S192]; 88 companies left the LSE in 2024 [S200] Reported. Integrity: "We earn trust by acting responsibly" [S307]. LSEG is itself a listed company, so its external numbers are scrutinised Inferred.
Twist "It's only internal, relax." Hold: "Then let's label the window clearly, so nobody reuses it externally by mistake."

Line 5: Valuations, shareholder and geographic analysis

5E. Who owns this issuer, and where?Easy
Setup Build a shareholder and geographic breakdown of a listed company from public data. Practise on LSEG itself.
Trap Mixing figures from different dates in one table with no dates shown.
Say "One dated public source per number. For LSEG at December 2025: Qatar Investment Authority 6.2%, BlackRock 5.7%, Capital Group 5.1%, Microsoft 4.1%, Lindsell Train 4.1%. I'd group holders by type: sovereign, index, active, strategic. I'd flag what's missing: Elliott built a stake in February 2026 but its size wasn't disclosed. For geography, I'd be clear that revenue 'by location of service provider' is where LSEG's entity sits, not where the customer is."
Why Top holders and revenue by location, Annual Report 2025 [S74]; Elliott stake [S86].
Twist "Can you find out who's buying this week?" Hold: "From public disclosures, yes. Not from our own venues' data about named clients. That isn't mine to use."
5M. Two sources give different numbersMedium
Setup You need LSEG's headcount for a slide. The Annual Report says 28,516 at end 2025; the job advert says 25,000; the investor deck says over 26,000.
Trap Picking one silently, or averaging them.
Say "I'd use the Annual Report figure, 28,516 at 31 December 2025, because it is audited and dated, and footnote the others as older marketing copy. The general habit: name the source, the date and the definition, and show the gap if it matters."
Why 28,516 [S300]; "over 26,000 people in 65 countries" [S303]; "25,000 people across 65 countries" in job ads [S317]. The JD's curiosity for data means checking definitions [S260].
Twist "Just use the round number, it's a slide." Hold: "Happy to say 'about 28,500'. I wouldn't use 25,000: it's a different, older number, not a rounding."
5H. "A valuation in an hour, please"Hard
Setup A senior colleague needs a rough valuation of a private company that is thinking about listing, for a meeting in an hour. Data is thin.
Trap A single precise number that looks authoritative, or "I can't, there's not enough data".
Say "I'd give a range, not a point, with the method in one line and the two assumptions that move it most, labelled 'indicative, internal, estimate'. I'd add what would change it. And because a possible listing that isn't public could be inside information, I'd keep the file and the conversation to the people who need it."
Why UK MAR Art 7: inside information is precise, non-public and price-sensitive [S349]; Code of Conduct need-to-know [S307]. Valuations shift: Visma (about €19bn reported) chose London then postponed to 2027 [S194] Reported.
Twist "The company wants to quote the top of your range in its pitch." Hold: "It's an internal estimate, not advice; that's for their advisers. I'd tell my manager about the request."

Line 6: Delivery of business intelligence

6E. Build the Markets KPI one-pagerEasy
Setup Your manager wants a one-page summary of Markets volumes for a team meeting.
Trap A table of numbers with no definitions and no "so what".
Say "I'd use the KPIs LSEG publishes, with definitions. H1 2026: UK average daily value traded £6.67bn, up 33.5%; Tradeweb ADV $3.2trn, up 24.8%; FX ADV $561bn, up 5.8%; SwapClear notional $1,165trn, up 29.4%. One headline line on top: volumes rose everywhere, fastest in UK equities and SwapClear, slowest in FX. Then one of my own measures, clearly labelled: revenue per unit of volume."
Why KPI table, H1 2026 [S302]. ADV means average daily volume. Revenue capture (for example FX revenue £272m on $525bn ADV in 2025) is this pack's metric, not one LSEG publishes [S301] Inferred.
Twist "Make it fit in one sentence." Hold: "Markets volumes grew across the board in H1 2026, led by UK equities and SwapClear, with FX the slowest."
6M. FX volume jumps 40% overnightMedium
Setup Your dashboard shows FX average daily volume up 40% day on day. Your manager wants the daily note out in 30 minutes.
Trap Reporting it as news without checking.
Say "I'd check before I report. Is it real: a market event, month-end, a holiday elsewhere? Is it data: a duplicated feed, a currency conversion, a changed definition? I'd compare against the source system and known events. If I can't settle it in 30 minutes, the note goes out on time with the figure flagged 'under review' and a time for the update."
Why LSEG reported "exceptional" clearing activity in Q1 2026 on volatility [S285], so big moves can be real. LSEG says customer-raised data quality issues fell 51% over four years [S301]: data quality is a measured priority.
Twist "The MD has already seen it and is pleased." Hold: "Then it matters more that I tell them today if it's wrong."
6H. Two seniors, two market share numbersHard
Setup Two senior people want LSEG FX's market share. One wants it against total global FX turnover; the other against a narrower electronic market. Each wants their version on the slide.
Trap Picking the more senior person's version, or the more flattering one.
Say "I'd show both, each with its definition, and say which question each answers. For example, LSEG FX's $561bn ADV against BIS global turnover of $9.6tn a day is about 6%, but BIS includes FX swaps, which are 42% of turnover, and the dates differ, so it's a rough estimate. Then I'd ask my manager to agree which one goes on the slide, and copy both people."
Why BIS April 2025: $9.6tn a day, swaps 42% [S163]; LSEG FX ADV H1 2026 [S302]. 561 / 9,600 = 5.8% is this pack's arithmetic across different dates Inferred, est.
Twist "Just pick one, I need it tomorrow." Hold: "Then I'd pick the one that matches the question on the slide, write the definition under it, and tell the other person so no one is surprised."

Line 7: Strategic initiatives

7E. Measure FXall use inside WorkspaceEasy
Setup You're asked how to measure whether FX clients are actually using FXall inside the Workspace desktop.
Trap One vanity metric ("number of logins").
Say "I'd measure adoption, depth and outcome. Adoption: the share of FXall clients who trade through Workspace at all. Depth: trades per client and which workflows they use. Outcome: support tickets, onboarding time and whether retention or cross-sell changes. I'd split by client type, and say where we only have proxies."
Why "We have now added a large proportion of FXAll's functionality" to Workspace [S302]. The FX account role targets cross-sell "across FX trading, workflow, data" [S313].
Twist "We don't have outcome data yet." Hold: "Then I'd track adoption and depth now, define outcome measures, and set a date to review them."
7M. Size LSE 24 demand in two daysMedium
Setup You have two days to give a first view on demand for overnight trading of ETPs on LSE 24.
Trap A confident single number with hidden assumptions.
Say "I'd start with who would trade between 17:00 and 07:50 London time: investors in Asia and the US, and UK retail investors after work. For each, one piece of evidence and one assumption. I'd give a range and the two assumptions that drive it, and list what client testing should tell us."
Why LSE 24: separate 24/5 venue, 17:00 to 07:50, ETPs first in H1 2027, client testing by end 2026 [S278]. ETP means exchange-traded product, such as an ETF.
Twist "The product head loves it. Just make the case." Hold: "I'll build the strongest honest case, risks included. A case that hides them won't survive the committee."
7H. "Give our venue users an LCH discount"Hard
Setup In a brainstorm a colleague proposes cheaper clearing at LCH for customers who trade on LSEG's own venues. "Easy cross-sell."
Trap Enthusiasm. It sounds commercial, and it collides with LSEG's founding rule for LCH.
Say "I like connecting the businesses, but I think this one hits a hard line. LCH has to offer services on fair, reasonable, open and non-discriminatory terms, and LSEG's trading users can't be favoured over other exchanges' users. So I'd redirect to connections that are allowed: workflow, like FXall inside Workspace, or joint products like RepoAgent from Post Trade Solutions and Tradeweb."
Why OFT decision on open access [S305]; LCH's "open access model" today [S304]; RepoAgent [S301]; FXall in Workspace [S302]. No LSEG statement ties ForexClear to FXall commercially (research gap).
Twist "Deutsche Börse ties trading and clearing and does fine." Hold: "It does. It's a different model. LSEG chose open access, and that's part of why the market trusts LCH with over 90% of cleared interest rate swap notional [S303]."

Line 8: Operational improvements

8E. Map the FX onboarding stepsEasy
Setup You're asked to map how a new FX client is onboarded, end to end.
Trap Proposing fixes before you know the process.
Say "I'd map it as it is today before suggesting anything: each step, who does it, how long it takes, and where work is handed over or redone. I'd talk to the people who do each step, including teams in other locations, and check my map with them. Then I'd mark the two or three biggest delays."
Why Onboarding of buy-side and sell-side clients runs in FXall Admin, from Manila among other places [S317]; LSEG runs operations hubs across several countries [S319].
Twist "The Manila team does half of it. Just guess their part." Hold: "I'd rather book 20 minutes with them. Guessing their part is how maps go wrong."
8M. "We like the old spreadsheet"Medium
Setup You find a manual spreadsheet step that causes repeated errors. The team that uses it doesn't want to change.
Trap Arguing from opinion, or going over their heads.
Say "I'd bring data, not opinion: how many errors in the last three months, how long each took to fix. I'd ask the team what they like about the spreadsheet, because there's usually a reason. Then I'd suggest a small trial run alongside the old way, so nothing breaks, and give the team the credit if it works."
Why LSEG reports engineering changes that "increased our velocity by 25%, while reducing major incidents by 50%", and an AI Q&A tool that cut query resolution time 40% across 22,000 queries a month [S301]. Change value: "We embrace change" [S307].
Twist "The last intern's idea broke things." Hold: "That's why I'd run it in parallel and keep the old way until it's proven."
8H. Your fix removes a four-eyes checkHard
Setup Your process improvement would save hours a week, mainly by removing a second-person check on client settlement details. Your manager likes the time saving.
Trap Proposing the removal because it makes your project look good.
Say "A four-eyes check is a control, so I wouldn't remove it in my proposal. I'd propose automating it instead: a system check that flags mismatches. Any change to the control goes through its owner and the second line. If they agree it's redundant, it can go properly, and on record."
Why Three lines of defence [S300]; LSEG's control framework includes "material control assessments and attestations" [S314]. FX Global Code P51: standard settlement instructions maintained by staff segregated from sales and trading [S343]. See the composure set below for the live version of this.
Twist "Nobody even looks at that check." Hold: "Then let's ask the control owner to confirm that in writing. If it's truly redundant, it'll be easy to remove properly."

Line 9: Risk monitoring and analysis

9E. Explain the default waterfall in 60 secondsEasy
Setup "Explain to a new joiner what happens at LCH if a member defaults."
Trap Jargon without order, or getting the order wrong.
Say "LCH stands between buyer and seller, so if a member fails, LCH takes on its trades. The losses are absorbed in order. First, the defaulter's own margin and default fund contribution. Next, LCH's own capital, its 'skin in the game'. Only then the other members' default fund. Initial margin is set at 99.7% confidence, and LCH says all nine member defaults it has managed stayed within initial margin. Lehman's $9 trillion swap book used about 35% of its margin."
Why Waterfall order, 99.7%, nine defaults [S351]; Lehman [S354]. Initial margin is collateral posted upfront to cover a member's possible losses.
Twist "And if that's not enough?" Hold: "There are further tools in LCH's rules, but I don't know the detail beyond the waterfall, and I'd check rather than guess."
9M. Member asks to pay a margin call laterMedium
Setup On a volatile day a clearing member's operations contact asks you to "have a word with risk" to delay an intraday margin call by a few hours, as a favour.
Trap Treating it as a relationship favour, or promising anything.
Say "I'd say: 'I'll pass that to the risk team now, exactly as you've put it. I can't promise anything: margin calls follow the same rules for every member.' Then I'd pass it on in writing straight away, tell the member who will reply, and leave the decision with risk."
Why LCH makes "multiple intraday margin calls" [S351]; LCH must treat users on non-discriminatory terms [S305].
Twist "They're one of the founding banks." Hold: "That's why the rules have to be the same. Members sit on the risk committee, and no one group has a majority [S304]."
9H. Limit breach found at 6pm on FridayHard
Setup Compiling a risk report on Friday evening, you notice a metric went over its limit two days ago. Nobody has flagged it.
Trap Leaving it until Monday, or quietly fixing the data so it disappears.
Say "I'd do a quick check that it isn't my own data error, five minutes, not a reason to wait. Then I'd tell my manager tonight with the evidence: what, when, how far over. If I can't reach them, the next person on the escalation path or the risk team. I'd log it as a risk event as the process requires. I wouldn't speculate on the cause."
Why LSEG's control framework includes "risk event and issue management standards" and a Group Risk team that "proactively identifies, escalates" [S314]; first line owns risk [S300].
Twist "It's probably nothing. It can wait." Hold: "Probably. A Friday flag that turns out to be nothing costs ten minutes. A Monday surprise costs much more."

Line 10: Interpreting data for risk projects and reporting

10E. Vendor risk data into committee MIEasy
Setup You're given a spreadsheet of third-party (vendor) risk ratings and asked to turn it into a one-page report for a committee.
Trap Pasting the whole spreadsheet in small font.
Say "I'd ask what decision the committee makes with it. Then: exceptions first (anything red or getting worse), the trend since last time, and each red item with its owner and next action. The full list goes in an appendix."
Why LCH first-line roles produce third-party risk MI (management information) "for senior management, committees and Board forums" [S318]. Third-party risk is a named principal risk [S302].
Twist "They don't like red. Can it look greener?" Hold: "I'll show the red honestly with the action next to it. That's what the committee needs to do its job."
10M. Pack due today, one feed missingMedium
Setup A committee risk pack is due at 5pm. The data feed for one entity hasn't arrived.
Trap Copying last month's figure in, or missing the deadline without warning.
Say "I'd tell my manager now, not at 4:55. Then I'd deliver on time with the gap clearly marked: 'data not received; last confirmed value X at date Y; update by Z'. I'd chase the data owner and log why it was late."
Why LCH Ltd's Board has Risk and Operational Resilience committees [S304]; Data is a named principal risk [S302].
Twist "Just use last month's figure. No one will notice." Hold: "I can show last month's figure, labelled as last month's. I can't present it as today's."
10H. Your analysis says the model is wrongHard
Setup Your back-testing suggests a margin model under-covers one product in stressed markets. Your manager says: "Models team owns that. Leave it."
Trap Dropping it, or going straight over your manager's head.
Say "I'd say: 'I may well be wrong, and I'd like to learn why. Could we send my two-page write-up to the model owner so they can check it?' I'd make the note short and factual: data, method, result, limits. If it were blocked and I still believed it mattered, LSEG has Speak Up channels, but I'd expect the normal route to work."
Why Model risk, including margining, is a named principal risk [S302]. Code of Conduct: "not look the other way"; no retaliation [S307]. Speak Up received 192 reports in 2025 [S300].
Twist "You're an intern. You don't understand the model." Hold: "That's possible. That's exactly why I'd like the owner to tell me where I'm wrong."

Line 11: Individual contributor and team work across the product lifecycle

11E. A vague task on day threeEasy
Setup Your manager says: "Have a look into post-trade for FX clients," then goes into a meeting.
Trap Spending three days on something nobody needed.
Say "I'd write down my understanding and send it: 'I'm reading this as: which post-trade problems FX clients raise most, in a one-page note by Thursday. Unless you'd like something different, I'll start there and check in on Wednesday.' Then I start."
Why The JD expects you to be "an individual contributor" [S260]. Post-trade on FXall covers confirmations, settlement instructions and reporting [S340].
Twist "No reply by Wednesday." Hold: "I'd send a two-line update and keep going on my stated plan."
11M. The dominator in the group exerciseMedium
Setup At the assessment centre, one candidate talks over everyone and pushes their option.
Trap Fighting them for airtime, or going silent.
Say "I'd build on their point, then widen it: 'That's a strong point on cost. Can we hear from everyone quickly before we decide? Priya, you mentioned the risk angle earlier.' I'd suggest criteria we agree on, keep an eye on time, and summarise near the end so the group decides."
Why An LSEG technology-track anecdote describes four candidates, about 30 minutes' reading then 30 minutes' discussion, two assessors watching group behaviour [S292] Reported.
Twist They dismiss your idea. Hold: "Fair. Let's test both against the criteria we agreed."
11H. Launch date set, operations not readyHard
Setup You track a product launch plan. Operations says client reporting isn't tested. The product lead wants to go anyway and asks you to mark it green.
Trap Marking it green to keep the peace, or making the go/no-go call yourself.
Say "My job is to make the risk visible, not to decide. I'd mark it amber with the reason, the owner and the impact, and make sure it's in front of whoever decides the launch. If they accept the risk, that's their call, and it's recorded."
Why LSEG business programme roles coordinate "Risk, Operations, Product, Technology..." and give "decision support and recommendations to senior management, governance forums and steering committees" [S315]. Transformation is a named principal risk [S302].
Twist "If you mark it amber, the launch slips and it's on you." Hold: "If it's amber, it's amber. A visible risk that's accepted is fine; a hidden one isn't."

Line 12: Fast pace, resilience and changing demands

12E. Priorities flip on WednesdayEasy
Setup Halfway through your project, your manager moves you to an urgent new one.
Trap Visible frustration, or leaving the first project in a mess.
Say "I'd confirm the new priority and deadline, then park the first project cleanly: a short note of where it stands and what's next, so I or anyone can pick it up. I'd tell the people waiting on it. Then full focus on the new one."
Why The JD asks for "focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands" [S260].
Twist "Can you do both?" Hold: "Yes, if the first moves to next week. Which matters more to you this week?"
12M. Three urgent asks at the same timeMedium
Setup An FX account manager wants a client deck by 3pm; the risk team wants a data pull by 2pm; your manager wants a research summary by end of day.
Trap Saying yes to all three and doing all of them badly.
Say "I'd sort by the priority order and real deadlines: the risk data first, because it feeds a control; then the client deck, because a client is waiting; then the internal summary. I'd tell each person when they'll get it. If two deadlines truly clash, I'd ask my manager to decide rather than choose between two senior people myself."
Why Priority order above. The JD's "instant reaction and long-term vision" [S260].
Twist "All three say theirs is most important." Hold: "Then it's my manager's call, and I'd make it easy: one message, three asks, my suggested order."
12H. Volatile day, manager on leaveHard
Setup Gilt yields jump in the run-up to the Budget, volumes spike, client calls pile up, and your manager is on leave.
Trap Acting beyond your role to look capable, or freezing.
Say "I'd stay in my lane and make it work hard. Check who's covering for my manager, and tell them what's coming in. Triage calls: anything about access, risk or settlement goes straight to the right team; everything else gets a callback time. Keep a log of every request and who owns it. At the end of the day, send the cover a summary."
Why Q1 2026 brought "exceptional clearing activity" on volatility [S285]; gilt yields rose before the 28 Oct 2026 Budget [S243] Reported. Business continuity is a named principal risk [S302].
Twist "A client asks where you think sterling is going." Hold: "I don't give market views. I can point you to our published data and the right team."

MK1123KMThe composure set: five hard scenarios

These five are the ones most likely to rattle you, because each puts a senior person, a client or your own mistake in the way of the right answer. Each has a decision tree. The first two trees below are drawn; the other three are written as steps. Learn the questions in the trees, not the wording.

C1. Two senior people want the same scarce thing

Setup. Two directors each ask you, on the same morning, to spend tomorrow on their analysis. Or two account managers each want the one client slot left in next week's product demo. Each says theirs is the priority.

#Ask yourselfIf yesIf no
1Do I know each request's real deadline and what it's for?Go to 2.Ask both: "What decision does it feed, and by when?"
2Is there a real clash, or can both be done with a small change (half a day each, a later slot)?Go to 3.Propose the split to both, in writing.
3Does one request involve a control, a regulator or a client commitment already made?That one goes first (priority tiers 1 to 3). Tell the other person why, and when you'll start theirs.Go to 4.
4Is it my place to choose between two senior people?(It rarely is.)Take it to your line manager with both asks and a suggested order. Copy nobody into a fight.
Say this in the interview

"I wouldn't pick between two directors myself. I'd find out what each piece is for and when it's needed, see if both can be done with a small change, and if not, take both requests to my manager with a suggested order. Both directors would hear the same thing from me."

C2. A senior person asks you to skip a control

Setup. A senior colleague, under deadline, says: "Just send the client file without the second sign-off. I'll take responsibility."

Say this in the interview

"I'd want to help them hit the deadline, so I'd first check exactly which check it is and whether there's an approved exception. If there isn't, I'd tell them I can't skip it, and I'd escalate straight away to get the second signer moving. 'I'll take responsibility' is kind, but it doesn't change who owns the control."

C3. You overhear possible inside information or another client's flow

Setup. In a shared kitchen, or on an open Teams call, you hear that a named company is about to announce a bond deal or a takeover, or how much a named bank traded yesterday. Later a friend at university, who trades shares, asks "anything interesting at work?"

Key term

Insider list: a record that issuers (and people acting for them) must keep of everyone with access to inside information, with the reason and the date and time of access, kept for at least five years [S348]. Information barrier: rules and systems that stop confidential information flowing between teams that shouldn't share it [S305].

C4. A mistake you made is in a report already sent to a client

Setup. On Tuesday you find that a chart in Monday's client report used the wrong month's volume. Your manager sent it to the client.

#Ask yourselfIf yesIf no
1Am I sure it's an error? (Five minutes to check, not a day.)Go to 2.Note what you checked; mention it to your manager anyway.
2Could it change a client's decision, or touch a regulated report?Tell your manager within the hour, in person or by call, then in writing.Still tell your manager today. Small errors hidden become big errors found.
3Has my manager decided how to tell the client?Prepare the correction: what was wrong, the right figure, what it changes. Short and plain.Offer a draft correction; don't contact the client yourself.
4Do I know why it happened?Fix the cause: a check step, a source label, a template.Find out before the next report goes.
Say this in the interview

"I'd tell my manager straight away: what's wrong, what the right figure is, and whether it changes anything for the client. I wouldn't quietly resend it. Then I'd fix the cause, probably by adding a check against the source before anything goes out. Integrity at LSEG is 'deliver on our promises', and a correct report is the promise."

C5. Acting on incomplete information against a deadline

Setup. At 4pm you need to send a recommendation by 5pm. One key data point won't arrive until tomorrow.

#Ask yourselfIf yesIf no
1Do I know what decision the deadline serves, and who makes it?Go to 2.Ask now: one line to the requester.
2Is the decision easy to reverse if the missing data changes the answer?Recommend on the best estimate, label every assumption, say what would change it, and when you'll update.Go to 3.
3Does it touch a regulatory filing, a client commitment, or risk limits?Escalate now: ask for the deadline to move or for a senior person to accept the gap on record.Send a range with the missing piece clearly named, and a time for the update.
Say this in the interview

"I'd first ask whether the decision can be undone. If it can, I'd send my best answer on time with the assumptions in bold and a time for the update. If it can't, or it touches risk or a regulator, I'd say so now and ask for either more time or a senior decision to go ahead with the gap. Late and labelled beats on time and wrong."

MK1124KMThe CV grill

At the assessment centre interview, expect at least one line of your CV to be tested three levels deep. Your CV details aren't in this pack, so this section gives the method, eight attacks with frame-holding answers, and a drill. The worked examples are placeholders: replace them with your own.

How a three-levels-deep attack works

LevelWhat they askWhat they are testing
1. What"Tell me about the investment society role."Can you explain it plainly in 20 seconds?
2. How and how much"How did you grow attendance? From what to what? How do you know?"Is there a real number, and did you measure it honestly?
3. Why you, and what if"Wasn't that just because term started? What would have happened without you? What would you do differently?"Can you separate your contribution from luck and the team, and do you learn?

The frame for a CV grill is the same four steps, with one rule added: never claim more at level 3 than you claimed at level 1. Inflation shows up at the third question, not the first.

Eight attacks and how to hold the frame

A1. "So what did you do? Not the team. You."
Hold "The team did the event; my part was the sign-up process and the reminder emails. That's where attendance moved." Name your part precisely. Credit others without shrinking yourself.
A2. "That number seems high. How did you measure it?"
Hold "From the sign-up sheet, comparing the four weeks before with the four weeks after. It isn't a controlled test, so some of it may be the time of term." Give the method and its limit before they do.
A3. "That sounds like an easy job."
Hold "Parts of it were. The hard part was [one specific thing], and that's where I learned [skill]." Don't defend everything; locate the hard bit.
A4. "Why did you leave after only eight weeks?"
Hold "It was a fixed eight-week role; I finished it and handed over [what]." State the fact, then the handover. No apology, no story.
A5. "You say you're interested in markets, but nothing here shows it."
Hold "Fair: it's not in a job title yet. It shows in [one habit or project]. For example, I've been following how London's FX share held at 37.8% in the latest BIS survey [S162] and what that means for a venue like FXall." Then stop.
A6. "Tell me about this grade / this gap."
Hold "That module went badly because [one honest reason]. What I changed was [habit], and my next result was [result]." One sentence of cause, two of change.
A7. "What would your manager there say your weakness was?"
Hold "Probably that I took too long to ask for help early on. By the end I was checking in after the first hour on anything unclear." Real, specific, already improving. No disguised strengths.
A8. "Why should any of that matter to us at LSEG?"
Hold "Because the internship asks for [JD phrase, for example 'curiosity for data... to draw conclusions and propose solutions'] [S260], and this is where I did that: [one line]." Map to the JD's own words.

The four-line drill for every CV bullet

For each bullet on your CV, write four lines on a card. If you can't fill a line, the bullet is weak: change the bullet or prepare harder.

LineQuestion it answers
1. WhatWhat was it, in one plain sentence a stranger understands?
2. NumberWhat changed, from what to what, measured how? (If no number exists, say what you would have measured.)
3. Your partWhich decisions or actions were yours, not the team's?
4. DifferentlyWhat would you do differently now, and why?
Worked placeholder 1: replace with your own

PLACEHOLDER bullet: "Events officer, university finance society: grew weekly market briefing attendance."
What: I ran a 30-minute weekly briefing on one market story for society members.
Number: PLACEHOLDER: average attendance went from about 15 to about 40 over one term, from the sign-up sheet.
My part: I changed the format to one chart and one question, and moved sign-up to a form with a reminder the day before.
Differently: I'd have kept the old format for two weeks alongside, so I could tell how much was the format and how much was the start of term.

Worked placeholder 2: replace with your own

PLACEHOLDER bullet: "Retail assistant: cut weekly stock-check time."
What: I suggested a new order for the weekly stock count in a busy shop.
Number: PLACEHOLDER: the count went from about three hours to about two, measured over four weeks.
My part: I timed each section, spotted that we walked the floor twice, and proposed one route. My manager approved it; the team ran it.
Differently: I'd have asked the evening team first. They had a reason for the old order (deliveries), and the first week went badly because I hadn't asked.

Why this matters

Placeholder 2 is deliberately close to scenario 8M (the old spreadsheet). The best CV stories double as scenario evidence: when an assessor asks "what would you do?", you can say "I've done a version of this" and give the four lines. That is what a strengths-based assessor hopes to hear [S264].

Don't say this

"We increased engagement significantly." No owner, no number, no method. Under a level-2 question it collapses. Every bullet you can't defend at level 3 should come off the CV before you submit.

MK1125KMHow to practise this part

Reading the cards is not practice. Saying them out loud, against a clock, on camera, is. Use this ten-day plan in the run-up to each stage, and score yourself with the rubric after every recording.

DayDo thisDone when
1Learn the four steps and the priority order. Write both on your index card.You can say both from memory in 20 seconds.
2 to 5Three rows of the ladder a day (nine cards). Answer each aloud, timed, before reading the model answer.Every answer lands between 45 and 75 seconds and ends with a Close.
6Ask a friend to read you the Twists cold, using the eight frame-breakers.You held your frame on at least six of eight, and could say why you changed on the others.
7Talk through the five composure trees from memory, with the drawings face down.You can name each question in each tree.
8Run the four-line drill on every CV bullet. Cut any bullet you can't defend at level 3.Every bullet has a number, your part, and a "differently".
9Record six random cards on video, one take each, camera at eye level.Watching back, you look at the lens to close and don't rush.
10Rest. Read the cheat sheet (Part 13) once in the evening.Done.

Self-scoring rubric (score each answer 0 to 2 per row)

Criterion012
SteadyStarted answering before restating the askRestated, but slowly or vaguelyOne clean line that frames the problem
SortNo priorities namedNamed the goods, not which winsNamed the collision and the winning tier
ActAbstract ("communicate with stakeholders")Steps, but no owner or timeTwo or three verbs, named owners, a time
FactNone, or an invented oneA fact without a source you could nameOne sourced LSEG fact, used naturally
CloseTrailed offSummarised, but no record or ownerOutcome, owner, record; then stopped
TwistFolded under pressureHeld, but sounded defensiveAcknowledged, then returned to the frame

Aim for 10 or more out of 12 on every card before the assessment centre. A score below 8 on any card means do that card again tomorrow, not the next one.

Why this matters

The Immersive Online Assessment scores consistency across many situations, and the video gives you one take [S289, S291] Reported. A method you have rehearsed 36 times is the most reliable way to be consistent when it counts.

MK1012KM
Part 12

Why LSEG, in three lengths

An answer built from how LSEG works, not from adjectives: compressed to 30 seconds, expanded to 2 minutes, and finished with one specific thing you would work on.

"Why LSEG?" is the question every candidate prepares, so it is the one where most answers sound the same. The way to stand out is to answer with mechanisms: how the business is built, why customers pay, and where the work actually happens. A mechanism is something a rival could not say about itself. "LSEG is a global leader" could be said by ICE, CME or Deutsche Börse. "LCH has to clear for rival venues on non-discriminatory terms, which is why banks trust it with their swaps" could only be said about LSEG [S305].

This Part gives you the four mechanism answers in compressed form, then the same material at three lengths: 30 seconds (video interview opener), 2 minutes (a full interview answer), and a close that names one thing you would work on. Then it covers the follow-ups: why this programme rather than a bank, why not a rival, and the honest case against LSEG.

Your CV goes here

Your CV details are not in this pack. Where you see [YOUR HOOK], add one true sentence about how you came to the topic: a module, a society, a job, a news story you followed. Keep it to one sentence. The rest of the answer should be about LSEG, not you.

MK1126KMThe four mechanism answers, compressed

Each mechanism answers one question an interviewer might ask on its own. Together they make the spine of your "Why LSEG?" answer. Learn the one-liners first; the evidence column is what you reach for if they push.

MechanismThe question it answersThe answer in two sentencesEvidence to reach for
1. StructureWhy is LSEG a group of separate businesses?Regulation forces ring-fenced entities: a clearing house holds other people's default risk, so it needs its own capital and board. And open access is written into LCH's constitution, so LSEG cannot run it as a captive.LCH about 94%, rising above 95% after the July 2026 deal [S300, S70]; Tradeweb 50.9% economic; Turquoise 84.2%; PTS 80% [S300]. "No exchange will be favoured over any other" [S305].
2. CollaborationHow do the businesses work together?At named joins, not by bundling. Trading turns into data and data into products, and the joins are specific and checkable.RepoAgent (PTS + Tradeweb, Nov 2025) [S301]; FXall functionality largely in Workspace [S302]; FTSE Russell pricing some indices off Tradeweb [S300]; a Group Head of Sales and Account Management since Jan 2026 [S306].
3. Customer valueWhy do customers pay, and keep paying?Because the safety has been tested and the liquidity is in one place. Netting more trades in one pot means less margin per member.9 member defaults, all within initial margin [S351]; Lehman's $9trn book used about 35% of its initial margin [S354]; SwapClear over 90% of cleared swap notional [S303]; data quality issues down 51% as content rose 113% [S301].
4. The centreWhere does a business management intern fit?In the coordinating layer between the front line and the central functions. Each principal risk has a named executive owner, and business roles pull Risk, Operations, Product, Technology and Legal together.Central counterparty risk owned by the Head of Markets [S302]; three lines of defence [S300]; a CDSClear programme manager coordinates "Risk, Operations, Product, Technology, Client Services, Legal, Compliance, Finance" [S315].
Key term

Open access: LCH clears trades from any venue on fair, non-discriminatory terms, and LSEG's own venues get no special treatment [S305]. Deutsche Börse does the opposite: Eurex trading and Eurex clearing sit in one "vertically integrated" model [S127].

Key term

Initial margin: collateral a clearing member posts up front to cover how much its positions could lose before it can be closed out. LCH sets it at 99.7% confidence for most services [S351].

The one-liners

  • Structure: "LSEG chose to be the neutral clearing house for everyone, and wrote that into LCH's rules."
  • Collaboration: "The businesses meet at specific points, like FXall moving into Workspace, not through bundling."
  • Customer value: "Customers pay for safety that has been tested: nine defaults, all inside initial margin."
  • The centre: "Business management sits where those businesses and the central functions meet, which is the part I want to learn."

MK1127KMWhy LSEG in 30 seconds

Use this as the opening of a video interview answer, or when an interviewer says "briefly". About 90 words: 30 to 35 seconds at a calm speaking pace. Read it aloud three times, then say it without the page.

Say this: 30 seconds

"What draws me to LSEG is how it's built. It runs trading venues like the London Stock Exchange, Tradeweb and FXall, but its clearing house, LCH, has open access in its rules. It has to clear for rival venues on fair terms, and banks still sit on its risk committee. That neutrality is why SwapClear clears over 90% of cleared interest rate swaps. Markets is now 40% of the group and its fastest-growing part, and business management sits right where those businesses meet. That's where I want to learn."

Sources behind each sentence: open access [S305, S304]; members and clients on the LCH risk committee [S304]; over 90% of cleared IRS notional outstanding, LSEG's own figure [S303]; Markets 40% [S71] and fastest-growing at +11.9% in H1 2026 [S70].

Don't say this

"LSEG is a world-leading, innovative and diverse company with great values." Every word could apply to a rival, and the interviewer will hear it from most candidates that day.

MK1128KMWhy LSEG in 2 minutes

About 300 words. The time marks show where you should be; if you are running long, cut the fourth paragraph first. Contractions ("it's", "isn't") are deliberate: they make it sound spoken, not read.

Say this: 2 minutes

0:00 "I'd like to work at LSEG because its advantage comes from how it's built, and the Markets programme is where you see that structure working. [YOUR HOOK: one true sentence on how you came to this.]

0:15 Start with the structure. LSEG isn't one exchange. The London Stock Exchange, Turquoise, Tradeweb, the FX venues and LCH are separate regulated businesses. LCH has open access written into its articles: it has to clear for rival venues on non-discriminatory terms, and LSEG's own venues get no special treatment. Deutsche Börse went the other way and tied trading to clearing. LSEG chose neutrality and kept the banks inside. Members sit on LCH's risk committee, and last year eleven banks bought 20% of Post Trade Solutions.

0:45 That's why customers pay. When Lehman failed, SwapClear closed out a nine trillion dollar swap book using about a third of Lehman's own margin. LCH says it has managed nine member defaults, all within margin. That record is why SwapClear cleared a record 1,941 trillion dollars of notional last year.

1:05 Then there's where the businesses meet. FTSE Russell now prices some indices off Tradeweb, Post Trade Solutions and Tradeweb built RepoAgent together, and most of FXall's functionality now sits inside Workspace. Markets is 40% of the group and grew 11.9% in the first half.

1:25 I can see the tensions too. The FCA found data users may be paying more than they would with stronger competition, and open access meant Euronext could take its clearing elsewhere. So the job isn't only growth. It's keeping customers' trust while charging for value.

1:45 That mix of customers, numbers and risk is what the programme's four areas cover, and it's what I want to spend the summer on. If I could pick one thing, it would be [YOUR CLOSE: one of the four below]."

Claim in the scriptExact fact and source
Separate regulated businessesLSE plc an RIE; Turquoise an MTF; LCH Ltd a Bank of England Recognised Clearing House; FX MTFs licensed in Ireland and the UK; Tradeweb listed on Nasdaq [S300, S304, S341]
Open access in its articlesOFT decision on LSEG's control of LCH.Clearnet, Dec 2012 [S305]; LCH Ltd still operates "an open access model" [S304]
Deutsche Börse tied trading to clearing"vertically integrated business model" [S127]; OFT example "Deutsche Börse/Eurex Clearing" [S305]
Eleven banks, 20% of PTS£170m, October 2025 [S301]
Lehman: $9trn, about a third of margin"$9 trillion OTC portfolio", "only 35% of its initial margin" used [S354]
Nine defaults within margin"managed 9 member defaults and, in all cases, losses were within the initial margin held" [S351]
Record $1,941trnSwapClear IRS notional cleared 2025, +21.2% [S301]
The joinsFTSE Russell price source [S300]; RepoAgent [S301]; FXall in Workspace [S302]
40%, +11.9%CEO on the H1 2026 call [S71]; H1 2026 interim results [S70]

Why this matters

The fifth paragraph is what makes the answer sound like an analyst rather than a fan. You name two real criticisms with sources, then turn them into a description of the job. It also matches the JD's line that "what you achieve is equally important as how you achieve it".

MK1129KMThe close: one specific thing you would work on

The JD says LSEG will "get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business" before placing you. A specific close does that work for them. Pick the one that matches the area you most want, and be ready for "why that one?". Each close has the same shape: the thing, why it matters now, what you would measure.

Close A. FX customers: FXall moving into Workspace

Say "If I could pick one thing, it would be FXall moving into Workspace. LSEG says a large proportion of FXall's functionality is now there. I'd like to help measure whether clients are actually moving their workflow: which client groups have switched, where onboarding and permissioning slow them down, and whether it changes retention or what else they buy from LSEG."

Why credible The integration is stated in the H1 2026 report [S302]. FX account managers are asked to "identify upsell, cross-sell, and new business opportunities across FX trading, workflow, data" [S313]. Onboarding runs through FXall Admin, including "Price Stream Entitlement requests" [S317].

Measure Share of active FXall clients using it through Workspace, by segment; onboarding tickets and time to first trade; client retention after the switch Inferred.

Follow-up If asked about pricing, use Forward First Fixing: over $1.5trn cumulative volume and fees waived for the rest of 2026 [S238]. "When does adoption justify switching fees on?" is a good question back.

Close B. Research: debt listings on the International Securities Market

Say "I'd like to work on debt listings, specifically the International Securities Market. It promises comments within three days of a first submission and two days after that, with no listing agent needed. I'd want to look at where its issuers come from, and whether turnaround has held up since the new prospectus regime started in January."

Why credible ISM is LSE's market for debt sold to professional investors, with admission decided by the Exchange, not the FCA [S346]. The "3+2" review windows are LSE's own promise [S347]. POATRs came into force on 19 January 2026 [S151]. An LSEG debt origination ad cites "1,300 global borrowers in over 60 countries that raise $500-600 billion annually" [S316] Reported.

Measure Issuers by country and sector; days from first submission to admission against the 3+2 promise; share of programme vs one-off issues Inferred.

Caution The ISM information pack predates current rules (it cites the UKLA and the Prospectus Directive), so say "the published 3+2 windows" and check current timings [S347, S346].

Close C. Business intelligence: what really drives Markets growth

Say "I'd like to help build the view of what drives Markets growth. The division grew 11.9% in the first half, partly on volatility. I'd split each line into volume and revenue per unit of volume, for example FX revenue against FX daily volume, to see which businesses are growing structurally and which are riding the cycle."

Why credible LSEG publishes the volume KPIs: FX ADV $525bn (2025) and $561bn (H1 2026); Tradeweb ADV $3.2trn; SwapClear notional; ForexClear members [S301, S302]. FX revenue was £272m in 2025 [S301].

Worked example £272m divided by $525bn a day over about 252 trading days is roughly £2 of revenue per $1m traded Inferred. LSEG does not publish this capture rate, so call it your own metric.

Measure Revenue capture per line, year on year; growth in calm months vs volatile months; new clients vs existing clients' volume Inferred.

Close D. Risk: LCH first-line risk reporting

Say "I'd like to work on the risk reporting LCH's first line produces: business continuity testing, third-party risk and the evidence behind central bank attestations, turned into information senior management and the Board can act on. With T+1 coming in October 2027, how quickly that reporting picks up problems matters more each year."

Why credible A current LCH first-line role coordinates "EMIR switch testing, WAR site testing", third-party risk MI for "senior management, committees and Board forums" and "Central Bank Attestation Support" [S318]. UK T+1 is planned for 11 October 2027 [S158]. Business continuity risk is owned by the COO, CRO and divisional heads [S302].

Measure Test completion against plan; open third-party risk issues by age; time from incident to report Inferred.

Don't say this

"I'd like to help with digital transformation and AI." It is not specific enough to measure, and the interviewer cannot picture you doing it. Also avoid claiming LSEG commercially bundles SwapClear with Tradeweb or ForexClear with FXall: no LSEG statement says so, and open access makes it unlikely.

MK1130KMWhy this programme, not a bank's graduate scheme

Expect this as a follow-up, often phrased as "Where else are you applying?" The interviewer wants to know whether LSEG is a real choice or a fallback. Do not criticise banks: banks generate about 72% of LSEG's revenue [S303], and some of your interviewers may have come from one.

Say this

"A bank would teach me one desk's view of the market. LSEG lets me see the market from the infrastructure underneath it. Banking customers are about 72% of LSEG's revenue, so in a Markets role I'd be working with many banks at once, on the venues and clearing they all rely on. The business earns fees for running trusted infrastructure rather than taking positions with its own balance sheet, so the questions are about customers, reliability and risk, which is what interests me. And the programme spans four areas, from FX clients to risk reporting, which is the breadth I want at this stage."

You see many banks, not oneLSEG's customers are the banks; Markets serves them allBanking 72% of revenue [S303]; FXall 200+ liquidity providers [S340]; SwapClear over 100 members [S141]
Fees for trust, not trading riskVenues and clearing earn per-trade and clearing fees; LCH mutualises default risk through margin and default fundsRevenue model [S303]; default waterfall [S351] Inferred contrast with banks

Don't say this

"Banks have a bad work-life balance" or "I didn't want sales and trading." Both describe what you are running from, not what you are choosing. Also do not say you want LSEG because it is "less risky": LCH manages default risk for the whole swaps market [S351].
